description_text:
THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS
AFSC/PZIMB, Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, intends to award a sole-source modification to Contract FA857926C0002 to Lockheed Martin Corporation, Fort Worth, Texas, for F-35 Joint Strike Fighter (JSF) AN/AAQ-40 Electro-Optical Targeting System (EOTS) Technical Refresh 3 (TR-3) gap-analysis and software sustainment capability assessment services.

The Government intends to award this action to Lockheed Martin Corporation under the authority cited in the approved justification and approval. Lockheed Martin is the original equipment manufacturer for the EOTS Operational Flight Program and possesses the specialized technical knowledge, system-specific configuration knowledge, access, data, development and test-environment familiarity, and technical support capability necessary to perform this requirement.

description_text:
U.S. Army Reserve, 88th RD has an objective to reduce energy consumption, reduce energy cost, and increase energy resiliency of multiple facilities located in Minnesota and Wisconsin. The 88th RD is seeking to identify additional Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs) that provide measurable energy and cost savings. Potential energy and water saving projects may include but are not limited to: envelope improvements, insulation upgrades, window upgrades, LED upgrades, geothermal heat pumps, lighting, controls, renewable energy generation including photovoltaic solar arrays, retro-commissioning, water conservation measures, heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) upgrades including boilers, furnaces, split systems, and chillers, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and Hydrogen Fuel Cells and microgrids. Additional ECMs of interest include re-tuning; retro-commissioning and re-commissioning; building automation and control systems; window replacement; minor building-envelope improvements; domestic hot-water system replacement; plug-load analysis and reduction, including refrigerators and freezers; water-leak detection; and other water-efficiency upgrades. The project will evaluate these and other cost-effective opportunities to modernize facilities, improve energy and water resilience, and support the 88th RD long-term energy, water conservation, and resiliency goals (as determined by 88th RD and ARIMD). These efforts align with statutory requirements under 10 U.S.C. § 2911 for energy security and resilience, and 42 U.S.C. § 8287 through the Department of Energy’s (DOE) Fourth-Generation Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract.

By combining these vehicles, the Army aims to enhance flexibility, reduce redundancy, and improve cost-efficiency in acquiring uncommon knowledge-based professional services. This integration will also ensure a unified approach in meeting the Army’s evolving technology and strategic needs, thus optimizing mission readiness and effectiveness.

This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items/services prepared in accordance with the format in Subpart 12.6 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This acquisition is for a commercial item or service and is conducted under the authority of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) FAR Subpart 13.5—Simplified Procedures for Certain Commercial Items; and FAR Part 12— Acquisition of Commercial Items; and is expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold.
Introduction and Background Objectives
The National Center for Translational Sciences (NCATS) requires a partner to facilitate user administration, process/workflow improvements, content development/moderation, requirements gathering, and dissemination of the SMART IRB (Streamlined, Multisite, Accelerated Resources for Trials Institutional Review Board) portfolio of services. SMART IRB relies on three systems: (1) the SMARTIRB.org website which is used for content distribution, notification, and educational purposes, (2) Joinder, through which institutions enter institutional information and sign the SMART IRB Authorization Agreement (AA), and (3) the Online Reliance System (ORS), through which Institutional Review Board (IRB) reliance arrangements under the SMART IRB Agreement are documented on a study-by-study basis. The selected partner will provide support in accordance with this SOW to aid in the facilitation and growth of SMART IRB.

description_text:
COMBINED SYNOPSIS / SOLICITATION
VISN 09 Annual Pharmacy Wall-to-Wall Inventory | Base Period and Four Option Years
Solicitation: 36C24927Q0021 | RFQ | Firm-Fixed-Price | Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside
1. Notice
This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR Subpart 12.6. Quotations are requested; no separate written solicitation will be issued. Applicable Federal Acquisition Circular: 2027-01.
2. Requirement
VISN 09 requires annual wall-to-wall physical inventory services for pharmacy medications and applicable pharmacy supplies at six VA medical center campuses. Contractor provides qualified labor, supervision, equipment, inventory tools, travel, section-level controls, product identification, pricing and electronic reporting in accordance with Attachment 1, Statement of Work.
3. Classification and acquisition strategy
NAICS: 541614, Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services. SBA Size Standard: $20 million in average annual receipts. PSC: R706, Logistics Support. Total Small Business Set-Aside. Applicable set-aside provisions and clauses are subject to Contracting Officer review before issuance.
4. Base Period and Four Option-Year Periods
The Government anticipates awarding one firm-fixed-price contract consisting of a base period and four separately exercisable option periods. Annual wall-to-wall physical inventories at all designated VA pharmacy locations shall occur between January 1 and February 28 of each applicable year. Base: January 01, 2027 February 28, 2027; Option 1: January 01, 2028 February 28, 2028; Option 2: January 01, 2029 February 28, 2029; Option 3: January 01, 2030 February 28, 2030; Option 4: January 01, 2031 February 28, 2031. A separate report for each pharmacy inventory is due within seven (7) calendar days after its physical inventory.
5. Places of performance
The contractor shall provide annual wall-to-wall pharmacy inventory services at the following six (6) VA medical center campuses. The services include the inpatient and outpatient pharmacy inventories identified in the Statement of Work and pricing schedule.

Submit technical and price quotations and required representations by 11/15/2026 at 11:59 P.M. to mario.russell@va.gov. Questions due 11/05/2026 by 11:59 P.M.

Include applicable commercial-services provisions and clauses, including FAR 52.212-1, 52.212-3, 52.212-4, and 52.212-5, as appropriate, together with applicable small-business set-aside provisions and clauses and any required option provisions. Contracting Officer to verify the final clause matrix before issuance. No wage determination or additional security provisions are requested in this working draft; applicability remains subject to required acquisition review.

Mario Russell, Contract Specialist | Department of Veterans Affairs, VISN 09 | Email: mario.russell@va.gov | Telephone: 615-226-6774

POINT OF CONTACT / QUESTIONS
Questions or concerns regarding this solicitation shall be submitted in writing only by email to Mario Russell, Contract Specialist, at mario.russell@va.gov. The subject line shall state 36C24927Q0021 VISN 09 Pharmacy Wall-to-Wall Inventory Questions. Questions shall be received no later than 11/05/2026 at 11:59 PM Central Time (CT). Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. Responses affecting solicitation requirements will be provided through an appropriate solicitation amendment or other authorized written communication.

ATTACHMENT 1 STATEMENT OF WORK
The requirement consists of a base period plus four option periods. All physical inventories at the six facilities shall be completed no later than February 28 of the applicable contract year. A separate report for each pharmacy inventoried shall be delivered within seven (7) calendar days after that pharmacy s physical inventory. 1. PURPOSE
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 9, requires the services of a qualified contractor to conduct annual wall-to-wall physical inventories of pharmacy medications and applicable pharmacy supplies at designated VA Medical Centers.
The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, equipment, supplies, software or inventory tools, travel, and other resources necessary to perform the required services.
2. BACKGROUND
VISN 9 requires an annual physical inventory of pharmacy medications and applicable pharmacy supplies at the facilities identified in this Statement of Work (SOW).
The inventory shall support the VA's financial, pharmacy management, and inventory-control requirements by establishing an accurate record of inventory quantities and replacement costs.
The Contractor shall perform the inventory in a manner that minimizes disruption to pharmacy operations and patient-care activities.
3. PLACES OF PERFORMANCE
The services shall be performed at the following VA Medical Centers:

4. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE
The contract shall consist of one base period and four option periods identified below. Each period requires one complete wall-to-wall physical inventory at each designated facility, conducted between January 01 through February 28. All physical inventories at the six facilities shall be completed no later than January 31 of the applicable contract year. A separate report for each pharmacy inventoried is due within seven (7) calendar days following its physical inventory.

The Government is not obligated to exercise any option. Inventory reports are due within seven (7) calendar days after each pharmacy inventory. Because an inventory performed on February 28 may generate a report due after the stated period, the Contracting Officer shall confirm applicable post-period delivery, correction, and acceptance terms before issuance; this draft does not extend the annual inventory period beyond February 28.
5. ANNUAL INVENTORY REQUIREMENT
The Contractor shall perform one complete wall-to-wall inventory at each designated facility during each contract period.
Unless otherwise approved in advance by the Contracting Officer or authorized VA representative, the physical inventory at each facility shall:
Begin at 8:00 a.m. local time on the scheduled inventory date.
Be completed within one business day.
Be scheduled on a Saturday or Sunday, when operationally feasible, to minimize disruption to patient-care activities.
Include all applicable pharmacy areas and inventory categories identified in this SOW.
The Government will establish the final inventory schedule in coordination with the Contractor and affected VA Medical Center personnel.
Any deviation from the one-day requirement must be coordinated with the affected pharmacy and approved by the Contracting Officer or authorized representative.
The Contractor shall provide a database with accurately formatted National Drug Code (NDC) and McKesson item numbers that correspond to the applicable products.
All physical inventories at the six facilities shall be completed no later than February 28 of each applicable contract year.
6. CONTRACTOR QUALIFICATIONS
The Contractor shall demonstrate a minimum of three years of experience performing wall-to-wall pharmacy inventory services.
The Contractor shall also demonstrate experience involving pharmacy inventory operations, medication and pharmacy-supply identification, NDC identification and validation, replacement-cost determination, McKesson Prime Vendor data where applicable, and electronic inventory reporting.
Experience performing similar services for VA pharmacies and experience with McKesson as a Prime Vendor are preferred.
7. INVENTORY SCOPE
The Contractor shall inventory applicable medications and pharmacy supplies located within areas under the direct control of the pharmacy.
Unless specifically excluded by this SOW, the inventory shall include:
Products purchased through the McKesson Prime Vendor.
Eligible direct purchases having a total dollar value of $100 or more per line item.
Applicable prosthetic items in unopened containers having a cost exceeding $100.
Inpatient pharmacy inventory.
Outpatient pharmacy inventory.
Bulk intravenous solutions.
Unit-dose repackaged medications.
Medications located within applicable automated dispensing and packaging equipment.
Other medications and supplies meeting the definition of inventory under this SOW.
8. EXCLUDED ITEMS
The following items shall not be included unless specifically directed by the Government:
All Hazards Pharmaceutical Cache inventory.
Equipment.
Prescription labels.
Empty prescription vials and containers.
Items not under the direct control of the pharmacy.
Patient-dispensed inventory that is no longer pharmacy stock.
Controlled substances, which shall be physically counted by authorized VA Pharmacy personnel.
For purposes of determining whether an item is included or excluded, the Contractor shall request clarification from the designated VA Pharmacy representative. Questions affecting contract scope, price, or other contractual requirements shall be referred to the Contracting Officer.
9. INPATIENT PHARMACY INVENTORY
The Contractor shall inventory applicable items located within the inpatient pharmacy, including medication and inventory maintained within automated dispensing, packaging, or unit-dose equipment.
Applicable systems may include Talyst, Omnicell, AutoMed, ATC, OS-PAC, unit-dose packaging systems, and other automated dispensing or packaging systems identified by the facility.
The VA Pharmacy shall provide the Contractor with available inventory data from applicable automated systems. The Contractor shall incorporate the VA-provided automated-system data into the applicable inventory report.
10. OUTPATIENT PHARMACY INVENTORY
The Contractor shall inventory applicable items located within the outpatient pharmacy, including inventory maintained within automated dispensing or fulfillment equipment.
Applicable systems may include Baker APS, ScriptPro, Optifill, and other automated dispensing or fulfillment systems identified by the facility.
The VA Pharmacy shall provide available inventory data from applicable automated systems for incorporation into the final inventory report.
11. CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES
Controlled substances shall be physically counted by authorized VISN 9/VA Pharmacy personnel.
The VA Pharmacy shall provide the Contractor with the applicable controlled-substance inventory data necessary for inclusion in the final inventory report.
The Contractor shall not independently count, handle, move, reconcile, or otherwise perform a physical inventory of controlled substances unless specifically authorized by the Government in accordance with applicable VA requirements.
12. PARTIAL CONTAINERS
Opened bottles of medication, other than medication used for compounding, shall be estimated to the nearest one-tenth of a bottle unless otherwise specified by the Government.
For higher-cost medications where a more precise quantity can reasonably be established, the Contractor shall have a methodology capable of recording whole-unit quantities for partial containers.
The Contractor shall document the methodology used and apply it consistently throughout the inventory.
13. INVENTORY IDENTIFICATION AND SECTION CONTROL
The Contractor shall establish a method for identifying each inventory section before counting begins.
The method shall clearly identify the beginning and end of each section, identify the inventory specialist responsible for counting the section, prevent duplication or omission when multiple inventory specialists work simultaneously, allow VA personnel to determine which areas have been completed, and support final reconciliation of all inventory areas.
The Contractor shall remove all temporary inventory markers at the completion of the inventory after confirming that all applicable areas have been counted.
14. INVENTORY DATA AND PRODUCT IDENTIFICATION
The Contractor shall maintain an inventory database capable of identifying applicable products using accurate NDC, UPC, UPN, and McKesson item-number information, as applicable.
The Contractor shall use current and accurate product and pricing information to determine the replacement cost of inventoried items.
Where McKesson Prime Vendor information is used, the Contractor shall ensure that product identification corresponds to the applicable McKesson item and associated VA pricing information.
The Contractor shall not alter or manipulate VA-provided costing files for the purpose of correcting Government-provided data.
If the Contractor identifies an apparent discrepancy, it shall document the discrepancy and obtain clarification from the VA Pharmacy before making any adjustment attributable to Government-provided information.
Contractor-caused inventory errors shall be corrected at no additional cost to the Government.
15. VA-FURNISHED INFORMATION
The VA facility shall provide, as applicable:
Current Prime Vendor pricing information.
Current costing information for direct-purchase items.
Automated dispensing and packaging system data.
Controlled-substance inventory data.
Access to pharmacy areas necessary to perform the inventory.
Knowledgeable pharmacy personnel to answer inventory questions.
Current shelf labels for Prime Vendor products, to the extent available.
McKesson Mobile Manager units or equivalent Government-provided pricing information, when applicable.
Other information reasonably necessary to perform the requirement.
The Contractor shall promptly notify the VA Pharmacy representative of missing or apparently inaccurate information.
16. CONTRACTOR-FURNISHED RESOURCES
The Contractor shall furnish sufficient qualified personnel to complete each facility inventory within the required performance period.
The Contractor shall provide inventory specialists, on-site supervision, inventory equipment and supplies, data-processing and reporting capability, required travel, transportation, temporary identification or tagging materials, and all other resources necessary to perform the requirement.
17. ON-SITE INVENTORY PROCEDURE
The Contractor shall:
Meet with the designated VA Pharmacy representative before beginning the inventory.
Confirm the areas included in the inventory.
Confirm receipt of applicable VA-provided data.
Establish section markers or other inventory controls.
Mark the beginning and end of each inventory section and identify the specialist responsible for the count to prevent duplication or omission.
Perform the physical inventory.
Record product identification and quantities.
Reconcile questions and apparent discrepancies with VA Pharmacy personnel.
Produce section-level inventory information as sections are completed.
Review applicable inventory information with VA Pharmacy personnel.
Perform required recounts or corrections.
Conduct a final facility-wide walkthrough.
Verify that all applicable sections have been counted.
Remove inventory markers.
Complete the on-site closeout with the designated VA Pharmacy representative.
18. SECTION-LEVEL VERIFICATION
For each inventory section, the Contractor shall provide sufficient inventory information to permit review by the Contractor's representative and VA Pharmacy personnel.
At least one detailed inventory printout or electronic equivalent shall be reviewed for each inventory specialist or counter working on the facility inventory.
VA personnel may request additional printouts, recounts, or supporting information when necessary to validate the inventory.
The Contractor shall correct Contractor-caused errors identified during the on-site verification process before departing the facility whenever practicable.
19. FINAL FACILITY CLOSEOUT
Before leaving a facility, the Contractor shall verify that:
All required sections have been counted.
Required recounts have been completed.
Known discrepancies have been addressed or documented.
Automated equipment data has been incorporated as required.
VA-provided controlled-substance data has been incorporated.
Inventory markers have been removed.
The final inventory status has been reviewed with the designated VA Pharmacy representative.
Any outstanding issue requiring Government action has been documented.
20. INVENTORY REPORT
The Contractor shall provide a separate final inventory report for each pharmacy or facility inventoried.
The Contractor shall submit a separate final inventory report for each pharmacy inventoried within seven (7) calendar days following completion of that pharmacy s physical inventory. All physical inventories at the six facilities must be completed by February 28 of the applicable contract year.
Each report shall contain, at a minimum:
Facility and pharmacy/section.
Item name and strength.
Package description.
NDC, UPC, or UPN, as applicable.
McKesson item number, when applicable.
Quantity.
Current package price.
Extended replacement cost by item.
Section/location.
Total replacement cost for the inventory.
The report shall be provided in an electronic format that can be opened, reviewed, and transferred into Microsoft Excel or an equivalent Government-approved spreadsheet application.
21. REPORT FORMAT
The Contractor shall provide data in a structured electronic format.
The Contractor shall ensure that each inventory item is represented by a discrete record; quantities and prices are numeric and usable for calculation; product identifiers are not truncated or improperly formatted; extended costs can be independently calculated from quantity and unit price; section/location information is retained; and facility and pharmacy totals reconcile to the underlying item-level data.
22. QUALITY CONTROL
The Contractor shall maintain an internal quality-control process sufficient to ensure the accuracy and completeness of each inventory.
The Contractor shall review inventory data for duplicate entries, missing product identifiers, missing quantities, missing prices, incorrect package descriptions, invalid or inconsistent NDC information, arithmetic errors, duplicate sections, omitted sections, and other apparent data-quality problems.
The Contractor shall correct Contractor-caused errors at no additional cost to the Government.
23. GOVERNMENT ACCEPTANCE
The Government will review each deliverable for completeness, accuracy, and compliance with this SOW.
A deliverable may be rejected when it:
Omits required inventory areas or items.
Contains material data inaccuracies.
Contains unsupported or unexplained pricing information.
Does not contain the required data elements.
Contains duplicate or omitted inventory records.
Cannot be reconciled to the physical inventory.
Otherwise fails to meet a material requirement of this SOW.
If a deliverable is rejected because of Contractor-caused deficiencies, the Contractor shall correct and resubmit it within three (3) business days after notification, unless the Contracting Officer establishes a different period.
Contractor-caused corrections shall be completed within three business days of notification unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer. The Contracting Officer must confirm contractual handling of corrections requested after the February 28 inventory period.
Corrections required because of Contractor error shall be performed at no additional cost to the Government.
24. PERFORMANCE STANDARD
The Contractor shall deliver a complete and accurate inventory for each facility.
The Government's determination of successful performance shall be based on completion of all required inventory areas, accurate identification of inventoried products, accurate quantities, accurate pricing and replacement costs, complete incorporation of applicable Government-furnished data, timely submission of required reports, and successful correction of Contractor-caused discrepancies.
25. SCHEDULE AND COORDINATION
The Government and Contractor shall coordinate the annual inventory schedule before each inventory cycle.
The Contractor shall submit an implementation plan identifying proposed inventory dates for each facility, expected arrival and start times, estimated completion times, number of inventory personnel, Contractor on-site supervisor, report submission dates, and any information or facility support required before the scheduled inventory.
The final schedule shall be approved by the Government.
All physical inventories at the six facilities shall be completed no later than February 28 of the applicable contract year.
The Contractor shall submit a separate inventory report for each pharmacy inventoried within seven (7) calendar days of that pharmacy s physical inventory. The Contractor shall provide sufficient time for Government review and required corrections.
The Contractor shall submit deliverables on the schedule specified in this SOW to support Government review and acceptance.
26. CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL
The Contractor shall provide qualified personnel capable of performing pharmacy inventory services.
The Contractor shall submit the names of personnel proposed to perform on-site services in accordance with applicable VA security and access requirements.
Personnel shall satisfy all applicable VA background-investigation, fingerprinting, privacy, security, training, and access requirements before receiving access to VA facilities or VA information.
The Contractor shall provide sufficient personnel to meet the one-business-day performance requirement.
27. SECURITY, PRIVACY, AND HIPAA
The Contractor and all Contractor personnel shall comply with all applicable VA security, privacy, information-security, HIPAA, and information-protection requirements incorporated into the solicitation and resulting contract.
The Contractor shall execute the required Business Associate Agreement (BAA), when applicable, before performance requiring access to protected health information or other information covered by the BAA.
The applicable VA security and privacy provisions contained elsewhere in the solicitation are incorporated by reference and remain controlling.
28. BUSINESS ASSOCIATE AGREEMENT
When required, the Contractor shall execute the applicable VA Business Associate Agreement before beginning performance.
Failure to satisfy mandatory BAA requirements may prevent the Contractor from beginning performance and may result in the Government taking appropriate contractual action.
29. INSURANCE AND BONDING
The Contractor shall maintain all insurance and bonding required by the solicitation, resulting contract, and applicable Federal requirements.
Evidence of required insurance shall be provided to the Government when requested.
30. CONTRACTING OFFICER AUTHORITY
The Contracting Officer is the only Government official authorized to make changes to the contract that affect price, quantity, quality, schedule, or other contractual terms.
The Contractor shall not rely upon instructions from VA personnel that constitute a change to the contract unless the change is authorized in accordance with the contract.
Routine coordination with VA Pharmacy personnel regarding performance does not constitute authorization to modify contractual requirements.
31. SERVICE CONTRACT ACT
The Service Contract Act, when applicable, shall apply to this requirement.
The Contractor shall comply with the applicable Department of Labor wage determination incorporated into the solicitation or resulting contract.
The Contractor shall be responsible for complying with all applicable wage, fringe-benefit, and labor requirements.
32. EVALUATION CRITERIA LOWEST PRICE TECHNICALLY ACCEPTABLE (LPTA)
The Government will use a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) evaluation methodology.
Award will be made to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price whose quotation is technically acceptable and whose past performance is acceptable, provided the price is fair and reasonable and award is otherwise in the Government's best interest.
The Government will evaluate quotations under the following factors:
Factor
Evaluation Method
Factor 1 Technical Acceptability
Acceptable / Unacceptable
Factor 2 Past Performance
Acceptable / Unacceptable, with Neutral treatment where applicable
Factor 3 Price
Total evaluated price
No tradeoffs will be made between price and non-price factors, and no additional credit will be given for exceeding the minimum technical requirements.
The Government may evaluate price before non-price factors and may limit further evaluation to the lowest-priced quotation(s), consistent with the solicitation.
33. TECHNICAL ACCEPTABILITY
Technical quotations will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis against the following minimum requirements.
To receive an Acceptable rating, the quotation must demonstrate all of the following:
At least three years of experience performing wall-to-wall pharmacy inventory services.
Experience performing inventory services for at least three pharmacies.
Experience sufficient to demonstrate the ability to perform the requirements of this SOW.
Capability to identify pharmaceutical products using NDC or equivalent identifiers.
Capability to determine replacement cost.
Capability to produce the required electronic inventory reports.
Capability to staff all six facilities as required.
Ability to comply with VA security, privacy, and BAA requirements.
Ability to complete each facility inventory within the required performance period.
Technical Ratings
Rating
Definition
Acceptable
The quotation demonstrates compliance with all minimum technical requirements.
Unacceptable
The quotation fails to demonstrate compliance with one or more minimum technical requirements.
A quotation that does not demonstrate every stated minimum technical requirement will be rated Unacceptable and will not be eligible for award.
VA or McKesson experience identified elsewhere as preferred will not be an additional unstated minimum requirement.
34. PAST PERFORMANCE
The offeror shall provide information for three prior pharmacy inventory contracts or orders of similar scope and complexity, or identify that fewer relevant references are available.
Past performance will be evaluated as Acceptable or Unacceptable using relevant information furnished by the offeror and information reasonably available to the Government.

Neutral
No relevant past performance exists, or relevant performance information is unavailable. A Neutral rating will not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably and will not, by itself, make a quotation ineligible for award.
VA pharmacy or McKesson experience is not required for an Acceptable rating.
For each reference, the offeror shall provide:

35. PRICE EVALUATION
Offerors shall submit firm-fixed prices for the base period and each option period in the Schedule of Supplies/Services.
The Government will evaluate total price by adding the base-period and all option-period prices, including any other price elements identified in the solicitation.
The lowest evaluated price will be determined from the total evaluated prices of quotations eligible for award.
The Government will assess price reasonableness and may consider unbalanced pricing in accordance with applicable acquisition requirements.
The Government may reject an offer if it determines that materially unbalanced pricing poses an unacceptable risk.
The Government may request clarification or other information as permitted by the solicitation and applicable acquisition procedures.
Evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise them.
Award will not be based on a price/technical tradeoff.
36. PRICING STRUCTURE
The pricing schedule should identify a separate firm-fixed price for each required facility/service combination.
Each price shall include all costs necessary to perform the requirement, including labor, supervision, travel, transportation, equipment, supplies, data processing, reporting, administrative costs, and any other costs necessary for complete performance.
Unless specifically identified elsewhere in the solicitation, the Contractor shall not separately bill the Government for ordinary costs associated with completing the required inventory.
37. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION
The offeror shall submit its proposal in two parts.
Part 1 Technical Proposal
The technical proposal shall address the requirements of this SOW and include the required experience and past-performance information.
Part 2 Price Proposal

The offeror shall submit all required representations, certifications, signed solicitation documents, BAA documentation, insurance documentation, and other documents identified in the solicitation.

A separate final inventory report for each pharmacy inventoried is due within seven (7) calendar days following completion of that pharmacy s physical inventory. Contractor-caused corrections are due within three business days after notification, unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer.

Any VA equipment, information, data, access credentials, or other Government resources provided to the Contractor shall be used solely for performance of this contract and shall be protected in accordance with applicable VA requirements.

41. ORDER OF PRECEDENCE
In the event of an inconsistency between this SOW and other portions of the solicitation or resulting contract, the applicable contract order-of-precedence provisions shall control.
The Contracting Officer shall resolve questions regarding contractual requirements.

description_text:
Architect and Engineering (A-E) Services
The Federal Highway Administration, Central Federal Lands Highway Division (CFLHD), anticipates soliciting and awarding multiple Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for A-E services with a partial small business set-aside.
CFLHD provides engineering and construction services on projects in the states of Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming on behalf of Federal Land Management Agencies and other Agencies. These Agencies include: the National Park Service (NPS); USDA Forest Service (Forest Service); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS); Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) and Tribal Governments; Bureau of Land Management (BLM); Department of Defense (DOD); U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE); and the Bureau of Reclamation (BOR). The shared capacity of the IDIQs will be $60 million.
The acquisition will be solicited and awarded on a competitive basis and is being made under the North America Industry Classification Code 541330 and is open to all business concerns. The planned duration for the contracts is a total of five years.
Projects are typically located in environmentally sensitive areas that necessitate context-sensitive design techniques and processes. Project topography type and climatic zones vary greatly including coastal, mountainous, desert and plains regions. Projects will primarily involve improvements to low-volume and low-speed roadways ranging from 3R (resurfacing, restoration and rehabilitation) to full reconstruction. The geographic jurisdiction of CFLHD includes, but is not limited to, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming.

title: Marine Resource Technical Services Throughout the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Pacific Area of Responsibility
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NAVFAC.NAVFAC PACIFIC CMD.NAVFACSYSCOM PACIFIC
description_text: The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Pacific, at Joint Base Pearl Harbor/Hickam, Hawaii intends to award Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Multiple Award Contract (MAC), Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to provide marine resource technical services throughout the Naval Facilities Engineering Command (NAVFAC) Pacific area of responsibility (AOR), and other areas worldwide as needed. This solicitation will be issued as an unrestricted procurement with a partial small business set-aside that will result in the award of multiple award contracts that are comprised of two major divisions. The resulting multiple award contracts will be comprised of two major divisions: An Unrestricted Division and a partial Small Business Set Aside (SBSA) Division. The work shall be located primarily in Hawaii, Guam and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI). The Government may also require marine resource technical services throughout the NAVFAC Pacific area of responsibility (AOR), and other areas in the NAVFAC AOR worldwide as needed. All Marine Resource Technical Services conducted under the resultant contracts shall conform to the statutes, regulations, instructions and guidelines in compliance with the Request for Proposal (RFP). The resulting contract will include requirements that include but are not limited to, the following: (1) Coordination of Monitoring Projects and Subject Matter Experts, (2) Data Management, (3) Analysis and Reporting, (4) Visual Surveys, (5) Diving and Marine Resource Surveys, (6) Marine Species Observers, (7) Passive Acoustic Monitoring, (8) Marine Species Tagging and Tracking, (9) Photo Identification, (10) Behavioral Studies, (11) Habitat Restoration, (12) Coral Translocation, (13) Anomaly Avoidance Surveys, (14) Event Reconstruction and Environmental Data Integration, (15) Ecological Analysis, (16) Outreach, (17) Miscellaneous Marine Biological Resource Services, (18) Biomonitoring, (19) Biosecurity and Aquatic Invasive Species Management, (20) Integrated Natural Resource Management Plans (INRMPs), (21) NEPA, Environmental Planning and Supporting Studies, (22) GIS Mapping, (23) Endangered Species Act (ESA) Biological Opinions, (24) Magnuson Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (MSA) Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) Assessments, and (25) Marine Mammal Protection Act. Work will be performed in accordance with the requirements of the Performance Work Statement, and may involve regulatory compliance, planning, analyzing, and various related services on any one or a combination of more than one task order. Exact location of each effort will be designated on individual Task Orders. The entire term of the contract is a maximum of $99 million or 90 months (consisting of a 12-month base period, six (6) 12-month option periods and one (1) 6-month extension of services period), whichever occurs first. Task orders will typically range between $3,500 and $10,000,000. Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. The Government makes no representation as to the number of task orders or actual amount of work to be ordered; however, during the term of the contract, a minimum of $5,000 is guaranteed for each awardee under the contract. As task orders are awarded that exceed the $5,000, the $5,000 minimum guarantee will be deobligated and the Government������������������������������������������������������s obligation for the minimum guarantee for the contract will be satisfied. Projects competed to the unrestricted division will require a minimum of 18% of the work to be subcontracted to small businesses. Approximately $68.5M will be work performed in the NAVFAC Pacific Area of Responsibility (AOR), $15M in the NAVFAC Hawaii AOR and $15.5M in the NAVFAC Marianas AOR. These amounts may fluctuate with the potential need for the different types of specific services listed above and whether adequate competition exists within the SBSA Division and those contractors are capable of successfully executing those services. If one or no SBSA Division contractors submit a proposal in response to a task order request for proposal (RFP), the Contracting Officer may compete the task order amongst the Unrestricted Division contractors.The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 541990 ������������������������������������������������������ All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services and the corresponding small business size standard is $19.5 million (which will determine eligibility for awards under the Small Business Set Aside (SBSA) Division). A MAC is a contract awarded from a single solicitation and may result in award to multiple contractors. agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NAVSUP.NAVSUP GLOBAL LOGISTICS SUPPORT.NAVSUP FLC NORFOLK.NAVSUP FLT LOG CTR NORFOLK
description_text:
See the Attached Solicitation, PWS and other Solicitation related attachments. This opportunity is a 100% Small-business set-aside CPFF Task Order under Seaport NxG.
The Naval Education and Training Security Assistance Field Activity (NETSAFA), Pensacola, Florida, requires educational and training services, engineering and technical services, logistics, administration, management assistance, consulting and facilitation services, and transportation support services, training liaison, special mission personnel, and curriculum development. These services may be required in various locations in the U.S. or in foreign countries and may include support to foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs) under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP)/Security Assistance Training Program (SATP). The PSC code for this action is U099 Education/Training-Other associated with NAICS code 541330 under the Knowledge Based Services Taxonomy of services.
NETSAFA supports international training in all warfare areas and at all levels of training for foreign countries. This is accomplished by staffing, operating, and managing international training support provided at NETSAFA's international training sites. The training sites are located in the NETASAFA International Training Center (NITC) located at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida and NAS Whiting Field, Milton, Florida, and NITC Detachment Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. These sites are outfitted with computer training facilities, classrooms, and equipment needed to teach courses. They provide training and training support services in Navy activities such as government-owned contractor operating facilities.NETSAFA's international training sites are currently operational and have established curriculum.
The training and other services required by this Performance Work Statement (PWS) are currently centered in four categories: General Training Programs, Aviation Training Programs, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs). Additionally, support will be required to meet emerging requirements in support of the SCETP/SATP. The instant requirement is for services associated with the international requirement of the United States and the foreign countries participating in the SCETP/SATP for a 12-month base period of performance beginning 01 March 2027 through 29 February 2028, with four (4) consecutive 12-month option periods pursuant to FAR 52.217-9, and a 6-month option period pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The contractor will be required to periodically perform these services in various locations in the U.S. and may be required to perform these services in foreign countries. If support is needed in a foreign country, the contractor may be required to support foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, mobile training teams, and mobile education teams under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP) /Security Assistance Training Program (SATP).

title: FY27 Mentor Protege Program (MPP) Broad Agency Announcement
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.AMC.ACC.ACC-CTRS.ACC-APG.W6QK ACC-APG
description_text:
1.0 Introduction & Program Overview
Mentor-Protégé Program:
The Department of War (DOW) Mentor-Protégé Program (MPP) is a premier business development initiative designed to incentivize large prime contractors to provide developmental assistance to small businesses. The primary goal is to enhance the capabilities of Protégés, enabling them to become more competitive and expand their presence in the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). Through this mutually beneficial partnership, Protégés gain valuable technical and business expertise, while the DoD cultivates a broader, more resilient supplier network to support its mission.
2.0 MPP Broad Agency Announcement (BAA)
BAA Management and Agreement Execution : The Office of Small Business Programs & Industry Engagement (OSBP&IE) manages this Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) and is the primary point of contact for submissions and review.
Opportunity Description:
Opportunity Name: FY27 Mentor-Protégé Program (MPP) Agreement Call
Opportunity Number: Refer to posting
Opportunity Type : This is a 2-phase submission.
Phase 1: White Paper submissions must be received no later than 5 p.m. Eastern Time (ET), 30 days after the announcement date.
Phase 2: Final Proposal requests will only be issued to selected White Paper submissions based on the evaluation criteria. Selected submitters will receive a Request for Proposal (RFP) for their Phase 2 response.
Dates: White Paper submissions must be submitted via email to the MPP Program Manager no later than 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET), 30 calendar days from the BAA announcement date . Submissions received after this deadline will not be considered until a subsequent evaluation cycle.
The Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) remains open, and White Papers are accepted on a rolling basis throughout the year. However, submissions are reviewed according to the following
Quarterly review cycle:
· Review Cycle I – March 29:
White Papers submitted on or before March 29 will be reviewed immediately following this date.
· Review Cycle II – June 30:
White Papers submitted after March 29 or before June 30 will be reviewed after June 30.
· Review Cycle III – September 30:
White Papers submitted after June 30 or before September 30 will be reviewed after September 30.
· Review Cycle IV – December 31:
White Papers submitted after September 30 or before December 31 will be reviewed after December 31.
· Review Cycle V – March 31:
White Papers submitted after December 31 or before March 31 will be reviewed after March 31.
Submission Address: All White Papers are to be submitted by email (Subject: FY27 MPP Mentor-Protégé Agreement – (Insert Mentor & Protégé Name) . All submissions will be acknowledged with an email confirmation within 24 hours of receipt. If a confirmation email is not received within 48 hours, please follow up to ensure delivery. The Government is not responsible for email system malfunctions or undeliverable email.
BAA Submission Process:
Phase I. White Paper Submission (Attachment 1): Firms respond to this Open Call by submitting a white paper summarizing technical and cost information.
Phase II. Final Proposal Submission: After successful evaluation of white papers, selected firms provide a full Technical Proposal, Cost Proposal (Attachment 2), and Letters of Endorsement. The proposal will be reviewed for allowability, allocability, and reasonableness.
Protégé Pilot Initiative (PPI) Application (Attachment 3): The Department of War (DOW) Pilot Protégé Initiative (PPI) was established under Pub. L. 117-63, div. A, title VIII, §856 (d), Dec. 23, 2022, 136 Stat, 2726. This pilot initiative provides Proteges in DOW reimbursable agreements an opportunity to propose projects supporting the advancement of engineering, software development, or manufacturing customization in support of the War Fighter. Proposals are limited to a maximum of up to 25% of the annual budget of the respective reimbursable agreement. The proposed amount will be used exclusively by Protégé for the project. PPI applications are due in Phase II with the final proposal.
3.0 Mentor-Protégé Program
MPP Objective & Benefits:
To leverage Mentor-Protégé Agreements (MPAs) to mature Protégé firms for its critical mission spaces. By incentivizing Mentors to provide technical assistance, the agency aims to integrate high-capability small businesses into the Defense Industrial Base. This expansion directly strengthens national security by ensuring a resilient, value-added supply chain capable of safeguarding sensitive defense assets.
4.0 Participation Requirements
Protégé Firm Eligibility:
Small business concerns eligible for federal contracts.
Meet SBA size standards.
Must satisfy one of the following: HUBZone, Women-Owned, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Native American/Hawaiian controlled, socially/economically disadvantaged, employing severely disabled individuals, nontraditional defense contractors, or contributing to national security priorities.
Mentor Firm Eligibility:
Prime contractors with $25M or more in DOW contracts in the last fiscal year.
Active DOW subcontracting plan.
Financially sound, good character, not debarred/suspended or under investigation.
Approved by DOW OSBP as a Mentor.
Note: Active SAM.gov registration is mandatory for all vendors, mentors, protégés, and subcontractors at the time of package submission.
5.0 Technical Priorities
The core technical priorities are structured around modernizing technology, integrating data, and securing IT infrastructure:
1- Modernizing IT Infrastructure and Cloud Optimization
National Background Investigation Services (NBIS): A primary focus is accelerating the delivery of NBIS to transform personnel vetting, including full transition to NBIS for Personnel Vetting operations including background investigations.
Cloud Migration: Transitioning systems, such as the Defense Information System for Security (DISS), to a secure, self-hosted cloud environment and transforming it to enhance scalability and agility.
System Modernization: Replacing legacy, slow-performing and siloed systems with modern, high performing components based on the DoW mandated Modular Open Systems Architecture (MOSA) approach.
2- Data Integration and Advanced Analytics
Data-Driven Decision Making: Enhancing data understanding, delivery, and management to enable faster, more accurate risk determinations in personnel and industrial security.
AI and Machine Learning: Implementing a variety of Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities to analyze large volumes of data, identify anomalies, and calculate potential risks while keeping human judgment at the center of trust decisions.
Automated Data Ingestion: Developing tools to automatically ingest data, improving the speed and quality of background investigations.
3- Cyber and Industrial Security
Securing the Defense Industrial Base: Protecting cleared facilities and IT systems from cyber-attacks, foreign insider threats, and vulnerabilities.
Behavioral Threat Analysis Capability (BTAC): Enhancing capabilities to detect insider threats through advanced behavioral monitoring.
Zero Trust Architecture: Strengthening cyber posture through modern, secure IT solutions that protect sensitive national security information.
4- Digital Workforce and Governance
Digital Skills Training: Empowering a skilled digital workforce, including expanding AI experience and cybersecurity awareness.
IT Governance: Establishing enterprise-wide IT, data, and cybersecurity governance to ensure compliance and efficiency.
6.0 Scope of Work
Allowable Developmental Assistance:
Refer to DFARS Appendix I, paragraph I-106 for specific guidelines regarding allowable developmental assistance. Mentors can use authorized subcontractors to provide developmental assistance to proteges. Authorized subcontractors include Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), Minority Serving Institutions (MSIs), APEX Accelerators (formerly Procurement Technical Assistance Centers (PTACs), Manufacturing Innovation Institutes (MIIs), and Small Business Development Centers (SBDCs).
Types of developmental assistance include, but are not limited to:
Technical/Engineering Assistance: Technology transfer, certifications, quality processes, manufacturing improvements.
Business Development Assistance: HR, accounting, marketing, safety, and company policies.
Federal Contract Language Training: FAR/DFARS compliance assessment and workshops.
Facility Clearance (FCL) Sponsorship & Guidance: Establish a formal process to assist the protégé in obtaining and maintaining a facility clearance to be eligible for classified contracts.
Personnel Security & FSO Training: Provide templates, policies, and coaching for running a compliant Facility Security Officer (FSO) program and managing cleared staff.
Cybersecurity Compliance (DFARS/NIST/CMMC): Train the protégé to build a secure IT/cyber program, share assessment tools, and prepare them for audits.
Insider Threat & Counterintelligence Program Setup: Provide insider threat program templates, reporting procedures, and exercises on recognizing suspicious activities.
Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) Compliant Accounting & Contracting Knowledge: Help the protégé set up a compliant accounting system, understand cost/pricing rules, and manage contracts.
Proposal Development Support: Share sample proposals, compliance checklists, and proposal writing strategies tailored to DCSA/DOW opportunities.
Foreign Ownership Control and Influence (FOCI): To work with U.S. companies must identify and implement FOCI mitigation strategies, which are evaluated before final proposals are submitted.
Information Technology Systems Enhancement: Upgrading hardware, software, and network infrastructure to improve performance, security, and scalability.
Note: Cybersecurity compliance (NIST SP 800 / CMMC Level I) is not reimbursable. However, DOW OSBP encourages companies to seek the services of Project Spectrum (https://www.projectspectrum.io) for CMMC Level 1 at no cost.
7.0 Proposal & Evaluation Process
Phase I. White Paper Submission:
Requirements: Complete the white paper template (Attachment 1) including a White Paper Submission (Attachment 1): Firms respond to this Open Call by submitting a white paper summarizing technical and cost information.
Formatting: 15 pages max, 12-pt font, Word/Excel/PDF formats (Letters of endorsement excluded).
Note: Email is for unclassified use only. For assistance with classified communications, please reach out to the contact above through an unclassified email first.
Evaluation Criteria:
Alignment with National Security and DOW priorities
Alignment with strategic plan and mission
Technical approach and developmental assistance
Cost reasonableness
Letters of Endorsement from CEOs (Pass/Fail)
FOCI Questionnaire (Pass/Fail)
Statement of Mentor and Protégé eligibility
Engineering and Technical Assistance is 50% or more of the overall proposed costs (Pass/Fail)
HBCU/MSI/APEX/SBDC/WBC/MEP Involvement (Pass/Fail)
Selection Notification for Phase II:
The MPP-I will notify offerors of their white paper evaluation results. Please note that debriefs or feedback regarding Step-One submissions will not be provided. Selected participants will receive an official invitation via email to proceed to Phase II. However, this invitation does not guarantee an award, as all selections are contingent upon successful negotiations and the availability of funds. Do not submit formal proposal materials until a specific request is received.
8.0 Phase II. Final Proposal Submission & Award
Final Proposal Requirements:
Invited offerors must submit a final proposal (updated white paper) within 30 calendar days of notification, unless an extension is granted. This submission must include a Statement of Work, a comprehensive technical approach for technology transfer, and a fully disclosed cost proposal aligned to a work breakdown structure. The proposal must demonstrate alignment with strategic objectives and detail the involvement of HBCU/MSI/SBDC/APEX/MII organizations. Additionally, signed Letters of Endorsement and Commitment from both Mentor and Protégé leadership are required. Final agreements will be issued as subawards under the DOW OSBP MPP-I Cooperative Agreement.
Optional: Protégé Pilot Initiative (PPI) Application:
The PPI application (Attachment 3) provides an opportunity for Protégés to propose projects supporting the War Fighter. Proposals are limited to a maximum of 25% of the annual budget of the reimbursable agreement. Applications are due with the final proposal.
Evaluation and Award Notification:
The evaluation criteria for the formal proposal are the same as for the Phase I white paper. Following the evaluation of submissions, selected organizations will be notified of their acceptance into the Mentor-Protégé Program via both a phone call and an official email.
Note: Specific requirements of the proposal will be outlined in the request for proposal.
9.0 Agreement Administration & Terms
Award Details and Period of Performance:
Reimbursable Mentor-Protégé Agreement contracts will follow a structured invoice and payment schedule. Instructions will be provided upon Agreement Award. The total Period of Performance for any proposal is capped at three (3) years/36 months. Typically, standard agreements entail a 12-month base Period of Performance with the option for two (2) additional 12-month periods, subject to the discretion of the Government.
Note: This BAA is soliciting Reimbursable agreements only, no Credit or Hybrid agreements will be accepted.
Cost, Reimbursement, and Liability:
All costs associated with preparing and submitting white papers, draft proposals, or final agreement proposals are the sole responsibility of the Mentor and Protégé. The Government will not reimburse or be liable for any expenses incurred.
Government Rights and Termination Clauses:
The Government reserves the right to review an MPA at any time. The Government may modify, suspend, or terminate an MPA for reasons including, but not limited to, lack of progress, non-compliance, or if it is no longer in the Government's best interest. Mentors and protégés may also initiate termination per DFARS Appendix I. Termination, suspension, or modification will not give rise to any claim for damages. Written notice will be provided; however, the Government reserves the right to withhold specific details related to the reason(s) stated. Instructions for termination by the Mentor or Protégé will be included in the MPA contract.

Secretary of the Air Force Concepts Development and Management (SAF/CDM)
Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) for Defense-Related Activities
FA7146-21-S-C001
Summary
Title: CDM Defense-related activities
Type: Closed/Open Two-Step CSO with Calls:
Open Period Initiation to 1 September 2026 (for receipt of White Papers) Ordering Period Initiation to 30 September 2026
Active Calls for White Papers & Point of Contact (PoC) Information
Call A002 (Posted 03/20/2026): AF/A1 Agile Refactoring and Integration (AR&I)
A call for white papers for the AF/A1 Agile Refactoring and Integration (AR&I) has been issued
For details, please refer to the full attachments to the posting.
Points of contact for this specific call are located within the call documentation.
Update 8/12/2026: The Phase 2 for this call is on hold until further notice due to priority changes in the department. An update to the SAM posting will be issued once the activity continues.
Purpose and Objectives
This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) is initiated under the Defense Commercial Solutions Offering Pilot Program. It allows for the competitive selection of innovative commercial items, technologies, and services. An award may result from a general CSO that identifies areas of mission or technical interest and includes a technical evaluation by subject matter experts.
SAF/CDM seeks innovative commercial solutions or new capabilities that fulfill its requirements, close existing capability gaps, and/or offer technological advancements in meeting the Objectives and Focus Areas detailed in the CSO attachment.
Submission Process
This CSO follows a two-step process before any award.
Step 1 White Paper Submission: Contractors may submit White Papers at any time during the Open Period. These should include a Cover Page, a Technical/Management section, and a Rough Order of Magnitude. When submitting, the email subject line must include the CSO number (FA7146-21-S-C001) and the specific call number, if applicable. Multiple submissions are permitted.
Step 2 Proposal Submission: Following a review of the White Papers, the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) may invite selected contractors to submit a full Technical/Management and Price proposal. A proposal will not be considered without a prior White Paper submission and an invitation from the PCO.
Eligibility and Award Information
Eligibility: This is a full and open acquisition. White Papers will be considered from all interested vendors, including small businesses and non-traditional contractors. Foreign participation is allowed as specified in the attachment.
Award: The Air Force anticipates making multiple awards under the Federal Acquisition Regulations or via Other Transaction Agreement authority. The Government reserves the right to award some, all, part, or none of a contractor's proposal.

This constitutes the Office of Inspector General's (OIG) Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), to solicit proposals from interested parties on a specific subset of OIG services. The OIG reserves the right to select for award all, some or none of the proposals in response to this announcement. A formal Request for Proposal (RFP), solicitation, and/or additional information regarding this announcement will not be issued. All applicable solicitation provisions, instructions, terms and conditions are contained in the attached documents. Specific clauses for any resultant contracts will be negotiated at contract award.

Specifically, the OIG does not fall under the purview of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). This BAA is intended for proposals related to professional, consultant and support services only.
USPS OIG contract holders must comply with the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1972, as amended (38 U.S.C. 4211 and 4212), for contracts worth $150,000 or more. See https://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm#overview for reporting requirements.
Proposals are accepted on a rolling basis, unless noted otherwise, and contracts may be awarded throughout the solicitation period. A position listing may result in one or more contract awards. The solicitation period ends on September 30, 2027, or until replaced by a subsequent BAA, whichever is earlier.
Please see the attached solicitation documents for details.

title: USAF Special Operations Forces Technical Data Management, Development, and Provisioning Project
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.AIR FORCE MATERIEL COMMAND.AIR FORCE LIFE CYCLE MANAGEMENT CENTER.INTELLIGENCE, SURVEILLANCE, RECONNAISSANCE - SPECIAL OPERATIONS FORCES.FA8509  AFLCMC WIUKA
description_text:
The Government is conducting market research to identify capable small-business sources with the expertise, capabilities, and relevant experience to provide technical manual development and revision, technical data management, configuration management support, engineering support services, and AC-130J-only provisioning support for Special Operations Forces (SOF) C-130 aircraft (AC, MC, and HC). AC-130J provisioning support includes; identification and recommendation of spare, repairable, and consumable material requirements; and support for provisioning conferences and Government-approved Source, Maintenance, and Recoverability (SMR) code recommendations.
The Government is considering an acquisition strategy consisting of a five-year technical data contract, including one 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods.
The contractor would provide technical writing and technical data development support for incorporation into subsequent Technical Order (TO) revisions and updates.
The contractor would provide configuration management support, including the policies, procedures, techniques, and tools necessary to:
• Evaluate proposed changes;
• Maintain configuration status accounting;
• Track and document changes; and
• Incorporate approved changes into TOs in accordance with applicable requirements.
The contractor would provide engineering services, as required, to review, compile, and develop authorized source data into technical data suitable for Government review and approval.
The contractor would provide AC-130J-only provisioning support to identify and recommend spare, repairable, and consumable material requirements necessary to support system operation and sustainment; recommendation of SMR codes for Government approval, and participation in AC-130J provisioning and configuration guidance conferences.
The contractor would furnish all material, support equipment, tools, and services necessary to perform the required technical data development, technical manual revision, configuration management, and engineering support services, except for items expressly identified as Government-furnished. The contractor would be responsible for providing, utilizing and maintaining, all support equipment and/or software required at their facility or a subcontractor’s facility.
The Government currently possesses a specification-control drawing for certain components within the anticipated requirement. The drawing is not a manufacturing (“build-to”) drawing. Lockheed Martin possesses the complete technical data package for the applicable part(s), and the Government does not currently have authority to release, purchase, or provide access to the complete package.
Respondents are advised that participation in this market research effort does not guarantee participation in any future solicitation or contract award. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting responses to this RFI.

title: Aegis Based Defense Engineering Services
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NAVAIR.NAVAIR NAWC WD.NAVAL AIR WARFARE CENTER
description_text:
1) INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE: NAWCWD is seeking technically competent sources for engineering services in support of Test and Evaluation (T&E) and systems engineering activities related to Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) and Theater High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) programs at Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF). The purpose of this sources sought is to determine what companies are capable of providing the required services in a competitive procurement and to gain market knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classifications relative to the North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code 541330 for Engineering Services which has a corresponding size standard of $47 million. Responses to this sources sought synopsis will be utilized by the Government to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and make appropriate determinations about potential sources. No solicitation is currently available and as such this is not a request for proposal and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. A decision to set aside all or part of this requirement is dependent upon a review of the information submitted in response to this sources sought. After review of responses to this sources sought, a synopsis and/or solicitation announcement may be published.
(2) PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: This requirement is for engineering services to be provided in support of Test and Evaluation (T&E) and systems engineering activities primarily related to Aegis-Based Defense, formerly Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) and Sea-Based Weapon Systems. Engineering service are provided to other entities, including (but not limited to) Program Executive Office Integrated Warfare Systems (PEO IWS), various Hypersonic programs, and Allied Foreign Military Sales (FMS) partners. Aegis-Based Defense is one weapon system in the layered defense provided for the United States and its deployed forces, friends and allies against ballistic missiles of all ranges in all phases of flight. This defense is provided through an integrated Ballistic Missile Defense System (BMDS), developed by the Missile Defense Agency (MDA). MDA is responsible for fulfilling the goals set out in the National Missile Defense Act of 1999 in deploying “as soon as is technologically possible an effective National Missile Defense system capable of defending the territory of the United States against limited ballistic missile attack”. In support of this goal, the Aegis-Based Defense program needs to collect high fidelity system under test and auxiliary sensor data in order to evaluate the results of the flight test and to determine if the system(s) met the mission objectives. Additionally, auxiliary sensor data is highly valuable in providing forensics for any anomalies that may have occurred during these events. Pre-/post-mission data analyses of this auxiliary sensor data is critical these flight test scenarios. This is a follow-on contract to N6893622D0024. The existing contract is Cost-Plus Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Level of Effort (LOE), and was awarded to Raytheon (RTX) on a sole source basis. The new contract will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP).
(3) REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: The MDA / Aegis-Based Defense program requires high fidelity pre-mission planning, real-time mission conduct and execution support, post-mission data analysis, and reporting of test results of high profile flight test events. Support shall be provided to various flight test events and systems engineering activities. This includes mission planning, test planning, generating test procedures, real-time mission conduct, data collection, real-time range safety mission support, mission data analyses and reporting, operations research support, and technical management support.
Aegis-Based Defense requires support for test planning, test conduct, data reduction/analysis, and reporting of auxiliary sensor data during flight test events. This includes in-depth pre-mission analysis, which provides inputs to instrumentation, sensor data collection CONOPS, and sensor configurations to maximize valuable data collection. Recommendations for test support positions (TSPs) to auxiliary sensors will aid in maximizing valuable data collected.
Inputs to test plans as well as mission requirements are needed to ensure mission test objectives are met. This includes auxiliary tracking and data collection objectives based on mission priorities and overall test objectives. Understanding test objectives will translate directly into what instrumentation should be used and how they should be configured. This includes inputs to all test participants (sea-based, ground-based, airborne, and space-based).
Real-time mission conduct support assists auxiliary sensor participants to make adjustments to configurations, tracking objectives, and/or tracking CONOPS based on changes to mission scenarios. This support can ensure successful data collection during live missile and test vehicle launches. Mission conduct and execution support includes providing sensor and analysis support to assist range safety.
Complex analyses and reporting of test results is needed to evaluate weapons and weapon systems to ensure mission test objectives have been met. This includes ingesting, reducing, processing, and analyzing all auxiliary data (optical, radar, telemetry) and data formats. Analyses and test results should be shared with the government and test community to ensure proper communication and collaboration.
(4) PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: This effort will primarily be performed at PMRF at Barking Sands, Kauai, HI. Support will also be conducted at the following national test ranges and locations: Joint Base Pearl Harbor Hickam (JBPHH) on Oahu, HI; Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division (NAWCWD) Point Mugu Sear Range (PMSR) at Point Mugu, CA; Vandenberg Space Force Base (SFB) in CA; Reagan Test Site (RTS) on Kwajalein Atoll; Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER) in AK; Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS) at Cape Canaveral, FL; Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) at Patuxent River, MD; and the Missile Defense Integration and Operations Center (MDIOC) at Colorado Springs, CO.
(5) CONTRACT TYPE: The Government is considering a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Idefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a five-year Ordering Period.
(6) SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: The Government requests that responses to this sources sought include the following: demonstrated capability to ingest, reduce, process, and analyze auxiliary sensor data and applicable data formats for the MDA /Aegis-Based Defense program. Auxiliary sensor data includes optics, radar, and telemetry, and applicable formats include binary, ASCII, and movie formats (h264, mp4, mkv, avi, mpg, etc.). Data analyses includes data reduction, data tracking algorithms, signature generation, data display/visualization, brightness/contrast and image enhancement, data registration, image sequence output, and background subtraction.
Demonstrated capability to generate an early track of a launch vehicle to provide a state vector solution to range safety entities for immediate awareness and assessment of the vehicle trajectory status to the range safety officer. This will allow range safety to take corrective action (if needed) and prevent the vehicle from violating range safety boundaries (i.e. – IIP destruct limits, safe firing bearings, etc.). This system must be capable of meeting all range safety assessment criteria, including latency times, data rate, and first state vector solution time.
Demonstrate ability to support Navy optical data collection aircraft with optical Subject Matter Expert (SME) for mission planning, sensor calibrations, real-time inputs to tracking operators, mission conduct, and post-mission data analysis.
Demonstrate familiarity with test ranges, range instrumentation, range safety criteria, and range data collection capabilities. Assessment of test range capabilities, site surveys, and inputs for range instrumentation to improve data collection during test events.
(7) ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:
Upon evaluation of capability statements, if it is determined that this requirement will be unrestricted and procured on a competitive basis, the Government intends to evaluate Small-Business responses and conduct further market research to identify a subcontracting goal.
CONTRACTOR RESPONSE: Any firm believing it can fulfill the requirement identified may submit a written response.
The written response shall reference solicitation number N6893627R5001 and provide a capability statement that clearly indicates the firm’s experience, assets, background, and ability to perform he required work.
Contractor responses shall also include the following information:
a) A reference to the solicitation number N6893627R5001 and brief title of this announcement;
b) Company name and address;
c) Company's point of contact name, phone number, and e-mail address;
d) Declaration as to whether a U.S. or foreign company;
e) Company size (Small or Large according to the identified NAICS and size standard identified);
f) If your company is a Small Business, specify if your company is one of the following: (a) Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); (b) HUBZone Small Business; (c) 8(a) Concern; (d) Woman-Owned Small Business; (e) Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business;
g) Provide any anticipated teaming arrangements and delineate between work to be accomplished by the prime and the work to be accomplished by the teaming partners;
h) A brief capabilities statement package (no more than 5 pages in length, double spaced, 12-point font minimum), demonstrating ability to perform the specific requirements discussed above;
i) An outline of previous projects related to the program description, identify specific work previously performed or currently being performed related to the program description; and
j) Any other specific and pertinent information as pertains to this particular area of procurement that would enhance the Government’s consideration and evaluation of the information submitted.
Questions and comments are highly encouraged.
If necessary, an opportunity for a site visit will be offered after the solicitation is issued. No Vendors should appropriately mark any data that is proprietary or has restricted data rights.
Responses shall be submitted by e-mail to the point(s) of contact listed above no later than 30 days from this notice date.

description_text:
This is a sources sought notice issued in accordance with FAR Part 5. For information regarding this acquisition, contact the Contracting point of contact listed herein. All inquiries shall be in writing.
The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) intends to award one (1) Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) to obtain contractor support services for non-inherently governmental project management and technical support for projects within Futures Development and Integration (CG-FD&I) Directorate, Chief of Staff (CG-COS), DCS-5, and Assistant Commandant for Capability (CG-7) which houses several subordinate offices around future agency strategy, capabilities assessment and execution, analysis, wargaming, modeling and simulation and similar.

description_text:
SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE
Tracking Number 632675877
The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) is seeking sources for the Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Command, Control, Communications, and Enterprise (C3E) Electromagnetic Spectrum Information (EMS) Information Technology Modernization (EMS-IT Mod) Support Contract
