DISA/Procurement Services Directorate/Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization (DISA/PSD/DITCO)/PS63
6910 Cooper Avenue
Fort Meade, MD 20755-0549
INTRODUCTION:
This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of small businesses and large businesses (including the following subsets: Small Disadvantaged Businesses, Certified 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Businesses and Woman-Owned Small Businesses) to provide the required products and/or services.
This notice also seeks feedback from industry on the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) in support of this requirement (Attachment 1).
DISA PAE C3E seeks capabilities from potential sources to provide a full range of technical, engineering, and administrative support services as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) and applicable Department of War (DoW) guidelines. This requirement may in the future expand, change, or be revised due to upgrades or transition of systems as a result of technology evolution, industry standard changes and DoW regulatory requirements.
The anticipated Period of Performance is:
15 FEB 2027 – 14 FEB 2031. One twelve-month base period with three option periods.
Base Period: 15 FEB 2027 – 14 FEB 2028
Option Period 1: 15 FEB 2028 – 14 FEB 2029
Option Period 2: 15 FEB 2029 – 14 FEB 2030
Option Period 3: 15 FEB 2030 – 14 FEB 2031
The anticipated Place of Performance will be at the contractor’s site with some contractor support required at PAE C3E located in the DISA Headquarters, 6916 Cooper Avenue, Fort George G. Meade, MD 20755.
DISCLAIMER:
THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS NOTICE. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.
CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND: The EMS IT Mod PMO Support requirement is a new requirement.
REQUIRED CAPABILITIES:
In response to this SSN, Vendors must describe their knowledge and experience to address the following capabilities. All of the required capabilities are critical elements of this requirement.
1. Describe your company’s knowledge and experience in designing and applying intuitive, user-centric design and user-experience methods to mission applications in high-stress tactical and disconnected, disrupted, intermittent, and limited (DDIL) environments
Please provide examples of:
Requirements gathering, such as eliciting, validating, and prioritizing user requirements through user-story sessions, tabletop exercises, stakeholder engagements, and one-on-one interviews.
Experience engaging with users in Combatant commands (CCMDs), DoW, or joint exercises to obtain user feedback to incorporate into final product-design and development decisions.
2. Describe your company’s knowledge and experience supporting EMS mission analysis workflow optimization across core functional areas, including frequency assignment and allocation, spectrum certification, host-nation coordination, electromagnetic interference (EMI) resolution, Joint Communications-Electronics Operating Instructions (JCEOI), and Joint Restricted Frequency List (JFRL) management.
Please provide specific examples of:
Working with Government stakeholders and development teams to reverse engineer, document, and track current and past workflow processes.
Identifying or implementing automation, process-improvement, and operational-efficiency opportunities within EMS mission systems.
3. Describe your company’s experience evaluating and integrating non-proprietary, peer-reviewed physics-based modeling and simulation (M&S) models into cloud and edge environments.
Please provide examples of:
Assessing model maturity, interoperability, performance, and supportability
Developing technical requirements, application programming interfaces, and interface control documents
Rendering model outputs within geospatial interfaces
Testing model performance in DDIL environments on Joint Operational Edge (JOE) nodes.
4. Describe your company’s experience integrating electromagnetic spectrum capabilities with Joint Command-and-Control and Joint Tactical Fires systems.
Please provide examples of:
Developing spectrum-data exchange requirements, architectures, standardized data formats, interfaces, and protocols.
Resolving interoperability issues and designing resilient edge capabilities for DDIL environments, including store-and-forward synchronization, reliable data synchronization, and bandwidth optimization.
Integrating EMS functions into JOE platforms.
5. Describe your company’s knowledge and experience preparing large structure, semi-structured, and unstructured datasets - including high-volume PDFs – for migration, reuse, and integration into an enterprise EMS data environment.
Please provide specific examples of:
Applying large language models (LLMs), machine learning (ML), or comparable automated techniques to identify, extract, cleanse, validate, and remediate legacy data.
Developing data-remediation rules, workflows, quality-acceptance criteria, and automated processes.
Mapping legacy data structures and formats to a unified EMS data standard.
SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:
Vendors must have a Secret facility clearance. Please provide your current Facility Clearance level. Personnel that perform on this requirement must have a minimum of Secret security clearance at the time of contract performance.
This requirement is for Systems Engineering and Technical Assistance (SETA). Please reference Section 13b of the PWS and identify any potential conflict of interests when submitting your response.
Please note that the contractor to whom this requirement is awarded (as well as its affiliates and subcontractors) shall be prohibited from participating in the development or production of any products related to this program IAW FAR 9.505-1 and DFARS 209.571-7.

Please outline the company's areas of expertise and those of any proposed JV/partner who combined can meet the specific requirements contained in this notice.
SUBMISSION DETAILS:

CAGE Code;
Prime contract vehicles; to include ENCORE III, SETI, NIH CIO-SP4, NASA SEWP V, General Service Administration (GSA): OASIS, ALLIANT II, VETS II, STARS III, MAS (including applicable SIN(s), groups or pools), or any other Government Agency contract vehicle that allows for decentralized ordering. Businesses who wish to respond must send a response via email NLT 2:00 PM Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) on October 27, 2026 to cori.m.bowen.civ@mail.mil and ramona.y.lin.civ@mail.mil . Interested businesses should submit a brief response to this notice with a statement package addressing the specific questions above (no more than seven pages using 12-point proportional font) demonstrating the ability to perform the services listed under Required Capabilities and providing feedback on the draft PWS. Slick sheets, trifolds, and other marketing materials will not be reviewed.
PAE CE3 representatives may choose to contact business responding to this notice and hold further market research discussions. Such discussions would only be intended to obtain further clarification of potential capability to meet the requirements.
The Government does not intend to answer questions regarding this sources sought notice or a potential solicitation that may result from this notice. Questions will only be accepted if a pre-solicitation or a solicitation notice is issued.
Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, must be clearly marked on all materials. All information received that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. All government and contractor personnel reviewing submitted responses will have signed non-disclosure agreements and understand their responsibility for proper use and protection from unauthorized disclosure of proprietary information as pursuant to 41 USC 423. The Government shall not be held liable for any damages incurred if proprietary information is not properly identified.

Request for Information
Project Manager, Short and Intermediate Effectors for Layered Defense
Avenger Weapon System Support
Synopsis:
The Short and Intermediate Effectors for Layered Defense (SHIELD) Project Office is conducting market research to determine if there are potential sources with the capability to provide engineering and technical services in support of the Avenger Weapon System. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201 (e), responses to this notice are not an offer and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. No contract award is intended as a result of this request. The U.S. Government will not pay for information received. The Government Point of Contact will be Ms. Lillian Irby, U.S. Army Contracting Command-Redstone, and can be contacted via email: lillian.m.irby.civ@army.mil. EMAIL ONLY, NO PHONE CALLS.
Administrative:
In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not an offer and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. No contract award is intended as a result of this request. The U.S. Government will not pay for information received.
Per FAR 52.215-3, Request for Information (RFI) or Solicitation for Planning Purposes:
a. The U.S. Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or to otherwise pay for the information solicited, except as an allowable cost under other contracts as provided in subsection 31.205-18, bid and proposal costs, of the FAR.
b. Although the term “proposal” may be used in this RFI, your response will be treated as information only. It shall not be used as a proposal.
c. This RFI is for planning and market research purposes only and should not be considered as a request for proposals or as a solicitation to do business with the U.S. Government.
Avenger System Overview:
The Avenger mission is to provide a lightweight, highly mobile, shoot-on-the-move, day/night, short-range surface-to-air missile and gun weapon system. Mounted on an M1097A2 High Mobility Multi-Purpose Wheeled Vehicle (HMMWV), it engages Fixed Wing, Rotary Wing, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle, and Cruise Missile threats. The Avenger M47A2 derivative system, termed Slew-to-Cue, receives cues to a track from an outside source and automatically slews to and follows the target beyond the line of sight.
Avenger System Description:
The Avenger Weapon System is a critical component of the Army’s Short Range Air Defense System (SHORADS). The system consists of:
Two Standard Vehicle Mounted Launchers mounted on a turret
A .50 caliber machinegun
Forward Looking Infrared
Laser Range Finder
Environmental Control Unit/Prime Power Unit
Auto-track systems and Identification Friend or Foe system
Two 12V, 100 AMP lead-acid batteries connected in series (24V system power)
360 degrees continuously rotating, gyro-stabilized turret mounted on the HMMWV
The fire unit can engage targets with missiles or the machinegun while on-the-move or stationery. The gunner can operate the system in-turret or from a remote location using the Remote-Control Unit.
Scope of Work and Contractor Requirements:
The SHIELD Project Office is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing comprehensive engineering and technical services in support of the Avenger Weapon System and all derivative systems.
Note : Proposers must have the required capability at the start of the performance period and must be able to perform all required tasks . Partial solution proposals will not be considered.
Core Support Areas:
The contractor will be responsible for complex system engineering, manufacturing, test equipment, logistics, and sustainment support. Support includes, but is not limited to:
Engineering and Integration:
Providing detailed technical expertise for Avenger Weapon Systems, Line Replaceable Units (LRU) (all variants), support equipment, and system interfaces.
Designing and fabricating new solutions based on the current Avenger design to meet U.S. Government requirements.
Performing complex system integration tasks.
Providing software engineering and development for current and future software requirements.
Providing in-depth system engineering analysis to support performance improvement, failure analysis, and other engineering activities.
Testing & Analysis:
Supporting test activities, including the assessment of test results.
Providing design and technical support for existing and future contractor- and U.S. Government-owned test equipment.
Performing reliability assessments and failure analysis with corrective action identification at the system and LRU level.
Quickly and effectively analyzing and resolving hardware/software failures to restore operational capability.
Logistics:
Performing logistics functions, including technical manual generation/modification, maintenance support, system repairs and Field Service Representative support.
Training and Fielding:
Redesigning, replacing, installing, and training on all LRUs.
Conducting training and system deployment, including New Equipment Training.
Supporting sustainment training for deployed systems.
Quality Assurance and Security:
Complying with all Quality Assurance requirements (configuration management).
Maintaining a facility compliant with all federal, state, and local requirements.
Ensuring compliance with current DoW Information Assurance and Cybersecurity requirements.
Meeting all contractor security, Communications Security, Federal, and DoW requirements, including Defense Security Service accreditation for both unclassified and classified information.
Personnel Requirements:
The U.S. Government requires a team of Field Service Representatives with expertise in Weapon Systems operation, sustainment, mechanical/electrical maintenance, physical security, and site maintenance.
Security Clearance: Contractor employees will be required to hold and maintain a Secret security clearance.
Operations: The contractor is responsible for the safe, efficient, and compliant operation and maintenance of Avenger Weapon Systems and sites.

title: Support for NRC’s Force-On-Force (FOF) Inspection Activities
agency: NUCLEAR REGULATORY COMMISSION.NUCLEAR REGULATORY COMMISSION.NUCLEAR REGULATORY COMMISSION
description_text:
THE U. S. NUCLEAR REGULATORY COMMISSION (NRC) is issuing this Sources Sought Synopsis as a means of conducting market research or as a market survey to determine the availability and potential technical capability of the business community to provide all management, supervision, administration, and labor required for the facilitation of the NRC’s Force-on-Force (FOF) inspection activities. The Contractor will be required to provide logistical support and expertise in Engagement Simulation Systems (ESS)/Multiple Integrated Laser Engagement Systems (MILES) equipment and weaponry required to conduct approximately 20 to 25 inspections (i.e., 40 to 50 FOF exercises) per year, in accordance with NRC’s site schedule. The scope of the proposed support shall include logistical, maintenance, and on-site support for NRC-evaluated FOF exercises at approximately 57 NRC-licensed facilities that are on a triennial FOF inspection cycle. Each NRC FOF inspection may include multiple exercises. Services will be performed remotely to the NRC located in Rockville, Maryland. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 541614, Logistics Management Consulting Services.
The purpose of this announcement is to provide potential sources the opportunity to submit information regarding their capabilities to perform work for the NRC in accordance with the requirements outlined below. All interested parties, including all categories of small businesses (small businesses, small, disadvantaged businesses, 8(a) firms, women-owned small businesses, service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, and HUBZone small businesses) are invited to submit a response.
The capabilities package submitted by a vendor should demonstrate the firm’s ability, capability, and responsibility to perform the principal components of work listed below. The response should also include past performance/experience regarding projects of similar scope by listing the project title, general description, period of performance, the dollar value of the contract, and name of the company, agency, or government entity for which the work was performed .
THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does NOT constitute a request for proposal. Submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary. The Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred.
BACKGROUND: This project supports Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations Part 73, which requires the NRC’s evaluation of its licensees’ ability to provide assurance that they can protect against the threat of radiological sabotage. As part of the effort to improve FOF testing at NRC-licensed facilities, the NRC has taken steps to enhance the realism of engagements between the nuclear facility’s security forces and postulated mock adversary forces during FOF exercises. For efficiency and flexibility in this effort, the NRC requires use of ESS and MILES equipment and weaponry. The Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Enterprise Assessment contractor has been supporting the NRC in these FOF exercises since October 1, 2012 under an Interagency Agreement. However, DOE’s contract will expiring in February, 2027, therefore, the NRC needs to find an alternative vendor who is capable of providing these services with very little or no ramp-up time.
CAPABILITIES REQUIRED:
The NRC is seeking to identify commercial organizations capable of providing the required logistical support to enable the NRC licensees to become familiar with the ESS/MILES equipment being used in the FOF exercises, provide instruction on how to mount licensee-provided equipment to the ESS weapons to reflect the licensee’s profile (i.e., sighting systems, slings, etc.), provide the necessary ESS/MILES equipment support during each NRC-evaluated FOF exercise, and conduct maintenance and cleaning of the equipment and weapons on an as needed basis.
Personnel working on this contract shall meet the minimum requirements for experience as follows:
Labor Categories Required and Position Minimum Requirements
ESS Support Manager/Senior ESS Specialist III* (One Full-time) - Current Armorer certification and ten-year minimum experience in management in order to manage the operation and liaison with the NRC in addition to ten-year minimum experience in operating and maintaining ESS/MILES equipment and weapons
ESS Armorer Technician III* (Two Full-time) - Current Armorer certification with five-year minimum experience in operating and maintaining ESS/MILES equipment and weapons
ESS Armorer Technician II* (2 Full-Time) - Current Armorer certifications with three-year minimum experience in operating and maintaining ESS/MILES equipment and weapons
ESS Armorer Technician I* (3 Full-Time) - Current Armorer certifications with one-year minimum experience in operating and maintaining ESS/MILES equipment and weapons
Administrative Support Specialist I - (One Full-Time) One-year minimum experience in office administration
*NOTE: These positions may require security clearances. The clearance level depends on the type of access to classified information and the secure facilities that will be needed to perform the work.
SCOPE OF WORK:
The NRC anticipates that the Statement of Work (SOW) will include the following tasks and deliverables:
Task 1 - Perform Warehouse Property Inventory Check
The Contractor shall lease a warehouse for the storage of ESS/MILES equipment and three Logistical Support Trailers (LST) and three pick-up trucks. NRC will provide the Contractor a hard copy list of NRC equipment currently being stored in the warehouse. The Contractor shall coordinate with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) for updating the inventory of each equipment in the warehouse each year. During the length of this contract, the Contractor shall tag and track the warehouse equipment and shall notify the COR in writing if there is a discrepancy in the inventory, such as an item being missing or damaged. The Contractor shall work with the COR in maintaining an accurate list of property inventory.
Task 2 - Provide Recommendations for Purchase of ESS/MILES Equipment and Weapons
Per COR request, the Contractor shall conduct market research and provide recommendations for the purchase of replacement ESS/MILES equipment and weapons. These recommendations shall consider getting quotes from multiple sources, and reviewing the FAR’s list of mandatory sources, the GSA Schedule, and excess from other agencies. Following market research, the Contractor shall provide recommendations to the COR in writing with the item specifications, pricing, method of market research, and how the equipment and weapons would benefit the NRC.
Task 3 - Transport and Operate On-Site Logistical Support Trailers
The Contractor shall transport and operate on-site Logistical Support Trailers (LSTs) for the maintenance, storage, and issuance of ESS/MILES equipment and weapons approximately twice monthly. The Contractor shall support the NRC FOF exercises with qualified personnel and the use of three LSTs. The LSTs are configured to provide secure storage and transportation of the ESS/MILES equipment and weapons. Additionally, the LSTs shall serve as a point of issuance and return of exercise equipment. The Contractor shall retain sufficient spare equipment in reserve to ensure sufficient equipment is available. The Contractor shall maintain a lease for three trucks suitable for transport of the LSTs. The Contractor shall maintain service agreements and ensure scheduled preventative maintenance and timely repair of the assigned LSTs and trucks. The trailers and trucks shall be replaced or refurbished on a five-year depreciation schedule, as directed by the COR.
Task 4 - Set up Logistics and Exercises
1. Coordinate Logistics for Exercises
As part of planning and preparation, the Contractor shall coordinate with NRC staff, licensee staff, and the mock adversary force lead (when applicable) regarding scheduling exercises, logistics, special needs (e.g., power supply or parking for trailer), and contingencies for en route emergencies, where applicable.
The Contractor shall ensure all logistical support for the NRC FOF exercises are accomplished (i.e., ammunition, weapons, administrative supplies, etc. are ordered and shipped to training sites). Weapons and equipment shall be appropriately tested (to ensure functionality), maintained, and prepared for transport.
Provide On-Site Support
1. Provide Set-up/Familiarization/CAF Support
The Contractor shall perform the following: 1) provide set-up and configuration of trailer; 2) provide ESS/MILES Safety Briefing and familiarity training presentations, to be presented either in-person by the Contractor or used in computer-based training (CBT), as appropriate, to NRC-licensee/utility security force and mock adversary force personnel, which shall include information such as safety features of ESS/MILES; 3) assist licensee personnel with any requested modifications to weapons (e.g., mounting preferred optics) and assist with ensuring each individual’s weapon is properly sighted, according to site procedures); 4) perform inspections of MILES harnesses and weapons and associated MILES equipment prior to each FOF exercise; and 5) provide MILES and/or specially designated adversary gear to the mock adversary force, as well as support, as requested by the mock adversary director or NRC inspection team leader.
2. Provide FOF Exercise Support
Typically, two NRC-evaluated FOF exercises take place (i.e., on Tuesdays and Wednesdays). The Contractor shall: 1) ensure that an ESS/MILES Safety Briefing was conducted via in-person by The Contractor or by licensee CBT to all exercise participants prior to conducting each exercise. The briefing shall describe and present information such as the safe and seamless integration of MILES equipment into existing procedures and protocols for conducting FOF exercises; 2) provide for issuance and retrieval of ESS/MILES weapons and equipment; and 3) provide on-site support for NRC inspection staff and licensee controllers in addressing any issues with functionality of weapons and equipment. The Contractor shall coordinate with a Saab Technician on any Saab equipment-related issues and repairs, and on download of exercise data upon conclusion of each exercise.
3. Coordinate with Saab Technician
The Contractor shall coordinate with the Saab Technician on ESS/MILES equipment and weapons inspections, preventative maintenance, and repair (as necessary). The Saab Technician shall support the FOF exercises by preparing MILES equipment for exercise activity and by producing a post-exercise MILES Activity Report (MAR). Upon completion of each exercise, a MAR shall be compiled by the Saab Technician from all MILES equipment used during each exercise. EA shall ensure that the Saab Technician submits the MAR to the NRC inspection team following the completion of each exercise. The Saab Technician’s responsibility shall ensure all MILES equipment is operational. The Contractor shall assign an expert MILES/ESS technician who shall provide a continuing interface with Saab on technical aspects of Saab support and expertise with Saab equipment operability.
Task 5 - Perform Quality Check of Government Property Post Exercise
Upon conclusion of the final exercise, the Contractor shall account for all NRC property and prepare the trailer for transport back to home location (or in some instances, directly to another licensee site).
Task 6 - Conduct Post-Exercise Activity
Upon arrival at home location, the Contractor shall: 1) unload equipment; 2) clean, inspect and arrange for repair of equipment, as necessary; 3) arrange for scheduled maintenance of trailer and truck; and 4) conduct weapon inspection and cleaning.
Task 7 - Prepare and Submit an After-Action Report
The Contractor shall prepare an After-Action Report (AAR) describing the results of each site visit to the COR. The AAR shall address the planning and execution of each visit, expert consultation provided in each exercise, and a compilation of the daily reporting activity highlights.
Task 8 - Support Adversary Selection and Training and TTC Training
1. Support Selection and Requalification Training of Mock Adversary Forces
The Contractor shall issue equipment and weapons to selectees and/or members during selection and training events of mock adversary forces, as directed by the COR. Armorers shall provide support during the selection and training events, to include Safety Briefings to mock adversary force selectees and members, to ensure safe operation of ESS/MILES. Upon completion of training, the Contractor shall collect and safeguard the ESS/MILES gear.
2. Support TTC Weapons Course
The COR will contact the Contractor when the TTC has ample participation in its Weapons Course which is conducted in Chattanooga, TN. The Contractor shall provide one armorer, as well as provisional ESS/MILES equipment and weapons, corresponding to the number of classroom participants. The Contractor shall coordinate logistics of participation and support of the TTC training with the Weapons Course Coordinator.
GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED PROPERTY (GFP)
Government-furnished property used for supporting the NRC will be maintained at the Contractor’s warehouse facility. The property will be controlled and accounted for by The Contractor and NRC as required in the FAR. Acquisition and disposition of equipment will be conducted by The Contractor through coordination with the NRC COR.
The NRC has purchased three trailers for the Contractor to transport and operate as Logistical Support Trailers (LSTs) for the maintenance, storage and issuance of ESS/MILES equipment and weapons at the specified NRC facilities, approximately one to three trips per month, as determined by the NRC schedule. The Contractor shall retain trailers at the Contractor’s Warehouse Facility. The Contractor will ensure scheduled preventative maintenance and timely repair of the LSTs. The Contractor will also provide a schedule for replacement or refurbishment of the LSTs based on a five-year depreciation, as directed by the COR.
HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE
If your organization has the capability and capacity to perform, as a prime contractor, all of the services described in this notice, then please respond to this notice and provide written responses to specifically address the requirements stated above in addition to the following questions. Please do not include any proprietary or otherwise confidential information in the response, and do NOT submit a proposal. Proposals submitted in response to this notice will NOT be considered.
Organizations responding to this market research survey should keep in mind that only focused and pertinent information is requested. If significant subcontracting or a teaming arrangement is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. Submission of additional materials such as glossy brochures or videos will not be accepted and is discouraged.
ADDITIONAL MARKET RESEARCH QUESTIONS
Organization name, address, email address, Web site address, telephone number, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI).
What size is your organization with respect to NAICS code identified in this notice (i.e., "small" or "other than small")? If your organization is a small business under the aforementioned NAICS code, what type of small business (i.e., small disadvantaged business, woman-owned small business, economically disadvantaged woman-owned small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, 8(a), or HUBZone small business), and confirm that you would be able to comply with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting? Specify all that apply.
Separately and distinctly describe which of the required capabilities listed above that your organization possesses and indicate your organization's role (prime contractor, first tier subcontractor, and/or supplier) in related contracts. Please also provide the contract number, contract type, customer name, address and point of contact phone number and email address, contract value, thorough description of supplies and services included in the scope of that contract, indication of how they are similar to the required capabilities described in this notice, period of performance (for services) or delivery date (for products), and any other relevant information.
Indicate whether your organization offers any of the required capabilities described in this notice on one or more of your company's own Federal Government contract vehicles (i.e., GSA Federal Supply Schedule contracts or Government-wide Acquisition Contracts) that the NRC could order from and, if so, which services are offered. Also, provide the contract number(s) and indicate what is currently available for ordering from each of those contract(s).
Provide a standard, non-proprietary commercial price list or similar standard non-proprietary commercial pricing information for how your company sells, as a prime contractor, required capabilities described in this notice that your organization has experience providing. Also, indicate what is included in that pricing.
Interested organizations responding to this Sources Sought Synopsis are encouraged to structure capability statements in the order of the areas of consideration noted above. All capability statements sent in response to this notice must be submitted electronically, via e-mail, to Carolyn.cooper@nrc.gov, either MS Word or Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF), within 15 calendar days from the date of publication of this notice. The subject line of the transmittal email must reference the notice ID number APP-27-CNRI-0001 .
DISCLAIMER AND NOTES: Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization’s potential capability and capacity to perform the subject work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. OBJECTIVE:
The USAF E-3G AWACS provides worldwide response to situations requiring immediate and continuous on-scene command, control, and battle management using embedded real-time surveillance to support employment of U.S. and allied combat forces. The E-3G consists of the air vehicle, sensor systems, and computing and communications equipment. The current USAF E-3G operational fleet consists of 15 operational aircraft. The E-3G DAR-400 (part numbers 63-2824652-01 through -03) is a mission critical asset and is in critical need of obsolescence resolution to prevent mission impact. Since the DAR-400 contains encrypted MCS, MSS, IPEC and GS data, a failure would directly impact operations and data security. General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS) has notified us that the DAR-400 will not be able to support or upgrade to changing NSA requirements.
SCOPE:
To execute the installation and integration of the obsolescence resolution for the mission-critical E-3G DAR-400 to prevent mission impact. The provided Government-owned KG-204 based solution is compliant with current DoD and NSA mandates to replace the legacy DAR-400 equipment.

title: Ground Systems and Mission Operations-4 (GSMO-4)
agency: NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION.NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION.NASA GODDARD SPACE FLIGHT CENTER
description_text:
This RFI is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals or a solicitation for a contract or grant award and it does not obligate the Government in any way. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this request.
Introduction
The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of supporting science and Earth science missions including, but not limited to: Earth Observing System; Earth Observing System Data and Operations System; Magnetospheric Multi-Scale mission; Global Precipitation Measurement mission; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; James Webb Space Telescope; Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (built by NASA for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration); Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope; and Solar Dynamics Observatory. This RFI is intended to gather market intelligence, technical approaches, and rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) considerations to inform a potential future procurement.
Background
The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) currently acquires mission operations support through the Goddard Space Mission Operations (GSMO‑3) contract. GSMO‑3 provides comprehensive, end‑to‑end mission operations services spanning the entire mission life cycle. The scope of work includes systems and facility engineering; launch and early‑orbit operations support; flight operations and flight dynamics services; sustaining engineering; and mission operations studies, design, integration, and testing of ground systems. Additional services include mission data collection and distribution, system administration, and information technology security and engineering analyses.
The GSMO‑3 contract supports a broad portfolio of NASA science and Earth science missions, including the Earth Observing System (EOS), Magnetospheric Multi‑Scale (MMS), Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Fermi Gamma‑ray Space Telescope, Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES), Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). These services are essential to sustaining and advancing NASA’s ground data systems and mission operations infrastructure, ensuring reliable communication, data processing, and mission control capabilities for ongoing and future missions. The contract also supports mission decommissioning and long‑term sustaining engineering required to maintain operational readiness for systems with multidecade lifespans. The scope also increasingly encompasses cloud infrastructure management, continuous cybersecurity monitoring, DevSecOps automation, and advanced collision avoidance/conjunction assessment activities.
Functions
FUNCTION 1- Mission Ground System Support Services
A. Ground Systems Engineering and Engineering Studies
B. Ground Systems Support Services
C. Ground Systems Integration and Test Services
FUNCTION 2 - Mission Operations System Support Services
A. Operations Systems Engineering
B. Launch and Early Operations Support
C. Flight Operations
D. Flight Dynamics Support Services
E. Mission Data Collection and Distribution
F. Mission Systems Sustaining Engineering
G. Systems Administration and IT Security
H. Database Administration
RFI Response Instructions
The Government is seeking feedback from contractors with relevant mission capabilities and experience. Responses should include the vendor implementation approach and rough order magnitude costs of performing the functions listed above. Responses should be limited to no more than 30 pages .
Transition from Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) to Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP)
The Government is evaluating the feasibility of transitioning the follow-on GSMO-4 requirement from a Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contract to a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract, either in whole or in part, including the use of Performance Based Payments for FFP Tasks. The Government seeks industry feedback regarding the practicality of such an approach.
Specifically, respondents are requested to address the following:
Is the current GSMO-4 scope sufficiently defined and stable to support an FFP contract? If not, identify the areas of uncertainty.
What technical, programmatic, schedule, or cost risks would your organization associate with transitioning this requirement from CPAF to FFP?
Which portions of the requirement, if any, do you believe are well-suited for FFP, and which portions would be more appropriately performed under another contract type (e.g., Time-and-Materials)? Please explain your rationale.
What assumptions or Government-provided information (e.g., historical workload, staffing profiles, performance metrics, technical baseline, service level agreements, demand forecasts, configuration data) would be necessary for your organization to develop a realistic fixed-price proposal?
What contract incentives or performance metrics would improve the viability of an FFP approach?
What acquisition or contract structure would best balance cost control, performance, innovation, and risk allocation for this requirement?
Please identify any lessons learned or best practices from similar transitions from Cost-Reimbursement to Firm-Fixed-Price contracts.
Are there specific contract provisions or performance requirements that should be modified to enable a successful transition to FFP?
Catalog Pricing Structure: The Government is exploring a 'Catalog-style' pricing structure for routine Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) operations, where missions are priced based on their Risk Classification (e.g., Class B, C, D). What are the benefits, risks, and potential cost-drivers your firm would associate with pricing mission operations by Class? What specific parameters, boundaries, or Service Level Agreements (SLAs) would be required in the catalog definitions to make this pricing model viable.
Core vs. IDIQ Structure: The Government is considering a contract structure that establishes highly stable, long-term flagship missions as the baseline 'Core' requirement, with all other missions and development efforts issued as IDIQ task orders. How would this Core-plus-IDIQ structure impact your pricing, workforce retention, and risk allocation strategies compared to a 100% IDIQ structure.
Requirements/Specifications

The Government maintains operations resources listed above. RFI responses may include the use of these GFE resources. For any GFE resources incorporated in their response, the vendor should include any GSMO implementation costs and the cost differences/savings as compared to the vendor providing all ground resources.

Submission Format Requirements
Use Times New Roman, 12‑point font for all text.
Maintain 1‑inch margins on all sides of every page.
The Cover Page and Table of Contents do not count toward the 30‑page limit.
Please do not paginate these two sections.
Submit your response in both PDF and Word (.docx) formats.
Email all submissions directly to daniel.s.han@nasa.gov .
In the email subject line , format the title exactly as:
“Response to GSMO‑4 RFI [Company Name, CAGE Code]”
Scope Guidance
NASA welcomes submissions that provide limited scope information for internal market research.
If your response covers only a portion of the contract scope, please clearly indicate “Limited Scope” on the Cover Page , along with a brief description of the capabilities included.
Q&A Sessions

NRCS Snow Survey maintains an extensive automated (SNOTEL) and manual (Snow Course) data collection network in the Western United States and Alaska. Congress mandated NRCS (then the Soil Conservation Service) in the mid 1930's "to measure snowpack in the mountains of the West and forecast the water supply." NRCS Snow Survey now provides reliable and efficiently collected data needed to produce water supply forecasts and to support resource management activities across the Western US. The high-elevation watershed locations, broad coverage, and real-time operation of the network provide important data to farmers, researchers, river and reservoir managers, emergency managers for natural disasters such as floods and droughts, and for power generation. In some remote locations, private local contractors have been utilized to conduct critical manual snow measurements. The contractors have the wherewithal (over-snow travel equipment, snow samplers) and knowledge of local terrain to complete work in a timely manner. Additionally, local surveyors have many years of experience using a federal snow sampler, calculating snow-water-equivalent, and communicating results to the main NRCS Snow Survey office. These surveyors are unique in terms of the combination of location, equipment, and willingness. Lastly, data continuity between years is key to making NRCS Snow Data most useful and to decrease data uncertainty (error). Year-to-year data continuity is best achieved by utilizing the same surveyors as long as possible.

title: Q519--Research Support Psychological Assessment for PTSD Clinical  Trial
agency: VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.RPO EAST (36C24E)
description_text:
Purpose
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is conducting market research in accordance with FAR Part 10 to determine the availability and capability of qualified small and large business concerns to provide psychological assessment services in support of a multi-site PTSD clinical research study.
This notice is for market research purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal (RFP), or commitment by the Government to award a contract.
Requirement Description
The VA requires contractor support to provide independent psychological assessment services for participants enrolled in a multi-site clinical trial Hybrid Implementation and Non-Inferiority Testing of Group Versus Individual Written Exposure Therapy (WET) for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), in a group format compared to the established individual format..
The contractor shall provide qualified evaluators to conduct structured diagnostic assessments remotely with access to HIPAA-compliant Box so that contractor can receive participant contact information securely and can transmit interview scores securely back to VA. For more information on Box, please see https://digital.va.gov/marketplace/product/box/
Must also have access to HIPAA-complaint video conferencing for conducting the interviews themselves and must be overseen by PhD-level clinical psychologists to ensure ongoing high quality practice. Participants must complete standardized diagnostic assessments at baseline, post-treatment, and three-month follow-up. These assessments include the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5) and the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI), both of which require administration by trained and qualified clinicians..
The anticipated effort includes approximately:
150 baseline CAPS-5 and MINI assessments
128 post-treatment CAPS-5 assessments
128 three-month follow-up CAPS-5 assessments
Total projected assessments: approximately 414.
Minimum Capability Requirements
Interested firms should demonstrate their ability to:
Provide master's- or doctoral-level clinicians trained in the administration of:
Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5)
Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI)
Recruit, train, supervise, and maintain an adequate pool of independent evaluators to support multiple research sites.
Conduct assessments using HIPAA-compliant video conferencing technology.
Securely receive and transmit participant information and assessment results using approved secure file-sharing platforms.
Conduct quality assurance and fidelity monitoring activities to ensure consistency and reliability of assessments.
Maintain compliance with applicable human subjects research requirements and regulatory training requirements.
Provide oversight by doctoral-level clinical psychologists with expertise in PTSD assessment and diagnosis.
Requested Information
Interested vendors shall submit a capability statement not to exceed five (5) pages that includes:
Company name, UEI, CAGE code, and business address.
Business size and socioeconomic status under the applicable NAICS code(s).
Experience providing psychological assessment services for:
PTSD research studies
Multi-site clinical trials
Federal agencies
Veterans or military populations
Experience administering CAPS-5 and MINI assessments.
Description of quality control and assessment fidelity procedures.
Description of available staffing resources and evaluator qualifications.
Recommended NAICS code(s) and rationale for why the code accurately describes the principal purpose of the requirement.
Any existing contract vehicles available for ordering these services.
NAICS Code
The Government is considering the following NAICS codes:
621330, Offices of Mental Health Practitioners (except Physicians)
541990, All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
Respondents are encouraged to identify the NAICS code they believe best represents the principal purpose of the requirement and provide supporting rationale.
Submission Instructions
Interested parties shall submit capability statements via email only to:
Ann Marie Stewart
Contracting Officer
Email: annmarie.stewart@va.gov
Responses are due no later than October 29, 2026, at 3:00 PM EDT.

description_text:
2. REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION & Performance duties
2.1 Scope of Support
The Contractor shall provide operational and strategic planning advisory support to the Area Support Group-Jordan (ASG-J) Operations Directorate (S-3), assisting in the coordination, development, and execution of comprehensive operational plans, contingency plans, exercises, and force protection programs in support of United States Army Central (USARCENT) and adjacent USCENTCOM entities.
2.2 Core Responsibilities and Duty Allocation
The following major duties (percentages approximate effort allocation) are derived from the official Army Position Description:
Physical Security and Force Protection Planning (approx. 30%): Develop, implement, review, and update comprehensive physical security and force protection plans, policies, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
Assist the ASG-J Provost Marshal Office (PMO) in identifying vulnerabilities and performing technical force protection inspections, assessments, and surveys.
Coordinate Mission Assurance Assessments (MAA) with USARCENT, conduct associated In-Progress Reviews (IPRs) and briefings and develop corrective action plans for identified deficiencies.
Coordinate with the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) to conduct physical security/force protection reviews on installation master plans, construction projects, and facility renovations pursuant to applicable DoD and Army regulations.
Deliberate and Crisis Action Planning / Contingency Plans (approx. 30%):
Integrate deliberate and crisis action planning support across USARCENT, subordinate formations, and USCENTCOM.
Serve as technical lead and project coordinator for contingency planning efforts, contributing directly to the drafting and refinement of Operations Plans (OPLANs), Concept Plans (CONPLANs), Operations Orders (OPORDs), Fragmentary Orders (FRAGOs), and Functional Plans.
Utilize the Joint Operation Planning and Execution System (JOPES) / Adaptive Planning and Execution (APEX) enterprise to formulate cyber operations annexes, appendices, and operational deployment workflows for deployed forces.
Exercise and Training Support / MDMP-JOPP (approx. 20%):
Support ASG-J S-3 operations to ensure field and command-post exercises align with USARCENT doctrine, policies, and priorities.
Apply deep operational understanding of Commander’s Intent, Running Estimates, Intelligence Preparation of the Battlefield (IPB), Deliberate Planning, and the Military Decision Making Process (MDMP) / Joint Operational Planning Process (JOPP) across Unified, Joint, Combined, and Service-component echelons.
Facilitate Operational Planning Teams (OPTs) and Joint Planning Groups (JPGs); conduct Course of Action (COA) development, analysis (wargaming), comparison, and decision briefing preparation for senior leadership.
Inter-Agency Representation and Staff Coordination (approx. 20%):
Represent the ASG-J S-3 during cross-functional working groups, operational syncs, and planning conferences.
Liaise with internal directorates, tenant units, host-nation representatives, and higher headquarters to align ASG-J operational roadmaps with theater campaign goals.
2.3 Mandatory Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)

agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.AIR FORCE MATERIEL COMMAND.AIR FORCE LIFE CYCLE MANAGEMENT CENTER.INTELLIGENCE, SURVEILLANCE, RECONNAISSANCE - SPECIAL OPERATIONS FORCES.FA8552  AFLCMC WIU
description_text:
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)
RELIABILITY AND MAINTAINABILITY (R&M) ENGINEERING SUPPORT FOR HELICOPTER DIVISION WEAPON SYSTEMS
Below is the general information and instructions, however the full RFI document is attached.
This effort is for an 8a setaside. However, responses from disadvantaged small businesses not certified as 8a participants are encouraged to respond and will be considered on a case by case basis in accordance with current FAR regulations.
Requirements
The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the facilities, expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements to complete R&M related tasks for helicopter platforms TH-1H, UH-1N, HH-60W and MH-139. These services include, but are not limited to, conducting root cause analysis of in-service failures, developing and updating preventative maintenance procedures, recommending design modifications to improve reliability, and providing on-site technical assistance to maintenance crews, etc.
Government furnished equipment will be provided as outlined in individual task orders as necessary. The Contractor is responsible for providing, maintaining, and calibrating all support equipment required at their facility or a subcontractor’s facility. Contractor furnished material or parts used for replacement shall equal or exceed the quality of the original material or parts.
Contractors/Institutions responding to this market research are placed on notice that participation in this survey may not ensure participation in future solicitations or contract awards. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this survey.
INSTRUCTIONS:
This effort is for an 8a setaside. However, responses from disadvantaged small businesses not certified as 8a participants are encouraged to respond and will be considered on a case by case basis in accordance with current FAR regulations.
Questions relative to this market survey should be addressed to the Program Manager (PM), Contract Specialist (CS), and Contracting Officer (CO).
PURPOSE/DESCRIPTION
The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the
facilities, expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements to complete R&M related tasks for helicopter platforms TH-1H, UH-1N, HH-60W and MH-139.
This requirement is for engineering support services. Our strategy is a for five to ten-year cost plus fixed-fee contract (basic plus four to nine option years) and will potentially continue through FY37.
Contractor’s facility must be located in the local area of Robins Air Force Base due to the need for frequent face to face reviews and collaborative efforts. The local facility must at a minimum accommodate the program management and technical writer personnel. Manufacturing and engineering labs can be located elsewhere if necessary.
When tasked by the Government, the Contractor shall perform analyses and/or services which include but are not limited to engineering research, rapid solutions, prototypes, integration and technical support services required to isolate and analyze system deficiencies, identification of appropriate solutions and production of all engineering data required to implement the improvements to prevent an adverse impact to rotary-wing aircraft reliability and maintainability. The tasking will be submitted via an Engineering Support Task Request (ESTR) form.
Examples of tasks that will be required on this contract include, but are not limited to:
Reliability Centered Maintenance (RCM) and Age Exploration (AE) program sustainment tasks such as maintenance data trend analysis, failure mode and effects analysis updates, preventative maintenance package task updates, AE candidate follow-up and updating existing RCM databases
Targeted Analyses which would include failure analysis, follow- up analysis, and independent technical reviews
The contractor shall provide engineering and technical expertise in support of avionics systems, aircraft structures, mechanical systems and support equipment as it applies to reliability and maintainability
Development of technical procedures and technical data updates
Supportability analyses
Conduct research related to supportability improvement
conduct research and analysis for rotary-wingHelicopter Division aircraft repairable items to correct asset shortfalls and maintain designated asset supply levels
fabricate or procure hardware or software to be utilized in modifications/upgrades as required by individual ESTRs
accomplish data mining/trend identification tasks
integrate new technologies into current system architectures to enhance reliability and maintainability as specified
provide engineering support to resolve electrical, avionics and EMI/EMC deficiencies on rotary-wing aircraft
In the cases of EMC/EMI compatibility or where proposed mechanical or electrical solutions do not comply with form, fit, function, and interface requirements, the contractor shall analyze the test plan(s) and other existing TDPs that define the platforms to ensure possible deficiencies are detected and resolved
provide hazard identification through safety analysis conducted on system/subsystem modifications, engineering change proposals, mishap data and deficiency reports
provide engineering support to isolate and analyze aircraft functional system deficiencies, identify appropriate solutions and produce all engineering data required to implement the improvements to prevent an adverse impact to rotary-wing aircraft reliability and maintainability
rapid response to field locations for “no notice” deficiency, grounded aircraft and mishap support
assist in maintaining configuration management for rotary-wing weapon systems
perform R&M evaluation and insertion of new technology into existing helicopter systems for modernization to improve performance, reliability, maintainability, and survivability of weapon systems, subsystems, and the support equipment
develop and provide prototypes, pre-production items, or one-time production items in quantities as specified in the ESTR to allow for testing by both the contractor and Government. The contractor shall provide prototypes, pre-production units, or one-time production units, conduct tests and evaluate the item(s) against specified requirements, and deliver an industry-validated technical documentation package
modification/changes/updates to engineering drawing packages, technical orders (TO), Flight Manuals and time compliance technical orders (TCTO)
provide engineering and technical installation services to support trial install/kit proof activities as they apply to reliability and maintainability
investigate failure modes for low Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF) components and develop/recommend solutions to improve MTBF via component redesign, material changes and/or maintenance practice changes
POCs for this RFI are:
Michelle Privette, Program Manager (michelle.privette@us.af.mil)
Phillip Russell, Contracting Officer (phillip.russell.9@us.af.mil)
Brent Talbert, Contract Specialist (brent.talbert@us.af.mil)
RFI responses are due 4 November 2026, 5:00pm EST

title: Water Resources Analytical and Professional Support Services - Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC)
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.US ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS.SCO ALEXANDRIA.ENGINEER CENTER SUPPORT ACT HUMPHREYS.W4LD USA HECSA
description_text:
The US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Mission Support Battalion (UMSB) intends to solicit for and negotiate several Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)s styled as a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) using full and open competition under RFO (FAR) Part 15 procedures. The MATOC is anticipated to contain a period of performance consisting of one base year plus four one-year option periods and may include an option to extend the MATOCs for up to six-months to extend the contract in accordance with RFO 52.217-8. The anticipated maximum shared capacity of the MATOC is $49,500,000.00. A partial small-business set-aside is anticipated which will be determined by tasks in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The tasks to be set-aside are to be determined.
Background :
The USACE Institute for Water Resources (IWR) is a Field Operating Activity (FOA) under the Commanding General, USACE, and the staff supervision of the USACE Headquarters (HQUSACE) Directorate of Civil Works under the direction of the Deputy Commanding General for Civil and Emergency Operations (DCG-CEO) and the Director of Civil Works (DCW). IWR was established in 1969 to provide the USACE Civil Works (CW) Program with the capability to analyze and anticipate emerging water resources trends and issues facing our nation. From its beginning IWR has responded to the continuing changes in water resources development policies.
IWR occupies a unique position within the USACE CW program and remains integral for insights into a host of complex and rapidly changing water resources issues. IWR operations are performed through these operating units:
USACE Mission Support Battalion (UMSB) in Alexandria, VA;
Hydrologic Engineering Center (HEC) in Davis, CA;
Navigation and Civil Works Decision Support Center (NDC) co-located at the Humphreys Engineer Center (Alexandria, VA) and the USACE New Orleans District office in New Orleans, LA;
Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center (WCSC) also located at the USACE New Orleans District office in New Orleans, LA
Risk Management Center (RMC) co-located in Denver, CO and Pittsburgh, PA.
IWR is the USACE center of expertise for integrated water resources management, focusing on planning analysis, hydraulic and hydrologic engineering, and on the collection, management and dissemination of Civil Works and navigation information, including the nation’s waterborne commerce data. IWR serves as the USACE center of expertise for dam and levee safety, analysis and adaptive management of water resources and infrastructure based on severe weather event data, planning, and environmental conflict resolution. IWR also operates the International Center for Integrated Water Resources Management (ICIWaRM) , under the auspices of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) .
IWR fulfills its mission by providing: (a) analysis of emerging and long-term water resources and waterborne transportation trends, needs and issues, (b) state-of-the-art planning and hydrologic engineering methods, models and training, (c) policy and program analyses and strategic planning to support and improve the effectiveness and efficiency of CW program. Among the specific purposes stated, delivered services will require consideration of data and analytical requirements of the USACE’s CW water resources missions to include the areas of study and expertise that IWR provides to its customers through its research, analysis, technical assistance and training activities to include but not limited to Navigation, Flood and Storm Damage Reduction, Aquatic Ecosystem Restoration, Emergency Management, Water Supply, Hydropower and Recreation.
IWR routinely provides technical assistance on a broad range of topic areas to USACE Headquarters and the Major Subordinate Commands (divisions, districts, and laboratories), other US Army Commands, federal and state agencies, foreign nations, and international organizations.
Description of the Requirement :
This MATOC will obtain products and professional services through technical research and analytical support, data management, facilitation, and training for IWR that is generally not readily available within the USACE. These services will be used by IWR to accomplish missions including but not limited to: Support, operation, maintenance, upkeep, enhancement, and development of Automated Information Systems (AIS) and applications operated and/or otherwise managed by IWR and its various centers. These services will require consideration of data and analytical requirements of the USACE’s CW water resources missions to include the areas of study and expertise that IWR provides to its customers. These systems include:
a. Analysis of emerging trends and issues in anticipation of changing water resources management conditions and the corporate development of policies, programs
b. Systems-based planning methodologies, tools and training across the CW portfolio for analysis, economic and socio-economic assessments.
c. Project-, regional- and national-level economic analysis, multi-criteria and risk-informed analysis, economic and socio-economic assessments:
d. State of the art hydrologic and hydraulic engineering tools, methodologies, models and management systems and associated planning and environmental methods, models and training.
e. Advanced engineering risk management expertise for dam, levee and infrastructure safety, and the development, application and stewardship of the engineering practice involving contemporary risk-related methods, models and training.
f. Support for USACE to anticipate, prevent or minimize water conflicts and coastal flood risk
g. Support for the USACE Community of Practice for Conflict Resolution and Public Participation to lead facilitation for stakeholder support.
h. Expertise on water security and Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) applied by the U.S. State Department, United Nations, other U.S. and international institutions and Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), to address water and natural resources planning, water policy and governance, water management, trans-boundary water conflict mitigation, and other water-related challenges within the U.S. and around the world.
i. Assistance to HQUSACE, Army, and DoW, working in partnership with USACE MSCs and DoW COCOMs, for strengthening theater security cooperation by facilitating civilian and military collaborations, emphasizing multi-national force capacity development on the life-cycle planning of the humanitarian response and consequence management across all forms of extreme water events and other natural and technological disasters.
j. A critical mass of knowledge on the engineering and scientific aspects of, extreme weather events, and other risk factors in collaboration with interagency partners and study development
k. Enterprise-level financial analysis expertise in support of the CW mission and USACE intergovernmental collaboration on public works infrastructure investment decisions. Development and sustainment of USACE financial programs such as CWIPF This support will include assistance and guidance related to the outreach, accounting, project and borrower eligibility screening, FCRA compliance, and related efforts necessary for successful implementation of the federal credit program (including through its existing partnership with EPA to help develop and implement CWIFP) .
l. Technical support to USACE on a wide range of water resources, marine transportation, flood/coastal storm risk reduction, conflict resolution, international water and natural resources stewardship and ecosystem management issues.
Scope :
The scope of this contract includes all of the Civil Works mission areas (i.e. Navigation, Flood Risk Management, Aquatic Ecosystem Restoration, Hydropower, Regulatory, Recreation, and Water Supply) providing capability for technical research and analysis, data management, training and facilitation activities, among other technical specialties support as they relate to relevant USACE missions.
Within these mission areas there are several key programs included in the scope of the contract. These mission areas include the following: Coastal Storm Damage Protection; emergency management and resilience adaptation relating to severe weather events; Asset Management/ USACE Infrastructure Strategy/ Public Private Partnerships/ Financing; Hydrologic and Hydraulic Planning and Engineering; Sediment Management and other issues as they arise within the Civil Works Program.
In addition, the scope of this contract is intended to cover the areas of study and the kinds of expertise that IWR provides to its customers through its research, analysis, technical assistance and training activities (i.e. National and Regional Economic Analysis for Flood Damage Reduction, Coastal Storm Risk Reduction, Water Supply, Hydropower, Recreation projects; Ecosystem Restoration Analysis; National Studies for Water Resources Development; Regulatory Program Analysis; in the field of Navigation Decision Support Systems; Institutional Analysis; Benefit-Cost Analysis; Regional Impact Analysis; Value-to-the-Nation Assessments; Financial Analysis of Water Projects; Cost Effectiveness or Incremental Cost Analysis for Environmental Projects; Hydrologic and Hydraulic Analyses and Studies; Homeland Security; and Survey Research Methods including Questionnaire Design.). This description is not intended to be all inclusive of the scope of this effort, but rather details what could be involved under this contract.
It should be noted that while Navigation is not the primary focus of this contract, both deep draft coastal ports & harbors and inland ports & waterways, including the analysis of dredging and lock and dam systems, are addressed in this scope. However, the analytical aspects of USACE's navigation activities are included herein because of the integrated nature of the nation's water resources and multi-modal transportation systems so as to capture those broad-based studies and analyses of an integrated nature, particularly those which involve trade-offs between multiple water resources purposes which span the entirety of the Civil Works program.
Submission Requirements : Please submit a capabilities statement in addition to responding to the attached Questionnaire. Submissions should not exceed 20 pages. Times New Roman is the prefered font with the preferred size being 12-point. Graphs and tables may use a smaller font. The questionnaire, table of contents, cover pages and resumes are not included in the page count. Responses should be submitted in PDF format. Responses should detail your capability to perform the required services included in the PWS. All communication must be in writing. No oral communication will be considered.
See the attached PWS (draft) for additional information and the attached Questionnaire for the MATOC.

The Boeing B-52H Stratofortress is an American long-range subsonic jet-powered strategic bomber. The B-52 was designed and built by Boeing, which has continued to provide support and upgrades. It has been operated by the United States Air Force (USAF) since 1955 and was flown by NASA from 1959 to 2007. The bomber can carry up to 70,000 pounds (32,000 kg) of weapons and has a typical combat range of around 8,800 miles (14,200 km) without aerial refueling.
The sustainment of the B-52H currently includes the delivery of engineering design, engineering support, and technical support services crucial for the ongoing maintenance and operational readiness of the B-52H aircraft, including its components and associated support and test equipment. Engineering services will be required at the following USAF operational bases: Tinker AFB, Oklahoma; Edwards AFB, California; Minot AFB, North Dakota, and Barksdale AFB, Louisiana.
