title: Independent Commissioning Agent (Owner’s Advocate) Services for U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE HEALTH AGENCY (DHA).ARMY MED RES ACQ ACTIVITY
description_text:
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/SOURCES SOUGHT (SS) NOTIFICATION INCLUDING INDUSTRY FEEDBACK
1. Title : Independent Commissioning Agent (Owner’s Advocate) Services for U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases
2. Contracting Office : Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), R&D Contracting Division 1 - Branch 4
3. Location : Fort Detrick, Frederick, MD
4. Summary : This RFI/SS is issued solely for information and planning purposes and shall not be construed as a solicitation, restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach, or serve as an obligation on the part of the USAMRDC. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are advised that the United States Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI/SS will be solely at the interested responder’s expense. Not responding to this RFI/SS does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposal, if any is issued. No evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to Responders responding to this RFI/SS.
The information resulting from this RFI/SS will determine interest and capabilities available in the marketplace; and will assist in developing acquisition strategy.
5. Background : The U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRIID), located at Fort Detrick, Maryland, is the premier lead medical research laboratory for the U.S. Department of War's biological defense research program. Since 1969, USAMRIID has provided leading edge medical capabilities to deter and defend against current and emerging biological threat agents. The Institute is the only laboratory in the Department of Defense equipped to safely study highly hazardous pathogens requiring maximum containment at Biosafety Level 4.
USAMRIID has executed its mission from Building 1425. While historically significant, the legacy facility has surpassed its design lifespan. To sustain the DoD's biosafety integrity and research posture, the Department authorized the design and construction of a state-of-the-art replacement facility: Building 8100. Groundbreaking for the replacement complex took place in August 2009.
In 2013, during the final construction execution and fit-out phases, Building 8100 experienced a fire that damaged critical mechanical, electrical, and plumbing infrastructure, Building Automation System controls, and associated laboratory boundary zones. Recovering from this event and achieving facility handover has become an acute operational hardship for the biodefense mission, delaying the transfer of ongoing medical research from the aging legacy facility.
Note: Primary physical repair, mechanical completion, and prime construction execution are administered by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE). The Contractor shall not draft new architectural designs, stamp or seal engineering drawings, or execute physical facility redesigns.
6. Scope: The Government requires an independent, third-party technical Commissioning Agent (Owner's Advocate) to bridge the technical divide between USACE/prime construction execution and the stringent operational, biosafety, and regulatory compliance requirements of the end-user (USAMRDC Headquarters and USAMRIID). The Commissioning Agent will independently evaluate, witness, and verify critical facility systems and controls, and systematically advise the Government on executing a staggered/phased transition to achieve functional occupancy, biosafety accreditation, and facility registration.
How to Respond:
Please submit a Capability Statement that describes relevant experience, expertise, and
capabilities based upon the size and scope of this requirement as outlined in the draft Statement of Objectives (SOO).
Capability statements will be reviewed/evaluated for (1) Relevant experience based on the size and scope of the outlined requirement; (2) Company specific capabilities that match the work outlined in the draft SOO.
The Government will utilize the capability statements and market data collected from this notice to determine whether the proposed acquisition can be set aside for small business concerns (including 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), or HUBZone programs) or if full and open competition is required under NAICS code 541330.
The formal closing date for this RFI/SS and for the submission of all responses is NLT 9 November 2026 at 12:00PM ET. All responses shall be submitted electronically using PDF or MS Word formats to the POC, Elizabeth O’Hara at elizabeth.m.ohara3.civ@health.mil.
All responses received will be considered; however, a determination by the Government not to solicit the proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government reserves the right to continue market research and may issue additional RFIs if deemed necessary.
Each response should include the following information and must not be more than fifteen (15) pages in length:
Business Information:
Company name, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone, website address (if available), and the name, telephone number, and e-mail address of a point of contact having the authority and knowledge to clarify responses with Government representatives.
Unique Entity ID number, CAGE Code, and company structure (Corporation, LLC, partnership, joint venture, etc.). Companies also must be registered in System for Award Management (SAM, at www.sam.gov) to be considered as potential sources.
Any and all Government Contracts/IDIQs (e.g. Federal Supply Schedule, OASIS+, etc.) you currently hold (to include the vehicle and your contract number) that could be used to fulfill this requirement.
Organization Conflict of Interest:
Independent verification requires that the Commissioning Agent has no conflicting roles with the facility’s prime construction contractors.
Do you or any proposed team members have an active role in the construction, controls, or installation for Building 8100?
Please confirm your ability to certify organizational independence in accordance with FAR RFO 9.5.
Technical Experience & Biocontainment Qualifications:
Interested parties are requested to provide concise, direct responses to the following four (4) topic areas. General marketing literature is discouraged.
BSL-3 and BSL-4 Containment Experience: Describe your firm’s specific experience serving as an independent Commissioning Agent or Owner’s Advocate on high- and maximum containment biological facilities (BSL-3, ABSL-3, BSL-4, ABSL-4). Highlight your experience with continuous negative pressure cascades, Bubble Tight Dampers (BTDs), APR doors, chemical suit shower skids and effluent decontamination systems.
Regulatory Compliance Experience: Describe your firm’s past performance conducting comprehensive gap analyses, compiling Federal Select Agent Program (FSAP) registration packages (Biosafety, Security, Incident Response, BSAT Movement Plans under 42 CFR Part 73), verifying Tier 1 physical security layouts (minimum three physical barriers), and managing a live tracking register in secure environments.
Commissioning and Operational Systems Verification Experience: Describe your firm’s past technical experience performing 100% on-site witnessing and log analysis for critical containment failure-scenario testing (exhaust fan failure, emergency power transfers) to verify zero airflow reversals across BSL-3/4 boundaries, along with safety interlock witnessing (BTDs, APR doors, suit showers), effluent decontamination systems, and independent Commissioning Report critical reviews.
Project Management Experience: Describe your firm’s experience serving as an independent "Owner’s Advocate" bridging the gap between prime construction contractors and medical research end-users, managing a staggered/phased transition plan without creating an Organizational Conflict of Interest.
Industry Questions:
To assist the Government in continuing to define this requirement and acquisition strategy, the following feedback from industry is requested:
Phased Occupancy Isolation Strategy: From a commissioning perspective, what are the primary risks and recommended controls when executing a staggered occupancy plan (e.g., occupying administrative offices and BSL-1/2 suites while adjacent BSL-3/4 spaces are undergoing active failure testing)?
Centralized RFI & Compliance Tracking Strategy: Are there any technical or operational limitations to your team developing and maintaining a live web-based tracking register accessible to the Government 24/7?
Deliverable Review Timelines: Are the turnaround times of the deliverables feasible (e.g., reports due 10 days from witnessing testing)?
Government Furnished Property/Information: What Government-Furnished Property and/or Information would you require on Day 1 to prevent delays?
Industry Day/Pre-Solicitation Conference: The Government is contemplating hosting an Industry Day / Pre-Solicitation Conference prior to the release of the formal solicitation.
Would attending an Industry Day be beneficial in preparing a comprehensive, competitive proposal?
If so, would an on-site physical walkthrough be preferred; or a virtual technical briefing? What would be most valuable to cover during the event?
If an Industry Day is not beneficial, what information in addition to the Statement of Objectives would you require in order to prepare a proposal?
Source Selection Process: The Government is considering utilizing Oral Presentations (conducted in accordance with FAR RFO 15.105-1) as a primary technical evaluation methodology in lieu of, or in combination with, voluminous written technical proposals. Under this contemplated approach, key personnel (e.g., Lead Commissioning Engineer, Biosafety Regulatory Lead) would present the firm’s proposed technical approach directly to the Technical Evaluation Board, followed by structured Government Q&A.
Would the use of Oral Presentations be viewed favorably by your firm, and would it streamline your proposal preparation process?
What format or presentation structure would provide the best opportunity to demonstrate your team's expertise?
What challenges or concerns, if any, would your firm anticipate regarding participation in oral presentations?
Would your firm prefer oral presentations to be held on-site or virtually?
Contract Type Feasibility: The Government is looking to award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract with Performance-Based Milestone Payments (FAR RFO 32.10) . Payouts will be strictly tied to measurable events and transition milestones. Is this contract structure viable and realistic for an independent commissioning agent?
If yes, what specific risk-allocation mechanisms or prerequisite assumptions should the Government incorporate into the milestone schedule?
If not, what alternative contract pricing structure (e.g., FFP Level-of-Effort, T&M, or Cost-Reimbursement) would you propose, and why?
Rough Order of Magnitude:
To assist the Government in assessing budget feasibility, respondents are requested to submit a non-binding Rough Order of Magnitude pricing estimate. Respondents may include a brief narrative explaining key cost drivers, proposed labor categories, and any critical pricing assumptions or dependencies. To assist with the estimate, below are baseline parameters:
Facility Parameter
Sizing & Scope Baseline
Total Facility Gross Square Footage:
835,000 GSF
Administrative & Headquarters Spaces:
Approx. 310,000 GSF (administrative offices, conference center, command suites)
BSL-1 & BSL-2 Laboratory Spaces:
Approx. 185,000 GSF (general research, diagnostic, and cell-culture laboratories)
ABSL-2
Approx. 65,208 GSF (vivarium)
BSL-3, ABSL-3, & ACL-3 Containment:
Approx. 165,000 GSF (14 distinct laboratory, vivarium, and insectary suites)
BSL-4 & ABSL-4 Maximum Containment:
Approx. 65,000 GSF (4 distinct suit suites + 8 chemical suit shower corridors + 4 Airlocks)
Central Utility & Mechanical Support:
Approx. 110,000 GSF (chillers, boilers, emergency generators, continuous EDS plant)
Critical Sterilization Equipment:
12 double-door pass-through containment autoclaves
Effluent Decontamination System (EDS):
Continuous-flow thermal decontamination plant (150 gpm design flow)
Period of Performance (PoP):
Non-Severable 60-month period
Primary Location:
Building 8100, Fort Detrick, Maryland (assume regular on-site presence during active functional and failure-testing windows)

TMDE requires a vendor familiar with the complete NGATS software baseline to perform the updates to the software and maintain the current cybersecurity posture. This effort is to provide that support in an ongoing manner with no less than quarterly software deliverables and monthly status updates

description_text:
The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a “Developer” for purposes of developing a parking structure with at least 900 spaces that directly or indirectly benefits Veterans.
For purposes of this effort, the Developer would be a non-VA entity who has the qualifications outlined in Section V of this Notice. The opportunity would involve a Developer entering into an EUL with VA and financing, renovating/constructing, operating, and maintaining the parking structure.
VA’s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans, which may include certain parking structures. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA’s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program.
The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose assets at the James J. Peters VAMC Campus under VA’s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. The James J. Peters VAMC is particularly interested in a parking EUL to alleviate the significant on-campus parking shortage.

title: National Guard Bureau (NGB) Centralized Clinical Quality Management (CQM) and Credentialing & Privileging (C&P) Services for the Air National Guard (ANG)
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.NATIONAL GUARD BUREAU.HQ NGB.HQ NGB DIR OF ACQUISITIONS.W39L USA NG READINESS CENTER
description_text:
1. DISCLAIMER
THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for planning and market research purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or an Invitation For Bid (IFB), nor does it guarantee the issuance of a future solicitation. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice, nor will it reimburse any costs incurred by respondents. All information received in response to this notice marked "Proprietary" will be handled accordingly. Responses will not be returned, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to respondents.
2. REQUIREMENT BACKGROUND & SCOPE
The National Guard Bureau’s Operational Contracting Division (NGB-AQ-C), on behalf of the Air National Guard Surgeon General’s Office (NGB/SGOK), is conducting market research to identify sources capable of performing non-personal Centralized Clinical Quality Management (CQM) and Credentialing and Privileging (C&P) Program Management Services.
This effort is a follow-on requirement to Contract No. W9133L22C1003. In accordance with DoD Instruction (DoDI) 6025.13, Defense Health Agency Procedures Manual (DHA-PM) 6025.13, Air Force Instruction (AFI) 44-119, and DAFMAN 10-211, the scope has modernized to incorporate full clinical quality management and line-side embedded healthcare support.
Key requirement objectives include:
• Credentialing and Privileging (C&P) Administration: Centralized management and maintenance of electronic Provider Credential Files (ePCFs) within the Joint Centralized Credentials Quality Assurance System (CCQAS) for approximately 2,500 military and non-military Health Care Providers (HCPs) across 90+ ANG Wings and Joint Force State HQs.
• Board Operations: Full administrative, scheduling, technical, and data management support for quarterly Centralized Credentialing and Privileging Boards (CCPB) and out-of-cycle fast-track privileging actions.
• Primary Source Verification (PSV): Timely initiation and execution of paid and non-paid PSVs directly from issuing bodies for all provider accessions, re-privileging, and medical special pay verifications.
• Health Risk Management & Adverse Actions: Maintenance of adverse action files, tracking mandatory timelines, hearing board facilitation, and administration of National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB) Continuous Query (CQ) monitoring and fee management.
• Clinical Quality Management Support: Providing advanced clinical Subject Matter Expertise via a Clinical Nurse Specialist (CNS) to direct MHS-mandated Accreditation & Compliance (AC), Clinical Measurements (CM), and Clinical Quality Improvement (CQI) initiatives.
• Embedded Healthcare Support: Tracking and monitoring line-side embedded medical personnel and Integrated Operations Support (IOS) personnel via AFMEDCOM tracking applications.
3. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT DETAILS
• Acquisition Strategy: Market research will determine small business set-aside feasibility.
• Contract Type: Anticipated Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) with Cost-Reimbursable (No-Fee) CLINs for authorized travel and paid primary source verifications.
• Period of Performance: Anticipated one (1) 12-month base period plus four (4) 12-month option periods starting September 2027.
• Applicable Codes:
- NAICS Code: 541990 – All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services ($19.5M Small Business Size Standard)
- PSC: Q701 – Support: Medical - Healthcare
4. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS
Interested, capable businesses are invited to submit a Capabilities Statement / Executive Summary that demonstrates their ability to satisfy the stated requirements.
Submissions shall not exceed three (3) pages (8.5" x 11" format, 12-point font, 1-inch margins) and must include:
1. Company Information: Name, address, CAGE code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and primary Point of Contact (POC) details (name, title, email, phone number).
2. Business Size & Socioeconomic Status: Specify size status under NAICS 541990 (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), WOSB, EDWOSB, SDVOSB, HUBZone). If 8(a), include entry and exit dates.
3. Existing Contract Vehicles: Identify any active GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS), GSA OASIS+, or other GWAC/Governmentwide contract vehicles held by your company under which this work could be procured.
4. Technical Capabilities: Demonstrated capability and relevant experience in:
- Operating and managing ePCFs within CCQAS (or comparable DoD/DHA provider management systems).
- Conducting high-volume Primary Source Verifications (PSV) and administering NPDB continuous queries.
- Managing medical credentialing boards (CCPB) and provider adverse action case workflows.
- Delivering Clinical Quality Management (CQM) oversight and clinical nurse specialist (CNS) support in accordance with DoDI 6025.13.
5. Relevant Past Performance: No more than three (3) relevant past or present projects (Government or commercial) within the past five years detailing customer, contract number, dollar value, and scope description.
6. Subcontracting / Teaming & Limitations: If teaming or subcontracting is contemplated, describe the management structure. Under FAR 52.219-14, the small business prime must perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance incurred for personnel. Confirm your company's ability to satisfy this requirement.
5. SUBMISSION DEADLINE & POINTS OF CONTACT
Submissions must be received electronically via email no later than 5:00 PM EST on 11 November 2026.
Please submit responses via email to both points of contact below:
• Contracting Officer: MAJ Orlando Castro Vallescorbo – orlando.castrovallescorbo@army.mil
• Contract Specialist: MAJ Guy J. Maily – guy.j.maily.mil@army.mil
Please use the following subject line in your email submission:
"Sources Sought Response: NGB ANG CQM and C&P Services - [Company Name]"

title: MODIFIED WC-130J RTP APN-241 WEATHER RADAR SUSTAINING ENGINEERING SUPPORT RESEARCH AND SUPPORT TASK
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.AIR FORCE MATERIEL COMMAND.AIR FORCE LIFE CYCLE MANAGEMENT CENTER.INTELLIGENCE, SURVEILLANCE, RECONNAISSANCE - SPECIAL OPERATIONS FORCES.FA8509  AFLCMC WIUKA
description_text:
The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualifications to support repairability maintainability, and sustaining engineering for the modified WC-130J RTP APN-241 Weather Radar. Potential sources must possess the ability to provide engineering studies for the WC-130J RTP APN-241 system in resolving reliability and maintainability issues, obsolete parts issues, identify and propose solutions to Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) issues, and analyze failure trends from both the depots and the field level shops to support the MC-130J CR-2M developmental testing. For vendors wishing to participate in this Request for Information (RFI), after reviewing the requirement, provide documentation supporting proof of company’s capability to meet the requested requirements. If lacking sufficient experience/capabilities in a particular area, please provide details explaining strategies to overcome the lack of experience/capabilities to perform that portion of the requirement. In accordance with RFO 15.101(c), this RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or services.
Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses incurred in response to this RFI; all cost associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in future RFPs nor does it ensure participation, if an RFP is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Federal Business Opportunities (SAM.gov) website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Potential sources must be able to install the APN-241 Weather radar in addition to troubleshooting system discrepancies. Potential sources must be capable of and have access to Northrop Grumman equipment. Potential sources would need to have the ability to ensure equipment would be able to detect rain rates in real-time directly in front of the aircraft either proving or disproving the capability.
The proposed services are required to have access to Northrop Grumman Corporation, and their databases which contain/maintain the APN-241 Radar System engineering software.
The following equipment is required to sustain WC-130J RTP and will be provided as GFE: RTP P/N 780R270G10 (NSN 5841-01-522-1618), Transmitter Module (1A05) P/N 444R372G01 (NSN 5841-01-433-9455), and General-Purpose Processor Module P/N 824R061G06 (NSN 5998-01-534-5169).
The modified configuration provided is the following equipment: WC-130J RTP P/N 780R270G13 (NSN 5841-01-546-5654), Transmitter Module (1A05) P/N 444R372G02 (NSN 6130-01-433-9452). And General- Purpose Processor Module P/N 824R061G13 (NSN 5998-01-564-1569).
Provide sustaining engineering support and repairment of the modified configuration: WC-130J RTP P/N 780R270G13 (NSN 5841-01-546-5654), Transmitter Module (1A05) P/N 444R372G02 (NSN 6130-01-433-9452), and General-Purpose Processor Module P/N 824R061G13 (NSN 5998-01-564-1569)
Provide engineering support during developmental testing not to exceed 400-man hours and provide on-site support at Eglin AFB for two engineers for a total of three 5-day trips.
The proposed acquisition strategy is a 2-year (plus 6-month extension option) contract beginning in FY27 and continuing through FY29.

description_text:
Sources Sought Notice
THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT PAY NOR REIMBURSE ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH RESPONDING TO THIS REQUEST. THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT.
The Department of Veterans Affairs is seeking a qualified Architect-Engineering (AE) firm to provide Schematics, Design Development, Construction Documents, Technical Specifications, Construction Period Services, Site Visits, Cost Estimates, As-Built Documentation, and all other related information for Project 58A5-27-503 Project Design Replace Flat Roof at the Canandaigua VA Medical Center, 400 Fort Hill Avenue, Canandaigua, NY 14424. this project is to develop a conditions-report and design documents for replacing the existing flat roofs on buildings 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 36, 37, 118, and various connecting tunnels. The conditions report shall be prepared after a thorough investigation of the existing conditions with estimated costs and improvements. The following design will include all selected repairs and improvements from the conditions report that fit within VA construction budget.
As part of the report and design effort, the existing conditions shall be tested and verified, including evaluation of the drainage, materiality, masonry, fall protection, equipment, ACM, insulation, and structural integrity. New work may include redesign / reconstruction of support structures, drainage, roof type change, and parapet wall restoration to ensure water intrusion and legacy issues are mitigated. In addition to repairs and modifications, all interior drainage piping shall be replaced minimum 10 from roof drain unless, otherwise discussed with VA for convenience or practical reasons or as needed due to conditions of ease or degradation.
This requirement is being procured in accordance with the Brooks Act as implemented in FAR Subpart 36.6. Applicable NAICS code is 541330 and small business size standard of $25.5 Million. Magnitude of Construction is between $500,000 and $1,000,000. This is a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Set Aside. The anticipated award date of the proposed A-E Contract is on or before December 30, 2026. Potential contractors must be registered in SAM (www.sam.gov ) and are visible/verified/certified as SDVOSB in Dynamic Small Business Search (https://dsbs.sba.gov/search/dsp_dsbs.cfm) at time of submission of their qualifications in order to be considered for an award.

Any consultant/subcontractor or otherwise business entity(s) used must be identified by name, office location and size/type of business (i.e., SDVOSB, VOSB, 8(a), small, large, etc.). Failure to provide this information will deem the firm s SF 330 submittal as non-responsive and preclude further evaluation
All A/E firms are advised that in accordance with VAAR 836.606-71 the total cost of the production and delivery of designs, plans, drawings and specifications shall not exceed six (6) percent of the estimate cost of construction. Other A-E fees are not included in the six (6) percent. Additionally, FAR Clause 52.236-22 (c) - Design Within Funding Limitation, will be applicable to this procurement action.

Project no. 528A5-27-503: A/E Design Replace Flat Roof

Canandaigua VAMC, 400 Fort Hill Avenue Canandaigua, NY 14424

This acquisition will be in accordance with FAR Part 36.602-1 and VAAR Part 836.602-1. The following evaluation criteria will be used to evaluate SF-330 technical proposals:
The A/E must demonstrate its qualifications with respect to the published evaluation criteria for all services. description_text:
This Request for Information (RFI) is issued in accordance with FAR Part 10 to conduct market research. The Government's purpose is planning only; this notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP)/Request for Quotation (RFQ) nor a promise to issue one in the future. The Government will not pay any costs for responding, and any submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future procurement. The Government is not seeking proposals or quotes at this time.
Scope of Interest / Functional Areas:
The Government is assessing the market¿s capability to provide comprehensive support under the following disciplines:
a. Audits for Medicare Parts A, B, D, and Medicaid medical record review and consultative services
b. Audits for Medicare Part C medical record review and consultative services
c. Evaluations and Inspections medical record review and consultative services
d. Expert consultant and witness services in support of the Office of Investigations and/or Office of Counsel to the Inspector General
A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is provided for industry feedback; requirements may change prior to any future solicitation.
Requested Information (do not submit proposals or quotes):
Please provide high level, non price specific information addressing the elements below. Do not include proprietary pricing, line item estimates, or any proposal/quote content.
Section 1: Corporate Capability & Experience
a. PWS Alignment: Demonstrate your organization's core capability to fulfill the functional areas outlined in the draft PWS.
b. Medical Review Experience: Outline your firm's high-level experience in conducting large-volume medical claims reviews for audits and evaluations and inspections; and support services for medical expert consultants and witnesses specifically across the following five domains (as referenced in the attached PWS):
1. Audit Medicare Parts A/B/D and Medicaid
2. Audit Medicare Part C
3. Evaluations and Inspections
4. Office of Investigations
5. Office of Counsel to the Inspector General
c. Geographic Reach: Describe your prior experience managing and executing nationwide or multi-jurisdictional medical claim reviews.
d. Capacity & Scalability: State your organization's maximum monthly claim review capacity, including your approach to scaling operations between normal workloads and surge conditions.
e Teaming & Subcontracting: Identify potential subcontracting partners or specialized vendors you would anticipate utilizing, including an estimated percentage breakdown of work performed by the prime contractor versus subcontractors.
Section 2: High-Level Technical Approach & Operations
a. High-Level Technical Methodology: Describe your conceptual approach to fulfilling the core tasks in PWS. Please limit this narrative to no more than 5 pages total, organized by the 5 PWS sections. Focus on your overarching claims review methodology, general sampling plan frameworks, documentation standards, and typical project timelines rather than a granular, step-by-step solution.
b. Quality & Accuracy Frameworks: Outline your corporate quality assurance processes, internal review protocols, and standard strategies used to reduce error rates and ensure consistency across large volumes.
b. Staffing & Key Qualifications: Provide a conceptual staffing structure or organizational chart. Identify the typical roles, credentials (e.g., MD, RN, CPC), and qualifications of the key personnel required to successfully support a PWS of this nature. Please identify whether these staff will need to be hired or if they are current employees/contractors. Also, indicate staffing availability for physicians with specialties (i.e. hospice, vascular surgeon, nephrologist, physical medicine and rehabilitation or physiatrists).
c. Risk & Mitigation: Identify the primary technical or operational challenges anticipated with a medical review scope of this size and outline your high-level mitigation strategies.
Section 3: Past Performance & Market Pricing
a. Relevant Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of similar Federal medical review contracts performed within the last five years. Also, provide up to three examples of similar Federal support services for medical expert consultants and witnesses within the last five years.
b. Performance Outcomes: Summarize the high-level outcomes of those past contracts, focusing on standard metrics such as timeliness, accuracy rates (including rate at which findings were overturned during the appeals process), and a history of successful audit findings.
c. Cost Drivers & Efficiencies: Provide a general overview of your commercial pricing structure and the primary cost drivers (e.g., specific labor categories, specialized technology/AI tools, administrative overhead). Highlight any built-in efficiencies or innovative workflows in your approach that typically yield cost savings for the government.
Section 4: Industry Feedback & PWS Refinement
a. Clarity & Feasibility Review: Identify any requirements, metrics, or tasks within the draft PWS that appear ambiguous, overly restrictive, or technologically infeasible based on current commercial market capabilities.
b. Recommendations for Improvement: Suggest specific enhancements, industry standard metrics, or structural changes to the PWS that would improve the clarity, feasibility, and competitiveness of the final solicitation.

Email responses by November 13, 2026, 12:00 PM Eastern Time to the Points of Contact below. Mark proprietary information clearly; the Government may use non proprietary information to refine its acquisition approach.

a. Contracting Officer: Shavonda Jamison ¿ Shavonda_Jamison@ibc.doi.gov
b. Contracting Specialist: Dorothy Royster ¿ Dorothy_Royster@ibc.doi.gov

agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE HEALTH AGENCY (DHA).DEFENSE HEALTH AGENCY
description_text:
Subject : Revenue Cycle Modernization & Innovation (RCMI) & Charge Description Master (CDM) Support Services to Defense Health Agency (DHA) Resources & Personnel Integration (R&PI), J-8 Financial Operations.
THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) OR A REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS (RFQ); IT IS STRICTLY A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI). NEITHER UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS NOR ANY OTHER KINDS OF OFFERS WILL BE CONSIDERED IN RESPONSE TO THIS RFI. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED PURSUANT TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT.
1.0 DISCLAIMER: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. Responses to this notice are not offers and will not be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. Responses to the RFI will not be returned. At this time, questions concerning the composition and requirements for a future RFP will not be entertained.
2.0 SUBJECT : The DHA R&PI, J8 Financial Operations is obtaining information for a potential non-personal services contract to provide administrative and technical execution services, as well as technical expertise, for the Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) activities, to include CDM optimization, enhancement, and operations, to support the DHA Electronic Health Record (EHR), Military Health System (MHS) GENESIS, and its itemized billing solution, RevX.
3.0 BACKGROUND: The DHA J-8 recognizes the need to enhance its RCM processes to ensure the efficient and effective management of healthcare finances within the MHS. Using the MHS GENESIS EHR as a catalyst, J-8 seeks to address several critical challenges within its RCM framework: Revenue Leakage and Inefficiencies, Compliance and Regulatory Risks, Data Accuracy and Integration, Patient Experience, Resource Utilization, Financial Transparency, Clean Audit Capability, and Technology and Innovation. In response to these challenges, DHA J-8 aims to launch the RCM Initiative to transform its RCM processes. The goal is to enhance workload capture, financial performance, compliance, patient satisfaction, and resource utilization while ensuring transparency and embracing innovative technologies within the MHS.
Industry practice is to document, and bill patient encounters based on an itemized list of charges. To ensure documented care in MHS GENESIS results in an all-inclusive itemized bill within RevX, numerous actions must occur throughout the revenue cycle process (assignment of Patient Identification Process (PIP), provider documentation, medical record coding, and patient billing). Administration staff must ensure the PIP providers completely document and select the proper patient orderable description of care provided. Medical record coders must properly code the care provided. Finally, Uniform Business Office (UBO) staff must properly generate a bill on established separate billing forms for professional charges and institutional charges.
The DHA supports and provides medical care for the Department of War, 9.4 million eligible beneficiaries through the $52 billion Defense Health Program (DHP), which includes contracted healthcare networks and Military Treatment Facilities (MTFs). The deployment of MHS GENESIS is complete and currently in a transition phase. While this major technology transformation has provided a significant set of enhanced revenue cycle and business management capabilities for the MHS, they have also brought new requirements to align with industry-leading practices and underscored underlying issues in the legacy environment. For the Government to fully realize the benefits of MHS GENESIS revenue cycle capabilities, these cross-functional challenges require an integrated approach to resolve.
The Government will direct the actual implementation and detailed tasks for the RCM Activity as the MHS lacks knowledgeable in-house staffing to execute these specific operations. Specific assistance is required to support the DHA Financial Operations, J-8 with capabilities for optimization of revenue cycle efforts to prioritize improvement opportunities, begin reducing work queue backlog in MHS GENESIS, increase clinical workload capture, increase total billed for Third Party Collections (TPC), identify and correct areas where revenue leakage may be occurring, improve enterprise knowledge of workload and revenue capture, and enhance MTF staffs' ability to manage their business and be audit-ready.
4.0 RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: Respondents should address the following in their response:
4.1 Organization Information:
a. Organization’s full legal name and Address
b. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), Cage Code, Tax Identification Number, and company structure (Corporation, LLC, partnership, joint venture, etc). Companies must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM, at www.sam.gov) to be considered as potential sources.
c. Small Business Designation certified by the Small Business Administration, if any.
d. Point of contact name, phone number, and email for individual with the authority and knowledge to clarify responses with Government representatives.
e.Information pertaining to the following:
Does your company participate in any Government-wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACS)?
Does your company have a Federal Support Schedule Contract?
Are you currently on General Services Administration (GSA) One Acquisition Solution for Integrated Services (OASIS) (Prime or Sub); and if so, which pool(s) does your company participate?
Does your company have a Cost Accounting Standards approved accounting system and are you immediately postured to perform cost reimbursement type contracts?
4.2 Company Capabilities Statement: The capability statements provided must include the following:
a. Your company’s program management plan and control policies that adhere to standard industry practices. Must demonstrate the ability to accurately track projects and ensure timely completion of projects. Must include a recruitment and retention strategy to confirm their capability to provide varying levels of support for the tasks listed below.
b. General information and technical background describing your firm’s experience within the last three to five years; specifically with contracts similar in scope, complexity, and size to meet the program objectives in accordance with the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks outlined below, to include subject matter expertise with Cerner/Oracle experience, data software developers, data analysis business process and workflow support, business support personnel, training, and risk mitigation.
c. Demonstrated working knowledge and experience in: RCM and Solution Owner, and CDM support in the context of MHS GENESIS optimization, enhancement, and ongoing operations; and support for Innovative Technology Design, Implementation, and Sustainment Support to enhance revenue cycle operations within the MHS GENESIS environment.
d. Sufficient information/details to determine how you fully meet the requirements as specified in the tasks listed from the Draft PWS provided below:
Possess and maintain tools for proper and compliant charge master input, including but not limited to government approved, fully vetted, and validated electronic CDM application.
An ability to utilize and pull from existing MHS data systems to populate the CDM.
Possess an expertise in CDM auditing to ensure defensible charges/prices.
Provide education regarding charge input and charge master related items to MHS Business Community personnel.
Advise the MHS on CDM policy and practices to ensure regulatory compliance.
Possess an understanding of medical record coding and how the CDM assists the medical record coders in accurately coding patient encounters.
Continuous update of CDM based on American Medical Association (AMA) quarterly releases and Current Procedural Terminology/Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (CPT/HCPCS) revisions.
Incorporate AMA/Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) code adds, modifications, and obsolete codes into the CDM.
Continue to support the on-going maintenance of annual updates from AMA code sets, and quarterly updates based on payer interpretations and changes to activate/inactivate CDM line items by site.
Conduct reviews of CPT/HCPCS cost-based prices as codes are added, deleted, or modified based on CMS annual and quarterly reports.
Include validation steps for existing, or unique, MHS code descriptions, revenue codes, surgical levels, clinical areas, and other Maintenance data components.
Support MHS-specific CDM modifications, additions, and deletions as requested by the DHA or MHS GENESIS client.
Continue to organize maintenance efforts by clinical specialty rather than facility to maintain efficiency regardless of the location of service while communicating CDM updates or modifications to clinical department leaders for validation.
Continue to develop/refine a supply item file to serve as the source file for all chargeable supply items.
Document and maintain maintenance and pricing guidelines in CDM standard operating procedure files and review/update inputs on a recurring basis.
Continue to evaluate, develop, and maintain the CHAMPUS Maximum Allowable Charge (CMAC) rate tables within the CDM based on annual Tricare data release and existing MHS rate structures; along with additional rate tables/prices scheduled required.
Continue calculation of regional cost-based pricing based on Military Treatment Facilities (MTF) historical data for all chargeable health care products and services.
Utilize MEPRS, CAPERS, DMLSS, and CMAC data sources to define cost-based and CMAC-based procedure pricing methodologies.
Analyze MTF localities at the Parent and Child facility level to construct proposed grouping methodologies based on geographic, workload, resource, or other consistencies to develop a defensible charge table structure.
Calculate standard rates (room, tiered surgical services, etc.) based on DoD costs incurred for delivering such services.
Communicate CDM pricing updates and decisions to billing department leaders for validation.
Maintain existing business process and methodology for 100 Character Descriptions for all active and obsolete codes, while updating list in line with all regulatory updates.
Create and maintain American Dental Association Current Dental Terminology code table and descriptions within the CDM as required.
5.0 SMALL BUSINESS SET ASIDE: The Government has determined this acquisition to be accomplished under the 8(a) program.
6.0 INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDING:
Submission: Please submit RFI response via email in a “.pdf” file type, to Ms. Jennifer Sikes at email address: Jennifer.m.sikes2.civ@health.mil and Ms. Courtney Chase at email address: courtney.f.chase.civ@health.mil. Please use the title in your email “RCM&CDM Support Services for R&PI, DHA J-8”.
Due Date: RFI response submission is due no later than 10AM on 16 November 2026.
Page Limit: Limit your total written response to 25 single-sided pages. The cover page and table of contents does not count towards the page limit. Beyond the 25-page limit, the Government may only review examples of media and graphic design, as requested above.
7.0 Tasks Listed in the Draft PWS
7.1 Revenue Cycle Management and Solution Owner Support:
7.1.1 The contractor shall provide Revenue Cycle Management and Solution Owner support in the context of MHS GENESIS optimization, enhancement, and ongoing operations. This support encompasses critical backend system maintenance and optimization for the full MHS GENESIS system platform. Required expertise with Oracle health EHR backend system configurations, existing and pending system capabilities. Key responsibilities include managing and resolving ticket queues through efficient triage and resolution processes, ensuring timely response to system issues and user concerns. The contractor will be responsible for the development and validation of workplans, training material and training courses of varying length of time and platforms which are essential for effective revenue cycle management within the MHS GENESIS environment, report generation in support of audit readiness, downgraded audit opinions pertaining to financial statements, and Medicare-Eligible Retiree Health Care Fund (MERHCF). Additionally, the contractor will provide a designated subset of the workforce to perform Author Query roles, to include writing, testing, modifying, and executing database queries, custom scripts, and data extractions utilizing Cerner Command Language and/or Structured Query Language within MHS GENESIS, RevX, and CDM systems.
7.1.1.1 A crucial aspect of this support will involve preparing the organization for potential transition to Oracle Health’s Patient Accounting (OHPA) or other identified patient accounting solution. This preparation includes assessing current processes, identifying gaps, and developing strategies to align DHA's revenue cycle operations with the new module's capabilities. Additional preparation includes full integration of business and clinical processes in support of successful end-to-end overall system health. The contractor shall provide expertise in troubleshooting, system configuration, process improvement, and change management to ensure smooth functionality of the full MHS GENESIS system platform from clinical, administrative, and business processes/practices, while simultaneously laying the groundwork for a seamless transition to OHPA or other identified patient accounting solution. This comprehensive support is vital for maintaining system integrity, enhancing user experience, optimizing current revenue cycle operations, and positioning DHA for future success with advanced patient accounting tools
7.2 Innovative Technology Design, Implementation and Sustainment Support:
7.2.1 The contractor shall leverage new and emerging technologies to streamline processes and significantly reduce human input errors that are currently impacting efficiency and accuracy. The contractor will be responsible for collaborating with DHA Functional Subject Matter Experts responsible for specific areas of the revenue cycle to identify, in some cases design of solution, and implement cutting-edge technological solutions that can automate repetitive tasks, improve data accuracy, and enhance overall system performance. This may include AI and machine learning algorithms for predictive analytics, RPA for routine tasks, or advanced data validation tools. To accomplish the design, development, and implementation of AI and RPA solutions, the contractor is required to procure and maintain the necessary specialized platforms and licenses. The contractor will also provide ongoing sustainment support to ensure the long-term viability and effectiveness of these innovative solutions.
7.3. CDM Support:
7.3.1 The contractor shall provide CDM support for MHS GENESIS optimization, enhancement, and ongoing operations. The support requires updating associated charge tables based on geographic location, hospital vs. clinic, and patient category. The contractor shall also coordinate with Cerner/Oracle Health (the contractor that deployed the full MHS GENESIS EHR platform) to ensure proper integration with the Cerner Charge Services Pricing Tool (Charge Services Servers). Additionally, the contractor shall provide overall Program Management Support for ongoing CDM operations.

description_text:
NAVAL SURFACE WARFARE CENTER DAHLGREN DIVISION
ADVANCE NOTICE / SOURCES SOUGHT
A DEPT INFRASTRUCTURE, LIBRARY AND SYSTEMS ADMINISTRATION SUPPORT
N0017827R3002
Summary of Requirement:
The Naval Surface Warfare Center Dahlgren Division (NSWCDD) is an engineering, software development, and systems test and integration center for Research, Development, Test & Evaluation (RDT&E) components of the United States (U.S.) Navy. The Strategic and Computing Systems Department (A Department) provides system administration, networking and Integrated Logistics Support (ILS), infrastructure, library support services, systems engineering, software development and test and evaluation capabilities to various program offices and projects. The various commands include, but are not limited to, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Marine Corps System Command (MARCORSYSCOM), Strategic Systems Programs (SSP), and Joint Cyber Command & Control (JCC2).
Projects include weapons control systems and warfare systems, notably, Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile (SLBM), Ship Submersible Ballistic Nuclear (SSBN), Submersible Ship Guided Nuclear (SSGN), Strategic Weapons System (SWS), Submarine Launched Cruise Missile - Nuclear (SLCM-N), Tomahawk Weapons System (TWS), Tactical Tomahawk Weapon Control System (TTWCS), Aegis (both land- and sea-based), the Ship Self-Defense System (SSDS), United States Coast Guard Cutters, DDG-1000 Guided Missile Destroyers, Combined Integrated Air and Missile Defense Anti-Submarine Warfare Trainer (CIAT), Guided Missile Frigate (FFG(X)) ships, other tactical Navy and Marine Corps programs, and cyberspace programs including the Mission Assurance Decision Support System (MADSS).
The overall focus of the NSWCDD A Department has grown and changed over time to broaden its scope to include any weapons system/weapons control system programs, combat systems, and other complex engineering systems. As such, A Department requires versatile and in-depth system administration and Integrated Logistics Support (ILS), infrastructure, library and support services throughout each of its organizational units with extensive experience in all aspects explained in this Statement of Work (SOW).
Work Locations and Full Time Equivalents (FTEs):
It is anticipated a total of 206 FTEs will be needed (excluding Surge SLINs) under the Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) Contract Line Item No. (CLINs): 34 FTEs for the Base Year (BY), 41 FTEs for Option Year (OY) one (1), 41 FTEs for OY two (2), 43 FTEs for OY three (3), and 47 FTEs for OY four (4); and 210 FTEs under the Fixed-Price (FP) CLIN: 38 FTEs for the BY, 40 for OY one (1), 44 for OY two (2), 45 for OY three (3), and 45 for OY four (4).
ATTACHMENTS: FULL ADVANCED NOTICE, A DRAFT STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW), DRAFT LABOR QUALIFICATIONS and QUAD CHART TEMPLATE ARE ATTACHED TO THIS NOTICE.
Contract Type & Period of Performance:
The Government contemplates award of a hybrid Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) and CPFF Task Order. The resultant order will have a Base Period of twelve months, and four (4) Option Periods each consisting of twelve months each, for a total of 60 months, if all Options are exercised.
Set-Aside:
At this time, a determination has NOT been made to set-aside this procurement. Responses to this Sources Sought will be evaluated and used to determine the set-aside status of this requirement.
Incumbent:
This follow-on work consolidates CPFF Task Order N0017819D8647/N0017821F3003 (Tatitlek Technologies, Inc., 561 East 36th Ave. Anchorage, AK 99503) and CPFF Task Order N0017819D8413/N0017821F3013 (Resource Management Concepts, 46970 Bradley Blvd, Suite B Lexington Park, MD).
Personnel and Facility Clearance Requirements:
Contractors shall meet the following mandatory requirements at the time of proposal submission or have an acceptable plan to meet the requirements by the start date of contract performance. In addition, mandatory requirements must be maintained throughout the life of the Task Order. The mandatory requirements are as follows:
Facility Clearance Level (FCL) Requirement: The Prime Contractor supporting this Task Order is required to have an FCL of TOP SECRET and safeguarding clearance level of SECRET at the primary facility supporting this Task Order.
Personnel Clearance Level (PCL) Requirement: All personnel directly supporting this Task Order, except Management and Support personnel, are required to have, as a minimum, a current SECRET security clearance in the Defense Industrial Security System (DISS). Interim clearances are acceptable. Personnel performing in the following labor categories shall have a final TOP SECRET security clearance in DISS:
Library Specialist (1 FTE)
SR Systems Administrator (6 FTEs)
Systems Administrator (3 FTEs)
Senior Network Administrator (1 FTE)
Network Administrator (4 FTEs).
Facilities Operations Technician (1 FTE)
Request for Capability Statements
A set-aside determination has not yet been made for this requirement. Interested SeaPort-NxG Small Businesses are invited to submit capability statements. Capability statements shall not exceed 15 pages, not including resume summaries, with font size 10 or greater. The Capability statements shall describe their ability to fulfill all or portions of this requirement. A set-aside decision or decisions will be announced when the solicitation is released. Capability statements shall include the following items:
(1) Sources Sought announcement number (for which the response is being submitted) and a description of the Offeror's capabilities relating to the attached draft Statement of Work (SOW). The description shall specifically address relevant experience and understanding of each work area for which this acquisition will support, and it shall address the Offeror's ability to meet each of the mandatory requirements.
(2) A company profile including the DUNS number and a statement regarding current Small Business status (including all applicable categories of Small Business: Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, HUBzone, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business, Economically Disadvantaged Woman Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business or Small Disadvantaged Business)
(3) The specific qualifications, capabilities, experience, and personnel security clearance level of all personnel the Contractor intends to utilize to support this effort. Identify whether individuals are employees of the Offeror, are contingent hires, or are employees of a planned team member (Sub-contractor). If employees are those of a planned team member, the name of the Sub-contractor shall also be identified.
(4) A description of the Offeror's ability to meet each of the Personnel and Facility Clearance requirements in SOW Section C.8.1 by time of award.
(5) Specific past performance on same or similar size and scope of work performed by the Offeror as a prime Contractor under a Government contract within the past five (5) years, including a description of the services provided, the dollar value of the effort, and the contract number.
(6) Provisions for any potential “similarly situated entity” arrangements being considered. A “similarly situated entity” means a first-tier Sub-contractor, including an independent Contractor, that has the same small business program status as that which qualified the prime Contractor for the award and that is considered small for the NAICS code the Prime Contractor assigned to the subcontract the Sub-contractor will perform. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count toward the 50 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded.

Industry Day
The NSWCDD Industry Day is scheduled for November 9, 2026, at the University of Mary Washington Dahlgren Campus (4224 University Drive, King George, VA 22485), with sign-in beginning at 08:00 AM and the briefing starting at 08:30 AM. Following the main presentation, NSWCDD will host optional, in-person, one-on-one sessions from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM; virtual sessions will not be offered. Interested parties must request a session during their initial Industry Day registration request, which must be submitted before the firm deadline of 5:00 PM EST on November 5, 2026. No requests for the one-on-one session will be accepted after the deadline of 5:00 PM EST on November 5, 2026. Please note that details are subject to change, and if one-on-one requests exceed afternoon capacity on November 9, 2026, NSWCDD will coordinate an alternate date to accommodate the overflow.
This notice is issued for informational and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. The Government is not requesting proposals at this time. Participation in the Industry Day is voluntary and is not required to compete for any future solicitation.
One-on-One Session Parameters & Conduct:
Purpose: The primary purpose of these sessions is for the government to receive information about a contractor's capabilities related to the DRAFT Statement of Work (SOW) attached to the Advance Notice/Sources Sought. While government personnel may ask clarifying questions during the session, they will not solicit formal proposals or ask for follow-up information that could be construed as a pre-solicitation.
Session Length: 15 to 20 minutes per company (final duration pending total registration numbers). To ensure equity, all sessions will be of equal length.
Industry Delegation: Limited to a maximum of two (2) representatives per company.
Government Attendance: A minimum of two representatives (Subject Matter Experts and/or Program representatives) along with the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) and/or Contracts Department representatives.
Official Setting: All sessions will take place exclusively in the designated meeting room. Meetings at other locations are strictly prohibited.
Security Classification: Unclassified. No classified discussions permitted.
Impartiality: Government personnel will remain strictly impartial and will not offer advice, assistance, or opinions that could be interpreted as a commitment or endorsement.
Registration & Scheduling Instructions:
Interested parties must submit their registration request via email no later than 5:00 PM EST on November 5, 2026. Confirmation and scheduling slots will be emailed at least 24 hours prior to the event.

title: FDA/CDRH Scientific Technical Capacity for Regulatory Review
agency: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION.FDA OFFICE OF ACQ  GRANT SVCS
description_text:
This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only . This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes – it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ) or a promise to issue an RFQ in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, if issued. The purpose of this SSN is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors, including large business sources, small business sources and their size classifications (i.e., HUBZone 8(a), 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned Small Business, and Small Disadvantaged Business) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code.
Responses to this SSN will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources.
Project Title: FDA/CDRH Scientific Technical Capacity for Regulatory Review
Background: To assist the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) in fulfilling its mission, CDRH seeks expert consultants to assist CDRH’s Offices with regulatory review across the total product lifecycle. CDRH requires consultants that have skilled experience to assist with medical device regulatory review work and supporting scientific activities, such as research, cybersecurity and digital health consultations, regulatory consultations and auditing, and interacting with industry and patients. The CDRH requires consultants that have sufficient skilled capacity in many science, engineering, and clinical specialties, including Anesthesiology, Biology, Biomedical Engineering, Chemistry, Clinical laboratory testing, Computer Science and Engineering, Consumer Safety, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Dentistry, Digital Health, Epidemiology, Gastroenterology, General Engineering, Health Science, Infectious Diseases, Interdisciplinary Engineer/Scientist, Molecular testing, Neurology, Optics, Patient Engagement, Physics, Psychiatry, Public Health, Pulmonology, Reprocessing medical devices, Social Scientist, Software Engineering, Statistics and Biostatistics, Sterilization, Toxicology, Urology, Veterinary Medicine, and Virology.
Objective: The primary objective of this effort is to provide the CDRH with a vehicle to acquire the support services of advanced professional and scientific consultants to assist CDRH’s Offices with regulatory review across the total product lifecycle, including the supporting scientific, engineering, clinical, and regulatory activities. The services provided will be critical scientific expertise and capacity in support for the evaluation of the continued performance, safety, and effectiveness, with respect to devices approved, cleared, licensed, or authorized for use for the treatment, prevention, or diagnosis of medical conditions by the FDA.
Instructions for Responses to this SSN: Your responses to the questions provided below will assist the Government in selecting the appropriate acquisition method. Page limit: Maximum 15 pages (font size Times New Roman 11 or larger). In addition to responses to the below questions, each vendor responding to this SSN shall also fill out and provide responses to “ Attachment B-Vendor Feedback Form .” The Vendor Feedback Form is not included in the 15-page limit. A copy of the company capability statement will also be accepted (but not in place of the responses to the below questions or the Vendor Feedback Form). The anticipated period of performance consists of one (1) Base Year and four (4) Option Years. Responses to this SSN must include company name, address, point of contact, size of business pursuant to the NAICS code, and must respond to the following questions:
Is your business a small business under the NAICS code?
Does your firm qualify as a Small Disadvantaged Business?
If disadvantaged, specify if your firm is certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act?
Are you considered a certified HUBZone firm?
Are you considered Woman-Owned or operated business?
Are you a certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned or Veteran-Owned business?
Included is a draft Statement of Work that is inclusive of the anticipated Task Areas (“Attachment A-Draft Statement of Work”).
All interested parties can provide written opinions/questions on the draft Statement of Work.
All opinions/questions expressed should focus on strengthening the draft Statement of Work Tasks to ensure industry understands and comprehends the government’s requirements.
Responses to this SSN shall be submitted via e-mail to Melinda Kim, Contract Specialist, at Melinda.Kim@fda.hhs.gov , (with a CC: to Nicholas Bisher, Contracting Officer, at Nicholas.Bisher@fda.hhs.gov ), by 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on November 17, 2026 . The subject line of the e-mail shall reference, “ Vendor Response to SSN 75F40127Q00006 .”
After a review of the received responses, a formal solicitation may be published on SAM.gov or on GSA eBuy. No solicitation is currently available. This is not a request for quotation and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. Responses to this SSN will not be considered adequate responses to the solicitation, a request to be added to a prospective offerors list, or a request to receive a copy of the solicitation.

title: C221--402-27-001 Repair Chiller 3 (AE)
agency: VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.241-NETWORK CONTRACT OFFICE 01 (36C241)
description_text:
Introduction
Network Contracting Office 1 (NCO 1), supporting VA New England Healthcare System (VISN 1), is seeking potential sources for an upcoming requirement for Architect and Engineering Services as described in the attached statement of work. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATION STATEMENTS (SF330). This notice is a market research tool and has not been set-aside for any small business category, but the notice is issued to determine appropriate set-aside categories. Responses to this notice, in conjunction with other Government market research resources, will be used by the contracting officer to determine the applicable socio-economic set-aside for the procurement.
Failure to respond to this notice will not impact consideration of architect and engineer firms (or joint ventures) which otherwise meet set-aside requirements and submit responses to the follow-up public announcement. Once the appropriate set-aside is determined, a separate public announcement requesting qualification statements (SF330s) will be publicized on Contract Opportunities in accordance with 40 U.S. Code Â§ 1101 and FAR 36.102.
General Project Description and NAICS
Synopsis of required services (See attachment for full statement of work): provide Architect/Engineer (AE) services to evaluate existing conditions, propose corrective measures, and design a construction project at the VA Maine Health Care System (Togus) in accordance with this scope of work. Scope will include Type A services only with design complete to 35%.
AE Part I Investigative Services/Schematic Design/Other Related Services shall include site visits, field investigation, studies and user interviews to prepare drawings, and cost estimates for all facets of work and disciplines/trades to repair Chiller 3 to a condition where it will operate as designed. Design should also include fixes for the reported cooling and oil leaks.
This procurement for Architect & Engineering services is assigned NAICS 541330 Engineering Services which has a SBA size standard of $22.5 million in average revenue.
Information Sought
The Government requests a letter of interest (or similar document) with responses to the following:
1. State your firm name (as it appears in SAM.gov), Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, and socio-economic status of the firm (i.e. verified SDVOSB, WOSB, SB, large business).
2. Provide a brief narrative on the firm s experience, providing services similar to those described in the attached statement of work.
3. What would be the expected make-up of the firm s team in terms of socio-economic categories and estimated percentage of work to be completed by your firm and each subcontractor?
If the procurement is set-aside for any category of small business, generally fifty percent of more of the work would need to be performed by the contractor or a similarly situated subcontractor in terms of percentage of cost. For instance, if set-aside for service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB), 50% or more of the contract would need to be performed by verified SDVOSBs no other small business categories would count towards the percentage. If set-aside for small business, 50% of the contract would be required to be performed by small businesses which would include performance by a verified SDVOSB because they are also a small business. If the procurement is not set-aside and reaches certain dollar thresholds, the Government would negotiate an acceptable subcontracting plan to utilize small business concerns.
4. A brief statement of overall interest in the project and capability of performing the work in conjunction with ongoing projects.
5. Any additional capabilities statements or other documentation that you feel will assist the Government in performing market research and determining the appropriate set-aside.
Submission Instructions
Interested parties are requested to submit the requested information not later than November 20, 2026, to Diane C. Davis via email to diane.davis2@va.gov. Please include 36C24127R0009 Sources Sought Response in the title of the email. the response burden to this notice is expected to be light; lengthy responses are not expected but no maximum page count is assigned. Please keep responses below 7MB or send multiple emails appending to the email subject 1 of n as appropriate. Please contact Diane Davis at the email address above with any questions.

title: USSS Construction Management & Engineering Services
agency: HOMELAND SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF.US SECRET SERVICE.U S SECRET SERVICE
description_text:
Request for Information
Construction Management Services
NAICS Code 541330, Engineering Services
Notice Type: Request for Information (RFI)
Agency: U.S. Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Secret Service (USSS)
Response Due Date: November 20, 2026
Point of Contact: Kimberly Johnson, Contracting Officer, Assistant Division Chief, Office of Procurement 1. Purpose
The U.S. Secret Service is conducting market research to identify qualified construction management firms capable of supporting future construction, renovation, design-management, and related task-order requirements. This Request for Information is issued solely for planning and market research purposes.
USSS is seeking information from firms operating under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 541330, Engineering Services , including small businesses and socioeconomic small-business concerns, that possess the organizational capacity, technical expertise, security capability, and geographic reach necessary to support future construction activities.
Responses to this RFI will assist USSS in assessing industry capability, the availability of qualified firms, small-business participation, competition, bonding capacity, staffing resources, geographic coverage, and potential acquisition approaches for a future BPA or IDIQ type contract with the USSS.
This RFI is not a solicitation, request for proposal, commitment, or promise by the Government to award a contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response.
2. Anticipated Requirement Description
The U.S. Secret Service (USSS) anticipates a nationwide requirement for construction management and related design, engineering, security, infrastructure, and maintenance services at Government-owned or leased facilities and other Government-designated locations throughout the United States and its territories. Work may include new construction, renovations, retrofits, system upgrades, emergency repairs, and sustainment activities performed in occupied, operational, secure, or time-sensitive environments.
Depending on the task order, firms may be required to provide services across the full project lifecycle, including:
Planning, requirements development, site surveys, existing-condition assessments, project scoping, and cost estimating.
Architectural and engineering design management, design review, value engineering, constructability review, and preparation of procurement-ready design documents.
Acquisition and preconstruction support, including bid evaluation and contractor-vetting assistance.
Construction administration and management, including quality control, safety and schedule oversight, stakeholder coordination, phased work, and management of design changes.
Equipment procurement, fabrication, installation, systems integration, testing, commissioning, documentation, training, maintenance, repair, and urgent-response support, as specified in individual task orders.
Anticipated task orders may cover one or more of the following service areas:
Physical security enhancements: Perimeter controls, security booths and command posts, vehicle and pedestrian access points, site improvements, structural hardening, ballistic or blast-resistant features, secure rooms, doors, gates, locks, and related protective measures.
Electronic security systems: Video surveillance and management, intrusion detection, access control, command-and-control, intercom and notification systems, supporting networks and equipment, system programming, cybersecurity hardening, integration, testing, and operator training.
Infrastructure and building systems: Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, communications, emergency power, structured and fiber-optic cabling, fire and life-safety systems, HVAC, environmental controls, and building-management or monitoring platforms needed to support security and mission continuity.
Preventive and corrective maintenance: Inspection, testing, calibration, software and firmware maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, component replacement, emergency response, spare-parts support, lifecycle assessment, and documentation for covered systems and infrastructure.
The scope is broad and non-exhaustive. Each task order may establish the applicable locations, technical requirements, deliverables, performance standards, schedule, security restrictions, acceptance criteria, and maintenance obligations. Firms may need to integrate new, existing, legacy, or proprietary systems while minimizing disruption and maintaining safety, security, and continuity of operations.
The Government anticipates that some future requirements may involve concurrent task orders of significant value. Respondents should identify their capacity to manage multiple projects simultaneously, including their ability to provide appropriately cleared personnel when required.
3. Industry Information Requested
Interested firms are requested to complete and submit the attached Interested Vendor Questionnaire, U.S. Secret Service Construction Management Services, Request for Information , along with the supporting information identified below.
4. Submission Requirements
Interested firms should submit the following:
A completed Interested Vendor Questionnaire .
A capability statement of no more than three pages .
Information for up to three relevant completed projects from the past three years.
Supporting project documentation, as available.
Evidence of SAM.gov registration and applicable socioeconomic certifications, if requested or applicable.
Responses should be submitted electronically in searchable PDF format to Kimberly Johnson, email: kimberly.m.johnson@usss.dhs.gov no later than November 20, 2026, 4:00 pm Eastern Standard time . The email subject line should read:
RFI Response: USSS Construction Management Services – [Company Name]
5. Additional Information
Respondents are encouraged to identify any recommended acquisition, contract-structure, ordering, scope-management, or small-business participation considerations that may help USSS develop a future requirement.
