description_text:
THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT.
This Sources Sought Synopsis is being used as a market research tool to determine the availability and adequacy of potential qualified small business sources prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation for architect-engineer services. All Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (VOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Businesses (EDWOSB), Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSB), Small Disadvantaged Businesses (SDB) certified under the Small Business Administration’s (SBA’s) 8(a) Business Development Program, Historically Underutilized Business Zone Small Businesses (HUBZone SB) certified by SBA, and all other small businesses are encouraged to respond. If you are a HUBZone or an 8(a) Small Business, please submit the SBA Certification Letter or contact information for assigned SBA Business Development Specialist.
Responses to this notice will determine the feasibility and/or basis for the Navy’s decision to proceed with an acquisition. Information received in relation to this notice will be used to assist the Government in developing an overall acquisition strategy, including the type and number of contracts and use of small business concerns.
The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this synopsis.
Large business submittals will not be considered.
NAVFAC Atlantic is seeking to identify potential sources with the capacity, experience and interest in competing for a contract for a Single Award Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Architect-engineering (A/E) Contract for Environmental Planning and Engineering Services of an interdisciplinary nature for the implementation of National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), Executive Order (EO) 12114, Environmental Effects Abroad of Major Federal Actions –Ship Homeporting and Related Operational Issues.
The principal geographic area covered by this contract encompasses NAVFAC Atlantic's AOR, NAVFAC Pacific’s AOR and the adjacent waters of the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, including the Continental United States, the Caribbean, Europe, and North Africa. Additionally, tasks associated with this contract may be assigned anywhere in the world.
The NAICS code for this proposed procurement is 541330 (small business size standard is $25.5 million). If the solicitation is issued, the solicitation will consist of a base period and four (4) one-year options totaling five (5) years of performance. The anticipated total work to be issued over the life of the contract via task orders (base year plus four one-year options) shall not exceed the estimated maximum amount of $75 million.
The successful contractor to any forthcoming solicitation shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, materials, and all equipment necessary to perform the services listed below. The preponderance of the work under this contract shall involve the accomplishment of work in the following major categories, including but not limited to:
The general scope of this contract requires engineering services, biological science, physical science, cultural resource, community planning, and military operations specialists. The engineers and community planners providing services under this contract must have competence attested by a licensor as a professional engineer or certified planner. The services required from the A-E firm or joint venture include, but are not limited to, architectural-engineering (A-E) or environmental services for the preparation of environmental planning documentation such as categorical exclusions (CATEX), environmental assessments (EAs), and environmental impact statements (EISs) under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), environmental consultations and permits, as well as environmental reviews and environmental studies under EO 12114. The preponderance of the work under this contract shall be the preparation of various documents to support the proposed infrastructure-related actions with respect to ship homeporting issues. Examples of taskings required to complete this work may include analysis of port facility and infrastructure construction, renovation, and/or demolition; dredging; base realignment and closure (BRAC) actions; and proposed operational actions related to ship homeporting, waterfront activities and manned and unmanned asset activities. The contractor shall use the most up to date guidelines for preparation of the NEPA documentation. This includes Navy Instructions and the current version of the OPNAV 5090.1, Environmental Readiness Program, Marine Corps Instructions and the most current version of the P509.2, DoD Instruction 4715.11/12, and Department of War NEPA Implementing Procedures.
Additionally, other tasks, studies, surveys, or documents may be required to complete the environmental planning documents including, but not limited to, environmental documentation for ship readiness and testing and training operations at the homeport locations and within Department of Defense-managed seaspace and Navy/Marine Corps training ranges, sketches, preliminary plans, cost estimates, descriptive text for future planning and work plans, modeling, geospatial analysis, information technology applications, traffics modeling and analysis, air quality modeling and analysis, noise modeling and analysis, encroachment analysis, and development and reproduction of a variety of public outreach materials of different media. For major testing and training exercises, the contractor shall be tasked with estimating marine mammal exposure from ordnance and sonar activities.
In order to complete environmental planning documents in compliance with NEPA and EO 12114 and 12898, and in accordance with applicable DOD instructions, the contractor may be required to complete some of the following related studies and services to provide a comprehensive evaluation of the impacts to the environment:
Air Conformity modeling and analyses under the Clean Air Act

Air quality management plans
Coastal Consistency Determinations in accordance with the Coastal Zone Management Act
Draft Letters of Authorization (LOA) and Incidental Harassment Authorization (IHA) applications
Endangered Species Act Section 7 consultations, biological surveys, and Biological Assessments
Essential Fish Habitat assessments
In-water acoustic analysis
Marine Mammal Density estimates
Marine Resource Assessments
Natural Resources surveys (species and habitat)
Wetland delineation and mitigation plans (both wetland and near shore)
National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) and American Indian Tribe consultation support including cultural resource surveys (both architectural and archaeological), records management, and archaeological collection management/support
Environmental permitting support
Mitigation planning and support
Socioeconomic analysis including Community Impact Studies and Environmental Justice
Analyses
Noise impact studies/modeling/monitoring (land and in-water)
Noise analysis and the use of military aviation simulation model (NASMOD)
Military Base Development Requirements to include Encroachment Action Plans for shore installations and at-sea operations and facility requirements analyses
Range analysis to include documentation in support of Range Sustainability Environmental Program Assessments (RSEPA), Water RSEPA, Operational Range Clearance (ORC), Range Condition management Plans (RCMPs)
Range containment modeling
Fate and transport modeling and analysis
Soil, sediment and water sampling
Water quality studies to include chemical and physical analysis of dredge material and bioassays
Toxic and hazardous waste studies (including Military Expended Materials)
Health risk and toxicology analysis
Storm Water Management studies
Total Ownership Cost (TOC) or life cycle cost analysis
Climate change and resiliency studies
Greenhouse gas accounting and analysis
Glint and glare modeling and analysis
Hydrology and erosion studies
Construction feasibility studies including slope, terrain, soils, watersheds, and seismic hazards
Renewable energy feasibility studies
Utility capability assessments and feasibility studies (electric, gas, sewer, and water) to support design plans
Air Installation Compatibility Use Zone (AICUZ) studies
Range Air Installation Compatibility Use Zone (RAICUZ) studies
Safety analyses (Surface Danger Zones, Impact Zones, Accident Potential Zones, Clear Zones, and Danger Zones)
Integrated Natural Resource Management Plans (INRMPs) and INRMP updates
Integrated Cultural Resource Management Plans (ICRMPs) and ICRMP updates
Modeling to determine tidal or sea-level rise impacts to shore lines and structures
Geospatial analysis and map generation in accordance with current guidance
Estimates of dredge and fill sediment volumes
Hazardous waste reporting and analysis (i.e. EPCRA)
Land Use Compatibility plans
Development of water and air quality management requirements
Construction design plans
Traffic and transportation analysis, studies, and roadway designs
Public involvement and outreach support
Public participation planning and implementation
Translation services for CATEX/EA/EIS and Public Notices
Environmental Condition of Property (ECP)
Literature reviews
Watershed planning
Installation master plans
The contract requires the selected firm to have online access to e-mail via the Internet for routine exchange of correspondence.
Statement of Capabilities Submittal Requirements: The Statement of Capability (SOC) will determine the feasibility and/or basis for the Navy’s decision to proceed with acquisition. title: Request for Information (RFI) for Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Protection (JPM CBRN P)  Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS)
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.AMC.ACC.ACC-CTRS.ACC-APG.W6QK ACC-APG NATICK
description_text:
This is a request for information (RFI) only for capabilities and experience which show potential for meeting the requirements described below. This is not a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP) or an Invitation for Bid (IFB). It is a market research tool being used to determine the availability and adequacy of potential sources for planning purposes only. Responses to this notice are not considered as offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of responses nor otherwise pay for the preparation of any information presented or the use of any such information.
1. Purpose
The Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Protection (JPM CBRN P) is conducting a market survey to identify industry capabilities, experience, and potential approaches for serving as a Product Support Integrator (PSI) and material integration support for the Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS) Reconfiguration and Technology Refresh effort.
The Government seeks a commercial partner capable of procuring and coordinating the delivery of commercially available components; receiving, tracking, and consolidating Government-sourced components; applying Item Unique Identification (IUID) markings as required; maintaining materiel accountability and readiness; conducting Preventative Maintenance, Checks and Services (PMCS) and Care of Supply in Storage (COSIS) as necessary, and delivering verified, complete component packages to Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA) for final system integration, build completion, and packaging.
This RFI is issued solely for planning and market-research purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, commitment by the Government, or authorization to incur costs. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response.
2. Background
CP DEPMEDS is a fielded CBRN protection system that supports Army Role 3 field-hospital operations. The program is executing a reconfiguration and technology-refresh effort using fielded, previously qualified, and commercially available components.
The revised support concept under consideration would use a commercial PSI to integrate component procurement, Government-furnished or Government-sourced materiel coordination, traceability, IUID marking, and delivery to Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA). PBA would retain responsibility for final assembly/integration of CP DEPMEDS sets, final packaging, associated Government acceptance activities, and delivery of sets to their fielding/final destination.
3. Scope of Information Requested
The Government seeks information on industry capability to perform the following functions:
A. Commercial Component Procurement
Procure commercially available components identified by the Government.
Conduct vendor management and order placement of components.
Identify long-lead items, supply-chain constraints, discontinuance risks, and proposed alternate sources.
Provide proposed substitutes only when specifically authorized by the Government.
Manage warranties, vendor documentation, certificates of conformance, and commercial shipping documentation as applicable.
B. Government Component Coordination
Coordinate receipt, transfer, and consolidation of Government-sourced components from designated Government organizations, depots, supply activities, or other locations.
Maintain accountability for Government-provided or Government-directed materiel while in contractor custody.
Maintain COSIS to prevent environmental degradation, corrosion, and shelf life expiration of stored equipment and supplies.
Reconcile shipping discrepancies, damaged materiel, shortages, overages, and documentation issues.
Maintain traceability between each component, its source, and its assigned CP DEPMEDS configuration or set.
Note: The contractor would not independently obligate Government funds or direct Government supply activities. The Government would retain authority for requisitions, funding, release, acceptance, and disposition decisions.
C. IUID and Asset Identification
Apply, validate, and document IUID markings for designated end items and components in accordance with Government-furnished requirements and applicable standards.
Verify marking quality, placement, readability, and association with the correct item record.
Maintain item-level records linking serial number, part number, National Stock Number, Unique Item Identifier, source, and destination.
Provide electronic IUID and asset-accountability data deliverables in a Government-specified format.
D. Materiel Receiving, Inspection, and Staging
Receive and inspect commercial and Government-sourced components.
Verify quantities, part numbers, serial numbers, condition, shelf life, and required documentation.
Store and stage components in a manner that preserves condition, supports shelf-life management, and enables rapid consolidation into required delivery packages.
Maintain COSIS to prevent environmental degradation, corrosion, and shelf life expiration of stored equipment and supplies.
E. Kit Completion and Delivery to PBA
Build component-level shipping packages in accordance with Government-approved bills of material, configuration lists, and delivery priorities.
Conduct kit-completeness checks before shipment.
Package, preserve, mark, and ship components to PBA in accordance with Government-approved shipping instructions.
Provide advance-shipment notifications, packing lists, serial-number/IUID records, and discrepancy reports.
If required, travel to PBA to help support the delivery and inventory of shipped equipment.
F. Program Management and Reporting
Maintain an integrated procurement and delivery schedule.
Provide recurring status reports addressing procurement status, component availability, shortages, long-lead risks, delivery forecasts, IUID status, kit completion, and shipment status.
Identify risks early and recommend mitigation actions, including alternate vendors, phased deliveries, or proposed substitutes.
Participate in Government-led integrated product team meetings as required.
4. Desired Capabilities
Respondents should describe experience performing comparable work involving:
Multi-vendor procurement and materiel integration;
Government-furnished property or Government-directed materiel;
IUID marking, validation, and data management;
Military logistics, asset accountability, and shipping documentation;
Kitting, staging, packaging, preservation, and shipment of complex equipment;
Supply-chain risk management and long-lead-item mitigation;
CBRN, deployable medical, field-hospital, shelter, or comparable expeditionary equipment. (Note: This is desired experience but not required for response.)
The Government is particularly interested in respondents able to manage multiple sources of supply and coordinate delivery of components to a Government integration location.
5. Industry Response Instructions
Responses should not exceed [15] pages, excluding attachments. Include:
Company Information: Name, UEI, CAGE code, business size, socioeconomic status, and points of contact.
Relevant Experience: Up to three relevant efforts performed within the past five years.
Technical Approach: Notional approach to commercial procurement, Government-component coordination, IUID, accountability, staging, kit verification, and delivery to PBA.
Facilities and Workforce: Relevant facilities, quality systems, logistics staff, IUID capability, and geographic support model.
Data and Reporting: Proposed methods for inventory visibility, serialized-item traceability, IUID data delivery, and Government status reporting.
Risk Management: Principal risks, including vendor lead time, part obsolescence, Government materiel availability, configuration changes, and transportation delays.
Rough-Order-of-Magnitude: Estimated startup period, staffing approach, major cost drivers, and recommended contract structure.
The Government requests that responses be submitted electronically to melissa.b.smith23.civ@army.mil, and veronica.a.stclaire.civ@army.mil. The email title should read “CP DEPMEDS Integrator RFI Response - [Vendor Name]”.
Responses shall be received NLT COB 28 November 2026.

For purposes of this effort, the Developer would be a non-VA entity who has the qualifications outlined in Section V of this Notice. The opportunity would involve a Developer entering into an EUL with VA and financing, renovating/constructing, operating, and maintaining the agreed upon use of the asset.
VA s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program.

East Orange VA Medical Center Background

The grounds are in four municipalities: Orange, East Orange, South Orange, and Newark. The site formerly belonged to the Bamberger estate, which was endowed originally to Princeton University and in turn, sold to a private owner and then purchased by the government. Recognizing the need for a medical facility to serve Veterans in metropolitan areas, Congress approved and funded the facility in 1943. The VAMC opened in July 1952.
The hospital provides primary care and specialty health services, including homeless Veteran care, mental health care, skin care (dermatology), dental care, digestive care (gastroenterology), cardiology, eye health and vision care (ophthalmology and optometry), palliative and hospice care, returning service member care, Veteran readiness and employment programs, and more.

Supplement B
SCOPE OF WORK:
A/E services are required for Schematics, Design Development, Construction Documents, Construction Cost Estimate and Construction Period Services for project number 657-27-101 FCA-Conduct Hazardous Material Abatement, 2027, AE Design. This project will conduct hazardous materials abatement across various buildings at the John Cochran (JC) and Jefferson Barracks (JB) Divisions of the VA St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) during FY27. The scope includes VPIH (Verification of Prior Investigation of Hazardous materials) for additional sampling, abatement design, and oversight. The abatement is limited and guided by the results of the most recent hazardous materials survey and areas prioritized for Infrastructure and Historic Construction Contract (IHCC) work or identified by Maintenance & Operations (M&O) for needed repairs. Locations and extent of abatement will be determined based on upcoming IHCC and M&O project priorities.
This delivery order shall cover the following tasks.
A/E Part Two Services of this design project (also known as Construction Period Services) includes responding to construction contractor Requests For Information (RFIs) during the solicitation and construction phases of the construction project, attendance at pre-bid, post-award and commissioning kick off construction project conferences, review of construction material submittals and shop drawings, approximately 5 site visits during construction to ensure compliance with the design drawings and specifications, preparation of site visit reports, coordination with project commissioning requirements, review of any construction project modifications for cost and technical acceptability, attendance in the final acceptance inspection, preparation of the punch list and preparation of record drawings of the completed construction project based on the construction contractor s as-built drawings. The A/E shall prepare a submittal log to be utilized by the VA during construction period services, maintain RFI log and provide meeting minutes for weekly construction meetings throughout the duration of construction. The A/E shall hire a third-party commissioning agent to commission all installed equipment.
The above paragraphs constitute a basic outline of the work to be accomplished and in no way comprises all the details for design of this project. The A/E shall initiate detailed inspection of the project site to determine the needs and conditions for the design of this project.
The A/E shall be solely responsible for the management, including all associated labor, equipment, materials, mailing costs, and inspection, to meet the requirements of the design project. The A/E shall further provide meeting minutes for all meetings held under this design project.
General Statement
A/E Part One Services (also known as Design Phase) for this design project includes site visit, field investigation, conduct of studies and user interviews to update drawings, specifications and cost estimates for all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate a construction project. This project will Conduct Hazardous Material Abatement, STL-JB&JC
2. DESIGN DEVELOPMENT:
a. The VPIH shall make investigations necessary to thoroughly evaluate the area. This may include, but not limited to, hazardous materials testing, identifying any and all asbestos and lead containing materials within the project area.
b. Upon completion of initial field survey and assessment, provide a comprehensive report of existing conditions and findings to VASTLHCS Facility Engineering Service. Hazardous material surveys and design shall be in compliance with National Emissions Standard for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAP) requirements for renovation and demolition projects.
c. The VA team will evaluate and identify any additional project scope based on the survey findings.
d. This project will be phased such that it impacts hospital function as little as possible.
3. Abatement Document:
a. After the VA approves the VPIH proposed scope of work, the VPIH shall prepare abatement documents necessary to accomplish the approved design development including drawings and specifications.
4. Review of Abatement Work Plan:
a. The VPIH shall review the contractor s proposed Abatement Work Plan and provide approval before proceeding to construction.
5. Abatement Oversight Service:
a. The VPIH shall perform oversight services as detailed later in this scope of work.
6. Functional Product:
a. It is important to emphasize that the VPIH shall perform design development and detailed design work and prepare detailed abatement documents.
b. VPIH Survey: The VPIH Firm will complete a survey, to include testing, identifying any and all asbestos and lead containing materials within the project area. This project will remove all lead and asbestos in areas being renovated.
c. Reference VA Asbestos Abatement Design Manual (PG 18-10) July 2011:
i. 1.8 DESIGN REQUIREMENTS: The following elements are required for all asbestos abatement project designs for VA facilities:
i. All project designs must be developed and/or reviewed and approved by an EPA Model Curriculum trained and applicable state accredited Asbestos Project Designer. This is to ensure that all applicable federal, state, and local regulations are followed regarding the design of asbestos abatement projects. These regulations include, but are not limited to, EPA NESHAP requirements, City of St. Louis Air Pollution division requirements St. Louis County Air Pollution division requirements, and Missouri Department of Natural Resources (MDNR) requirements. VA representatives conducting peer review of asbestos designs need not be accredited Asbestos Project Designers.
ii. All asbestos inspections performed in VA facilities for the purposes of gathering information for the development of the asbestos abatement project design must be performed by EPA Model Curriculum trained and applicable state-accredited Asbestos Building Inspector.
iii. VA Master Specifications have been developed for typical asbestos abatement work. The appropriate sections shall be edited to meet the project scope of work and specific project requirements.
iv. The VPIH shall carefully coordinate specifications with the drawings so that all work required by the drawings is included in the specifications. Specification content that does not apply to the project shall be deleted.
v. The VPIH shall modify the existing Master Specifications, when feasible, to address any abatement that is not specifically identified by the VA Master Specifications.
ii. 1.9.2 DRAWINGS The following criteria must be used when creating drawings to be used in support of the asbestos abatement project.
i. Refer to VA Design and Construction Procedures for general drawing requirements.
ii. Consolidate notes and place them on the right-hand side of the sheet.
iii. Show scale, compass point, orientation, key plan, title, column grids and numbers, match-lines, room numbers and titles corresponding to the Architectural drawings.
iv. Clearly identify all locations of materials to be removed during the asbestos abatement project.
v. Clearly identify any life-critical systems that exist in abatement areas to ensure that these systems are isolated and not disturbed during the project.

title: LARS Hardware Refresh
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.AIR FORCE MATERIEL COMMAND.AIR FORCE LIFE CYCLE MANAGEMENT CENTER.INTELLIGENCE, SURVEILLANCE, RECONNAISSANCE - SPECIAL OPERATIONS FORCES.FA8509  AFLCMC WIUKA
description_text:
The Government has a requirement to obtain a hardware refresh of the Lightweight Airborne Recovery System (LARS), formally identified as Personnel Locator System (PLS) v12 AN/ARS-6, on the HC-130J due to the existing system being end of life from widespread component obsolescence. Any refreshed LARS are required to maintain all current system capabilities and project a minimum 10-year period of sustainability. Such capabilities include Terminal Area Communications (TAC), Terminal Area Guidance (TAG), and Combat Survivor Evader Locator/Next Generation Survival Radio (CSEL/NGSR) full compatibility. In addition, the LARS hardware refresh shall produce a Form, Fit, Function (FFF/F3) version of the current system. The USAF's MC-130J, the USAF's HH-60W, and the USN's MH-60S will benefit from a FFF hardware refresh of LARS as well.
This effort will consist of the Non-recurring Engineering (NRE) required to produce a refreshed hardware configuration for LARS. This includes all necessary design reviews, developmental testing events, operational testing events, etc. It is also expected that up to five test articles will be required to fully prove out the refreshed LARS ability to fulfill the requirements described above. The effort associated with the retrofitting/fielding of the proved refreshed LARS will be a separate contract.
The resultant contract is planned to have a period of performance of three (3) years, consisting of one (1) base and two (2) option periods.
The Government intends to issue a Sole Source Solicitation to:
Cubic Defense Application, Inc.
9233 Balboa AVE
San Diego, CA 92123-1513
CAGE Code:87G32
Large Business
The authority for this requirement is 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Electronic procedures will be used for this solicitation. Request a copy of the solicitation from the following website: www.sam.gov. Approximate issue date of the solicitation is October 21, 2026. Approximate response date for receipt of proposal is November 20, 2026.

title: Medicaid Data Analysis for Bacterial Respiratory Pathogens and Information Systems
agency: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION
description_text:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) awarded a sole source contract with MATHEMATICA INC., 1100 1ST ST NE FL 12, WASHINGTON, DC. 20002
This notice is provided in accordance with RFO FAR 8.401 & GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1) .
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases, Division of Bacterial Diseases (DBD) requires support Services with the contractor listed above. The requested contractor Mathematica qualified as “innovator status” vendor for data analysis by Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). Mathematica also has demonstrated experience and specialized staff with unique access and analytical capabilities for Medicaid data sets which captures the largest segment of US healthcare data, including births.
The contractor shall perform analyses across four technical dimensions defined in the Statement of Work: (1) validating infant GBS case counts using TAF OT claims and evaluating a fourth case definition tied to maternal Medicaid IDs; (2) developing and refining a probabilistic mother-infant linkage algorithm using the Medicaid Case Number and supplementary variables; (3) estimating maternal vaccination coverage (COVID-19, influenza, Tdap, and prospectively RSV) accounting for bundled payment code effects; and (4) applying methods to reduce gestational age missingness using prenatal claims data. These tasks require continuity with linkage algorithms and case-definition logic Mathematica has already built and validated under prior CDC task orders.
The authority permitting other than full and open competition is Title III of the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 (41 U.S.C. 251, et seq.); Title 40 U.S.C. 501, Services for Executive Agencies, as implemented at FAR 8.401 and GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1) "Only one source is capable of providing the products, services, or solution required at the level of quality required because the products, services, or solutions are unique or highly specialized." Through its prior contracts, Mathematica has already built key parts of this analysis—including updating the medical codes used to identify cases, working to link mother and infant records more completely, and adjusting for how individual states handle Medicaid enrollment for newborns. This steady, hands-on progress means Mathematica starts this next phase of work already ahead, with the knowledge and tools in place that a new
contractor would not have.
All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation to Robin C. Meyer, Contract Specialist, at rcm2@cdc.gov, which shall be considered by the agency. The deadline for submissions is Ocotber 31, 2026 at 4:30PM EST.
The Government will review any/all information submitted to determine if other responsible sources exist that could provide this requirement. Information received in response to this announcement will be used solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

title: Generation and Delivery of Meteorological and Hydrological Forecasts for the Western Washington and Northwest Montana River Basins
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.US ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS.ENGINEER DIVISION NORTHWESTERN.ENDIST SEATTLE.W071 ENDIST SEATTLE
description_text:
The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, intends to issue a firm-fixed-price purchase order on a sole source basis to Upstream Tech for commercial hydrologic and meteorological forecasting services. These services support the Water Management Section’s critical missions for the Green, White/Puyallup, and Kootenai River basins, which include standard reservoir regulation, seasonal water supply forecasting, dam safety, and real-time emergency flood-fighting operations. This requirement will be procured in accordance with RFO 12.102(a), which allows for solicitation from a single source when the contracting officer determines that only one source is reasonably available. The Product Service Code for this requirement is R427 (Support – Professional: Weather Reporting/Observation) and the NAICS code is 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services), with a size standard of $19.5 million.
The Government has determined that Upstream Tech is the only source capable of providing the required services without unacceptable disruption, mission risk, and substantial duplication of cost. The required services include the generation and delivery of high-resolution, basin-specific meteorological and hydrological forecast data feeds. Market research confirms that Upstream Tech has unique qualifications, as its proprietary forecasting models, analytical tools, and automated data pipelines are deeply integrated into the District's daily water management operating procedures and Corps Water Management System (CWMS). A transition to an alternative vendor would require an estimated 12 to 18 months to develop, calibrate, and validate new models, which would introduce unacceptable risks to public safety and dam safety operations.
This notice is not a request for competitive quotes. Information received will normally be considered for the purpose of identifying small business vendors with the capability to fulfill the requirement. The Government will not pay for any information received.
Any firm that believes it can provide the stated service can provide supporting documents demonstrating their capabilities and specifications. Information received will be used primarily for market research purposes to determine the feasibility of competition for future requirements. Information can be sent to the Contract Specialist, Dwain Graham, at dwain.m.graham@usace.army.mil. This procurement will be made in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services.

title: C1DA--AE Replace Roofing  539-25-101
agency: VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.250-NETWORK CONTRACT OFFICE 10 (36C250)
description_text:
Provide complete design services, including all necessary schematics, design development, surveys, cost estimates, construction drawings and specifications, and construction period services (CPS) for solicitation to replace and repair roofing and lighting protection at the Cincinnati VA Medical Center, 3200 Vine Street, Cincinnati, OH 45220 (Building Numbers: 1, 2, 3, 8, 13, 14, 15, 16 and trailers) and the Fort Thomas Campus, 1000 S. Ft. Thomas Ave, Ft. Thomas, KY 41075 (Building Numbers: 64, 117 and trailers), in accordance with the general items as written (231000 sq-ft - estimated).
This project will replace and repair the roofing and lightning protection. Replacement of outdated roofing and lighting protection will reduce overall emergency maintenance, increase facility operation, and provide proper protection.
SELECTION CRITERIA
The Government will evaluate each potential contractor under the terms of its:
A. Professional qualifications necessary for satisfactory performance of required services;
B. Specialized experience and technical competence in the type of work required, including, where appropriate, experience in energy conservation, pollution prevention, waste reduction, and the use of recovered materials;
C. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time;
D. Past performance on contracts with Government agencies and private industry in terms of cost control, quality of work, and compliance with performance schedules;
E. Location in the general geographical area of the project and knowledge of the locality of the project; provided, that application of this criterion leaves an appropriate number of qualified firms, given the nature and size of the project;
F. Experience in construction period services to include professional field inspections during the construction period, review of construction submittals, support in answering requests for information during the construction period, and support of construction contract changes to include drafting statements of work, and cost estimates shall be included as an evaluation criterion when construction period services is included in the statement of work for A-E services, and;
G. The extent to which potential contractors identify and commit to the use of service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, veteran-owned small businesses, and other types of small businesses as subcontractors.
SUBMITTAL INSTRUCTIONS
All interested and capable contractors must submit an electronic copy of their SF 330s, via email, by the closing time/date of this announcement. Note the following:
No hard/physical copies will be accepted.
Limit SF 330 packages to 50 pages. Only the first 50 pages will be evaluated.
Submit all documentation as one single file. The total size of the electronic submission (email and all attachments) must not exceed 15MB; larger emails may get rejected by the network server and will be considered non-responsive.
Cited relevant projects must be within the last five (5) years.
Submit packages via email to the contract specialist by the deadline:Â ronald.heidemann@va.gov
Subject line must include the notice number: 36C25027R0009
Please include your firm s POC and UEI in the email body.
***End of Presolicitation Notice**

description_text:
***This opportunity is for SEAPORT NXG MAC HOLDERS ONLY. No other offers will be considered. SeaPort MAC holders will need to register for PIEE accounts in order to receive solicitations and submit proposals/offers.***”.
Issuing Activity: Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Division, Keyport
Notice Type: Request for Information (RFI) /Market Research
NAICS Code: 541330 - Engineering Services
Product Service Code (PSC): R425
Response Due Date: Wednesday, November 4, 2026 at 17:00 PST
Point of Contact: Contracting Officer, Angela Barlow; Contract Specialist, Stacy Noble
Purpose and Operational Context
Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Division, Keyport (NUWCDIVKPT) is conducting market research in accordance with FAR Part 10 to determine industry capability, capacity, and commercial best practices regarding the execution of upcoming taskings under a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Level-of-Effort CLIN structure.
The primary objective is to evaluate whether requirements can be reliably priced, scheduled, and delivered on an FFP Level-of-Effort basis without transferring excessive or unmanageable performance risk to either the contractor or the Government. Responses will directly inform the acquisition strategy, Performance Work Statement (PWS)/Statement of Work (SOW) development, and eventual solicitation structure.
The Government requests that interested industry respondents address the specific inquiry areas outlined below:
Area 1: Feasibility – FFP Level-of-Effort Viability Assessment
State definitively whether your organization can propose and execute the complete scope of taskings on a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Level-of Effort basis. If only portions are feasible under FFP Level-of-Effort, identify which discrete tasks can be FFP Level-of-Effort and which require alternate structures.
Area 2: Execution Approach and Pricing Basis
Describe your proposed execution approach and pricing basis. If FFP level-of-effort pricing is feasible, explain how you will scope, estimate, and deliver the work, including key milestones, deliverables, verifiable acceptance criteria, and labor/material estimating methods used to support price stability. If FFP level-of-effort pricing is not feasible, identify and, where practicable, quantify the technical, operational, schedule, supply-chain, Government-furnished property, requirements, or regulatory uncertainties that drive cost risk and preclude a firm-fixed-price approach.
Area 3: Delivery and Quality assessment
Describe how your organization will demonstrate its ability to consistently deliver quality work under an FFP contract. Include the quality management processes, qualified personnel, relevant past performance, inspection/testing methods, internal review procedures, corrective-action processes, and objective evidence—such as quality plans, certifications, sample reports, performance metrics, or customer references—that support your capability to meet contract requirements, schedule, and acceptance criteria.
Area 4: Pricing Premium Assessment
Please describe any anticipated impact to proposed pricing if the Government were to use an FFP contract type in lieu of a Cost contract. Specifically, would the shift to FFP result in a price premium to account for an increase in contractor risk? If so please provide an estimated percentage range and identify the principle risk factors contributing to this risk premium.
Response Instructions & Submission Structure
Section 1: Corporate Profile - Page Limit: 2 Pages
Company name, CAGE code, UEI number, Seaport MAC Number , business size status under relevant NAICS, and primary corporate POC.
Section 2: Capability Assessment – Page Limit: 8 Pages
Direct responses to Areas 1 through 4 above, including specific breakdown of FFP Level-of-Effort execution methodologies or risk rationale.
Section 3: Relevant Past Performance – Page Limit: 3 Pages
Up to three (3) examples of similar requirements successfully executed under an FFP Level-of-Effort or hybrid contract structure within the past five (5) years.
Government Disclaimer (FAR 15.101 FAR Overhaul)
1. Non-Binding Notice
RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), a promise to issue an RFP in the future, or an invitation for bid.
2. No Reimbursement
Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this announcement. All costs associated with responding are solely at the interested party's expense.
3. Market Research Usage Only
Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a commitment to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal.

This A-E Services requirement is being procured in accordance with the Brooks Act (Public Law (PL0582) and implemented in accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 36.102. The completed SF 330 will be evaluated by the Marion VA Medical Center Evaluation Board and the selection report shall serve as the final selection list, which will be provided directly to the Contracting Officer. The Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement.
The most highly rated firm must physically come to the site and review the project before submitting a price proposal and letter of understanding at no cost to the government.

Award of any resultant contract is contingent upon the availability of funds.

Feeder #3, one of the three primary electrical feeders, has exceeded its life expectancy. There are three feeders that run between a system of manholes on the VAMC campus. Most campus buildings have a dual electrical feed. Existing conduits run between manholes are in an unknow condition.

(RRMNA) for Rolls-Royce Marine Gas Turbine Engines and their related shipboard auxiliary systems on all applications used throughout the U.S. Navy. Specifications. As a result, RRMNA is the only contractor qualified to perform the efforts associated with the Statement of Work under this requirement.
Pursuant to 10 U.S.C 2304(c)(1), RRMNA is the only responsible source capable of fulfilling the Navy’s requirements for the specified effort. description_text:
Industry Day Announcement
Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Armament Directorate
Supply Chain Illumination Capability
Hosted by AFLCMC/EB
BLUF: AFLCMC/EB requires a secure, scalable, AI-assisted federated data capability that integrates but not unnecessarily replaces existing government, Service, and contractor data sources. The capability must provide end-to-end supply-chain mapping, risk identification and assessment, near-real-time situational awareness, mitigation tracking, and evidence-based decision support for priority munition programs, initially within the Long-Range Weapons, Affordable Munition, and Adaptive Weapons portfolios, with potential expansion across the Armament Directorate portfolio.
1. Introduction
The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Armament Directorate (EB), plans to conduct a virtual Industry Day to conduct market research and obtain industry feedback regarding a potential Supply Chain Illumination capability for the munitions enterprise.
The Armament Directorate is pursuing an artificial intelligence-assisted, federated data capability to map critical munition supply chains to raw-material sources. The intended capability would provide enterprise-level visibility into supply-chain dependencies, bottlenecks, supplier risks, competing demands, and mitigation actions in support of senior-leader decision-making and mission outcomes.
This Industry Day is intended to inform the Government’s market research under Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 10 and help identify mature, scalable commercial and non-traditional solutions that can support the Directorate’s supply-chain visibility requirements. This announcement does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), solicitation, commitment, or promise to issue a solicitation in the future.
2. Background
The Armament Directorate currently lacks an integrated mechanism to assess critical supply-chain risk across its acquisition divisions, military Services, and contractor-supported weapon systems. Existing data sources are fragmented (data lives in siloed systems), contractor logistics support arrangements can limit visibility into multi-tier supply chains, and shared dependencies across military and commercial demand can create unanticipated production risk.
The Government seeks to improve end-to-end visibility of materials, suppliers, production dependencies, single points of failure, foreign-source dependencies, and mitigation actions across priority munition portfolios down to the raw materials at the lowest of sub-tier suppliers. The initial proof of concept is expected to focus on PAE-prioritized programs within the Long-Range Weapons, Affordable Munition, and Adaptive Weapons portfolios, with potential expansion across the Armament Directorate weapon-system portfolio.
3. Industry Day Objectives
The Government seeks industry feedback on approaches to establish a secure, scalable Supply Chain Illumination capability that can:
Map supply chains from end item to raw-material origin for critical munition programs, through all tiers of subcontractors.
Federate existing government, Service, and contractor data sources without unnecessarily replacing established systems.
Identify and assess supply-chain risks , including bottlenecks, single points of failure, constrained materials, supplier financial and manufacturing risk, foreign influence, and competing demands.
Support data-sharing standards and interfaces that protect legitimate competition sensitive information while providing the Government sufficient visibility for risk management and decision support.
Enable near-real-time situational awareness through application programming interfaces and other appropriate data-exchange mechanisms.
Apply AI-assisted analytics , including machine-learning and knowledge-graph approaches, to identify relationships, risks, and mitigation options across complex, multi-tier supply chains.
Track mitigation actions through end-item delivery and produce evidence suitable for waiver assessments and senior-leader decision-making.
Integrate with relevant enterprise architectures and platforms , including existing Air Force, Army, Navy, and digital Bill of Materials efforts, as appropriate.
4. Event Details for the Virtual Industry Day Open to All Contractors
Date: 15 December 2026
Time: 0900hrs CST
Location/Platform: Teams Link
Classification: Unclassified
Registration Deadline: 16 November 2026
The Government will provide an overview of the operational problem, desired endstate, preliminary technical considerations, and potential next steps. The agenda may also include question-and-answer sessions and opportunities for industry participants to provide oral or written feedback.
5. Registration and Participation
Registration is required. Interested organizations should submit the following information no later than 16 November 2026 :
Company name
Company address
Attendee name, title, email address, and telephone number
Identification of the company’s primary point of contact
A brief description of the company’s relevant capability or experience
Any requested accessibility or administrative support requirements
Submit registration information to: AFLCMC EB, Bryant Callahan (850) 882-0260, bryant.callahan.3@us.af.mil .
6. Follow-On Engagement
Following Industry Day, the Government may issue a Request for Information, schedule one-on-one market-research discussions, request white papers, or conduct other market-research activities for live demonstrated capabilities only. Participation in Industry Day is not required for participation in any future acquisition or market-research activity unless expressly stated in a future notice.
7. Individual Demonstration Sessions
Although not required, contractors may request one-on-one discussions for the sole purpose of providing a live demonstration that addresses the following questions for munitions:
Supply Chain Risk: Which suppliers, components, and lower-tier dependencies present the greatest risk to weapon system readiness and production schedules?
Operational Performance: How do suppliers lead times, material availability, and supply chain disruptions influence production delays and repair turnaround times?
Investment Prioritization: Which supply chain vulnerabilities should receive priority investment to improve production capacity, reduce delays, and strengthen operational readiness?
Predictive Analytics: To what extent can historical supplier performance, component lead times, and material shortages predict future supply chain disruptions?
To coordinate a one-on-one session with the Government, contract Bryant Callahan, as shown in paragraph 9. Any one-on-one session will be scheduled after the Virtual Industry Day on15 December 2026.
8. Informational Notice

The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting registration materials, participating in Industry Day, providing feedback, or responding to any subsequent market research request. This language follows the informative-posting framework used in the supplied Industry Day announcement.

title: Wideband and Narrowband Global SATCOM Sustainment (WNGSS) IDIQ Contract
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.SPACE SYSTEMS COMMAND.PEO MILITARY COMMUNICATION AND POSITION NAVIGATION TIMING.FA8823  SUSTAINMENT MCPNT SSC/PKL
description_text:
The United States Space Force (USSF), Space Systems Command (SSC), intends to award a sole-source Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to The Boeing Company (CAGE: 18600), P.O. Box 92919, Los Angeles, CA 90009-2919, for the Wideband and Narrowband Global SATCOM Sustainment (WNGSS) effort.
The anticipated contract will have a five-year base ordering period and one ten-year optional ordering period, with a total estimated ceiling of approximately $945.9M ($480.6M base and $465.3M option) if all options are exercised. This IDIQ contract will provide the critical, full life-cycle engineering, sustainment, cybersecurity, modernization, and operational enhancement support for multiple Military Satellite Communications (MILSATCOM) constellations.
The scope of this requirement includes, but is not limited to:
Space Vehicle & Constellation Sustainment: 24/7 real-time anomaly analysis, fault isolation, and recovery; factory reachback engineering; telemetry trending; orbital analysis; maneuver planning; collision avoidance (COLA); and end-of-life (EOL) disposal for the Wideband Global SATCOM (WGS) and Ultra High Frequency Follow-On (UFO) satellite constellations.
Ground Command & Control Support: Sustaining engineering, software maintenance, and enhancement for the Global SATCOM Configuration and Control Element (GSCCE) ground system.
Software, Database, & Simulation Sustainment: Maintenance and updates for satellite flight software, the Satellite Simulator (SATSIM), operational databases, and engineering tools.
Pre-Handover & Transition Support: Support for the transition of new space vehicles (e.g., WGS-11, WGS-12) and hosted payloads (e.g., Protected Tactical SATCOM Prototype [PTS-P]) from development into the operational sustainment baseline.
Statutory Authority:
This acquisition is being conducted on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements."
Justification for Sole Source:
The Boeing Company is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) for the WGS satellites, UFO satellites, and critical components of the GSCCE ground system. Boeing possesses unique qualifications and exclusive ownership of the proprietary data, software, and specialized infrastructure required to perform this sustainment effort. The Government does not possess sufficient data license rights for the technical data packages (TDPs), flight software source code, or high-fidelity satellite simulators (SATSIM) to permit a competitive acquisition. This proprietary data, which was developed at private expense, includes detailed design documentation for the Boeing 702HP and 702MP satellite platforms, simulators, and ground control software. Boeing has repeatedly declined the Government’s requests to sell the necessary data rights.
Without access to this OEM-owned data, no other contractor can perform the required engineering and sustainment without introducing substantial duplication of cost to the Government and unacceptable delays and risk to on-orbit assets critical to national security. Market research confirmed that Boeing is the only contractor fully capable of satisfying all of the requirements of this acquisition without a break in critical service to the warfighter.

description_text:
US ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS (USACE) — LATIN AMERICA AND CARIBBEAN DISTRICT
INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT: DAY 1 — ARCHITECTURE & ENGINEERING (A/E) SERVICES
Requirement: Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization - AE
Customer Agency: Peruvian Navy
Notice ID: W51DQV27Z1CV8
NAICS Code: 541330 – Engineering Services
Event Date: Wednesday, December 1, 2026
Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja, Lima, Peru
RSVP Deadline: November 18, 2026, at 3:00 pm CT
General Overview
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Caribbean District, is hosting an Industry Day event in Lima, Peru, to engage with industry partners regarding the upcoming acquisition of the Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project and NAMRU-S O&M Project.
To provide focused engagement for distinct industry sectors, the event is structured over three specialized days:
Day 1 (Tuesday, December 1, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Architecture & Engineering (A/E) Services (NAICS 541330)
Day 2 (Wednesday, December 2, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Construction (NAICS 236220)
Day 3 (Thursday, December 3, 2026): U.S. Navy Medical Research Unit South (NAMRU-S) Lima and Iquitos, Peru - Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Services (NAICS 561210)
This announcement specifically covers Day 1 (A/E Services). Separate announcements address Day 2 (Construction) and Day 3 Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M).
Purpose of the Event
The purpose is to present the planned Architectural and Engineering (A/E) requirements in support of shoreside and port facility modernization at Callao Naval Base, brief prospective prime design firms and specialized consultants on USACE engineering criteria and U.S. Federal contracting standards, provide walk-in technical guidance on federal vendor registrations, and conduct private one-on-one market research capability briefings.
Summary of the Sessions
The program includes three distinct sessions:
A/E Design: A comprehensive briefing detailing project scope, facility design packages, site conditions, host-nation and DoD design standards, BIM requirements, procurement timelines, and USACE compliance guidelines.
One-on-One Capability Briefings: Private, scheduled 15-minute briefings reserved for prospective A/E firms to present specialized technical and managerial capabilities directly to the USACE acquisition panel.
Federal Systems Registration Support: Individual, walk-in technical assistance to help prospective firms navigate SAM.gov, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and NCAGE.
Please note: This announcement is issued solely for market research and informational planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), an Invitation for Bids (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the U.S. Government. No contract award will result directly from this event.
Logistics & Schedule
Date: December 1, 2026
Hours: 08:30 – 4:00 PM CT/Local Lima Time
Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja
Av. San Luis S/Nº Cdra. 24, Urb. San Borja Sur, Lima, Peru
Daily Schedule Note: A detailed schedule of presentations, networking intervals, and allocated session times is currently being finalized. The specific daily agenda will be published in a forthcoming update to this announcement prior to the event.
Event Details & Specific Sessions
Session 1: A/E Seminar & Design Scope Briefing
USACE engineering, project management, and contracting representatives will deliver a detailed technical presentation covering:
Master planning, site layout, and architectural vision for the Callao Naval Base modernization.
Design criteria, geotechnical and seismic considerations, coastal environment durability standards, and Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC).
Building Information Modeling (BIM), specialized mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP), fire protection, environmental permitting, and host-nation building codes.
Overview of the federal A/E Brooks Act selection process (FAR Part 36.6), evaluation criteria, submission requirements (Standard Form 330), and milestone schedules.

title: Solutions for Intelligence Analysis 4 (SIA 4)
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE INTELLIGENCE AGENCY (DIA).VIRGINIA CONTRACTING ACTIVITY
description_text:
SUBJECT: Request for Information (RFI) for non-personal services to support the Solutions for Intelligence Analysis 4 (SIA 4) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)
1. INTRODUCTION
It is the Virginia Contracting Activity’s (VaCA’s) policy to foster productive exchanges of information between the Government and vendors before issuing requests for proposals (RFPs). This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This is not a solicitation or RFP. The Government will not award any contracts based solely on this RFI, nor will the Government pay for any costs incurred in responding to this announcement. No RFP currently exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the RFP.
Due to the intelligence nature of the anticipated requirements, the Solutions for Intelligence Analysis 4 (SIA 4) procurement will be classified. Following the conclusion of this RFI, anticipate all future SIA 4 procurement actions will be released through the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) Acquisition Resource Center (ARC). The Government anticipates that all vendor proposals will be classified. Vendors desiring to participate in this procurement should prepare now to ensure they have the required access and ability to respond.
As part of its market research, VaCA is issuing this RFI to determine if an adequate number of qualified interested vendors exists with the requisite experience and skill sets required to provide intelligence analysis and analytics supporting professional services. Given the complexity and technical nature of Defense Intelligence Enterprise (DIE) requirements, high levels of analytical intelligence expertise, tradecraft, and mission area knowledge are essential to providing the most accurate and highest quality intelligence support possible. In addition to identifying potential sources, vendor input is sought to clarify commercial industry terminology and approach.
Responses to this RFI will be assessed for the purpose of market research, information and planning purposes only. As such, industry responses will not be treated as proposals. The Government further reserves the right to terminate this request and change its requirements if needed. Responding to this RFI does not guarantee participation in future Government activities. Responses to this RFI are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form binding contracts. Response to this RFI is not mandatory for participation in the SIA 4 solicitation.
Vendors should be advised that all submissions become Government property. Responses to this RFI will not be returned.
2. PURPOSE
This document serves as the RFI of the VaCA vendor community pursuant to RFO 15.101 “Early exchanges with industry.”
VaCA is conducting preliminary planning and market research to enable design and release of an SIA 4 RFP. VaCA is issuing this RFI to open the announcement and early participation to the full market so that all high-potential sources of support can be identified across industry. The goal is to identify the portion of the market that can provide the best competition for the SIA 4 follow-on contract, including both established providers and new entrants with relevant capabilities. As this will be a classified procurement, it is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor the NRO ARC for updates and to prepare now to ensure they have the access and ability to respond through secure channels subsequent to this RFI.
Responses to this RFI will be assessed to identify sources that are considered best qualified to meet future requirements. Best qualified sources are those sources which demonstrate the greatest depth and breadth of skills, experiences, and knowledge relevant to the mission, goals, and objectives of the VaCA.
3. BACKGROUND
As a follow-on to the current SIA 4 contract vehicle, SIA 4 is planned to be a non-personal services contract for intelligence analytics support to the VaCA and the DIE. Services are anticipated both in CONUS and OCONUS. In some cases, OCONUS services will subject personnel to harsh and hostile conditions in environments designated by the U.S. Government as Imminent Danger and / or Hostile Fire Zones.
4. ANTICIPATED SCOPE OF WORK
Once solicitated, the Government intends to award prime contracts to multiple companies, including small businesses. It is the policy of the Government to provide maximum practicable opportunities in its procurements to small and disadvantaged businesses. To support future small business requirements, all prime contract awardees MUST include as part of their team at time of proposal submission small businesses representing the four primary set-aside categories – small disadvantaged business (SDB) (including 8(a)-certified SDB), woman owned small business (WOSB), service-disabled veteran owned small business (SDVOSB), and historically under-utilized business zone (HUBZONE).
The planned period of performance (PoP) for the anticipated multiple award IDIQ contracts will be a five (5) year base ordering period with one optional five (5) year ordering period. Executed task orders (TOs) may have up to a one (1) year base period and up to four (4) option periods (no option period will exceed one (1) year in duration). The future SIA 4 vehicle is anticipated to include a Small Business On-Ramp and Small Business / Other than Small Business Off-Ramp provisions.
To be considered for award under the anticipated multiple award IDIQ contracts, potential offerors will need to possess and maintain an active Top Secret (TS) level Facility Clearance (FCL) and be able to support work at the Top Secret // Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS//SCI) level. The anticipated multiple award IDIQ contracts will require all supporting contractor personnel to be U.S. citizens who possess and maintain an active TS clearance with SCI access and successful screening by counter-intelligence polygraph. Failure to meet these requirements by the time of the proposal submission will make the offeror ineligible for award.
The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this contract is planned to be 541990: All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services. Offerors submitting as a prime contractor must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) with NAICS code 541990 designated at time of proposal submission. Failure to register through SAM and designate this NAICS code by the time of proposal submission will make the offeror ineligible for award. Additionally, the Product Service Code will be R423: Support – Professional: Intelligence.
5. INFORMATION DESIRED
Please address the following items in your response:
A. Company name, mailing address, phone number, and email of designated primary and alternate points of contact.
B. Company website address.
C. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code.
D. Level of company facility clearance and company storage authorization. If your company has an active, approved Secure Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF), please provide the number of SCIFs, their location(s), and seating capacity.
E. Business size and type (large business or small business including any applicable set-aside category (SDB, WOSB, SDVOSB, or HUBZONE) based upon NAICS code 541990 – All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services.
F. For the anticipated prime offeror, when was your company’s most recent DCAA audit? If not previously audited, does your company hold SF-1408 certification of your accounting system? When was the SF-1408 issued, and when was it most recently recertified?
G. What quality assurance standard / methods do you think are best for management and surveillance of services provided through this type of procurement? What quality management certifications does your company hold?
H. Are there general terms and conditions in Federal contracts that hamper your performance or creativity in bidding for an intelligence support services contract? If yes, briefly describe.
I. What recommendations do you have for individual qualifications and skills requirements the Government should consider when designing the Labor Categories for the SIA 4 IDIQ?
J. The Government is considering design of the SIA 4 solicitation that will focus heavily upon the offeror’s proven past performance rather than generic technical statements.
The concept currently being considered follows the model used for the SIA 3 Small Business On-Ramp (HHM402-26-R-0003) that required up to 25 past performance citations, spread across the IDIQ’s Mission Task Areas and dispersed between the prime offeror and the offeror’s team. On-Ramp past performance citations were required to be not more than three years old, and a minimum of one year on contract was required to qualify. Additional weight was then applied to the dollar value of the contract. As the majority of Small Business On-Ramp offerors successfully cited all 25 requested past performances, for the SIA 3 solicitation, a requirement for as many as 30-35 past performance citations is being considered.
Please provide your feedback on the usage of this model for the SIA 4 solicitation. Is it too restrictive? If additional qualifying factors should be applied, what do you recommend?
K. Are there any operating locations that your company would not support?
L. Please address the following specific topics / questions as applicable to your team.
L.1. Innovation and Technology Development Focus
L1.1. VaCA requests detailed recommendations on how the follow-on IDIQ and its TO structure can better encourage innovation and technology development without sacrificing mission delivery. Describe contract mechanisms, governance patterns, and delivery practices that have worked in comparable Government environments to accelerate capability upgrades. VaCA is especially interested in practical approaches for rapid technology insertion, secure prototyping, and evaluation (for example, use of test environments, sandboxes, or pilot TOs within accreditation constraints, and scalable transition from pilot to production.
L.1.2. Responders should address what the Government can do, within standard Federal contracting constructs, to reduce barriers to innovation. Discuss what terms, conditions, or oversight patterns tend to inhibit experimentation, modernization, or tool adoption, and propose alternative approaches that still protect the Government’s interests. Where relevant, address data and interface considerations that support interoperability and avoid vendor lock-in, including recommendations for open architectures, modular delivery, documentation expectations, and sustainment pathways.
L.1.3. Responders are also invited to describe how they incorporate emerging analytic techniques, methodologies, tools, and environments into day-to-day production, and how they institutionalize analytic tradecraft while integrating new technology. Provide concrete examples of how innovation was operationalized in prior programs, including what the Government asked for, what the contractor delivered, how value was measured, and what constraints (security, data access, accreditation, governance) had to be managed.
L.2. Quality, Measurement, and Objective-Based Contracting (OBC)
L.2.1. VaCA requests recommendations for OBC approaches suitable for intelligence analytic support. Describe how to define outcomes and acceptance criteria that are rigorous and auditable while still reflecting the realities on intelligence activities. Explain what success indicators and failure indicators should be used, how they should be measured and assessed, and what data or artifacts should be collected to support surveillance and continuous improvement. Include views on quality assurance (QA) methods that work well for this type of procurement and how QA should interact with tradecraft standards, mission prioritization, and surge requirements.
L2.2. If responders used OBC or outcome-based performance structures in analytic or analytic-adjacent services, describe what worked, what did not, and what you would change if designing the contract from scratch. Include suggestions for performance incentives, including both monetary and non-monetary incentives, that effectively drive high-quality analytic outcomes and modernization behaviors rather than simply staffing levels.
L.2.3. VaCA requests specific information on your recent experience delivering intelligence analysis or similar analytic support under Fixed Price (FP) arrangements, including Firm Fixed Price (FFP) or other FP constructs. Describe which work elements were successfully executed on FP, what assumptions were necessary to make FP workable, what the Government did to define scope and acceptance in a measurable way, and what risks required active management by both parties.
L.2.4. If you believe intelligence analysis services can be acquired by FFP, describe how you would structure deliverables, objective measures, surge handling, and scope control to maintain mission responsiveness. If you believe certain analytic support elements are not suitable for FP, explain why and propose alternatives, including hybrid approaches within an IDIQ (for example, FP for well-defined products or recurring services, and other structures for inherently variable work). VaCA is also interested in how OBC can be paired with FP TOs to align contractor incentives with mission outcomes and modernization.
M. Provide a brief overview of any teaming agreements or arrangements you intend to utilize if selected for the SIA 4 IDIQ.
N. If there are additional items not covered above that you believe the Government needs to consider in developing SIA 4, please provide that information.
6. ANTICIPATED PROCUREMENT MILESTONES
Should the Government decide to award IDIQ contracts, individual TOs would be subject to the availability of funding during the fiscal year in which each requirement is competed, beginning in FY29.
7. SUBMITTAL INSTRUCTIONS
A. The Government will not entertain or respond to telephonic inquiries. Any RFI amendments will be published through the SAM.gov website.
Responses to this RFI are due to the appropriate email address shown below NLT 5 P.M. Eastern, Tuesday, 24 November 2026. Responses are requested in PDF format and must not exceed ten (10) pages in length. Any information in excess of the page limit will not be considered. “Times New Roman” font is to be used in responses and will not be smaller than 12-point pitch, in standard and bold weights; no expanded, condensed, or reverse type should be used. Figures in tables, headers / footers, and graphic captions may use 10-point pitch.
Sales brochures, videos, and other marketing information materials are not requested and will not be considered.
Viable interested parties will demonstrate, in any response submitted, company capabilities to meet the performance objectives and the Government customers’ requirements. The SIA 4 solicitation is anticipated to be a team-based approach between the prime and subcontractors.
Any information received in response to this RFI that is marked “Proprietary” will be protected and handled accordingly. Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained in their response.
All responses / submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. The VaCA will not pay for information received in response to this RFI.
B. The Government anticipates that the majority of responses to this RFI will be UNCLASSIFIED. All UNCLASSIFIED questions and responses are to be submitted to the SIA 4 PMO and Contracting team at sia3pmo@dodiis.mil and raqeeba.mohammed@dodiis.mil. Any CLASSIFIED questions and responses to this RFI will be submitted to sia3_pmo@coe.ic.gov and raqeeba.t.mohammed@coe.ic.gov.
8. INDUSTRY DAY
The Government intends to conduct an Industry Day for the SIA 4 requirement during Q2FY27. Event details will be published to the NRO ARC.
9. POINTS OF CONTACT
Contract Specialist:
Ms. Raqeeba Mohammed
202.231.6067
raqeeba.mohammed@dodiis.mil or sia3pmo@dodiis.mil
raqeeba.t.mohammed@coe.ic.gov or sia3_pmo@coe.ic.gov
10. SUMMARY
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY to identify sources that can provide intelligence analytic services. The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The VaCA has not made a commitment to procure any of the items discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur costs for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.
